title: Balance-sheet acquisition
text:
Id: balance-sheet-acquisition
Name: Balance-sheet acquisition
Side: acquisition
Perimeter: No operating component transfers
Description: The acquisition of a defined portfolio of assets and specified liabilities, without acquiring a material workforce or the operating technology needed to run a standalone business.
Detailed Definition: Absa acquires one or more specified assets and liabilities but does not acquire a genuine core operating component or an independently operable business. Assets are not mandatory: a liabilities-only acquisition can fall within this archetype. A transfer of records, client data or technical interfaces may be necessary to manage the acquisition.
Characteristics:
  - The transaction direction is acquisition by Absa.
  - At least one specified asset, liability, right or obligation enters the Absa perimeter.
  - No genuine operating component transfers or remains within a controlled acquired perimeter.
  - Any records, customer contract rights, data, interfaces or servicing arrangements are required only to administer the acquired positions and do not themselves constitute a transferred operating capability.
Examples:
  - Acquisition of a loan or receivables portfolio.
  - Acquisition of a defined investment portfolio and associated contractual rights.
Lifecycle Status: available
Start Label: Start
End Label: Run

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: deal-scouting
  Index: 01
  Title: Deal Scouting
  Purpose: Identify and qualify the opportunity, confirm strategic fit and define the perimeter of assets and liabilities in scope.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Opportunity screening and strategic fit assessment
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Initial perimeter definition (assets and liabilities in scope)
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Deal perimeter summary
    -
      Name: Indicative archetype and complexity view
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Archetype classification sheet
    -
      Name: In-country capability assessment
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where the portfolio sits in a jurisdiction with limited or non-aligned existing operations.
    -
      Name: Market benchmarking of comparable portfolios
      Requirement: optional

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: due-diligence
  Index: 02
  Title: Due Diligence
  Purpose: Test the value, quality and risk profile of the portfolio and confirm what must be true to complete.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Financial and credit due diligence on the portfolio
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Due diligence request list
    -
      Name: Legal and title review of assets and liabilities
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Risk, compliance and Section 54 assessment
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Data quality and completeness review
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Data migration mapping template
    -
      Name: Regulatory approval mapping
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where the portfolio spans more than one jurisdiction or a regulated licence transfers.
    -
      Name: Independent portfolio valuation review
      Requirement: optional
-
  Id: legal-drafting-signature
  Index: 03
  Title: Legal Drafting & Signature
  Purpose: Agree and sign the transaction documents, including the conditions that must be satisfied before Legal Day 1.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: SPA drafting and negotiation
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Conditions precedent schedule agreed
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Conditions precedent tracker
    -
      Name: Signature and internal approvals
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: TSA scoping
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies only where servicing of the portfolio continues after Legal Day 1.

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: mobilisation-planning
  Index: 04
  Title: Mobilisation & Planning
  Purpose: Stand up the programme, confirm the operating model and build the integrated plan to Legal Day 1.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Programme governance and workstream mobilisation
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Operating model on a page
    -
      Name: Plan on a page and detailed integrated plan
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Plan on a page
    -
      Name: Risk, assumption, issue and dependency log opened
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: RAID log
    -
      Name: In-country delivery team mobilisation
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where a regional Spoke carries delivery accountability alongside the central Hub.
    -
      Name: Third-party delivery partner onboarding
      Requirement: optional

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: programme-execution
  Index: 05
  Title: Programme Execution
  Purpose: Deliver the workstream activity required to make the portfolio ready to transfer and to be serviced on Absa systems.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Product, pricing and servicing set-up
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Data preparation, cleansing and migration build
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Data migration mapping template
    -
      Name: Finance, reporting and reconciliation readiness
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Weekly workstream reporting and governance
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Workstream status report
    -
      Name: Technology build or configuration
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where servicing the portfolio requires new or changed system capability.
    -
      Name: New licence or entity establishment
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where Absa has no existing operations in the jurisdiction.

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: business-testing
  Index: 06
  Title: Business Testing
  Purpose: Prove end-to-end that the portfolio can be booked, serviced and reported before go-live.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: End-to-end business process testing
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Test and defect log
    -
      Name: Migration trial runs and reconciliation
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Defect triage and resolution
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Interface testing with counterparties
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where servicing depends on external interfaces or a vendor platform.
-
  Id: client-onboarding-ldi-readiness
  Index: 07
  Title: Client Onboarding & LD1 Readiness
  Purpose: Complete client onboarding, confirm regulatory and operational readiness and evidence the criteria for Legal Day 1.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Client onboarding and screening completion
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Client communications issued
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Client communication pack
    -
      Name: LD1 readiness criteria evidenced
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: LD1 readiness checklist
    -
      Name: Consent or re-papering exercise
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where client consent is required to transfer the relationship or contract.

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: dress-rehearsals
  Index: 08
  Title: Dress Rehearsals
  Purpose: Rehearse the cutover sequence under realistic conditions and confirm the runbook, timings and roles.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Cutover runbook walkthrough
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Cutover runbook
    -
      Name: Timed rehearsal with participating workstreams
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Rehearsal findings and runbook update
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Second full rehearsal
      Requirement: optional
-
  Id: go-no-go
  Index: 09
  Title: Go/No-Go
  Purpose: Take the formal decision to proceed to cutover against agreed criteria and open risks.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Workstream readiness confirmations
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Go/No-Go decision pack
    -
      Name: Open risk and defect review
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Formal decision recorded
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Regulator or counterparty notification
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where a regulator or counterparty must be notified before completion.

title: Stages
text:
-
  Id: cutover
  Index: 10
  Title: Cutover
  Purpose: Execute the transfer of the portfolio to Absa systems and books across Legal Day 1.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Runbook execution and command centre
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Cutover runbook
    -
      Name: Migration execution and reconciliation sign-off
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Legal Day 1 completion confirmed
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Fallback or rollback invocation
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies only if cutover exit criteria are not met within the agreed window.
-
  Id: hypercare
  Index: 11
  Title: Hypercare
  Purpose: Stabilise servicing after Legal Day 1 and hand the portfolio into business as usual.
  Activities:
    -
      Name: Elevated monitoring and issue resolution
      Requirement: necessary
      Artefact: Hypercare exit report
    -
      Name: Reconciliation and reporting stabilisation
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: Handover to business as usual and programme closure
      Requirement: necessary
    -
      Name: TSA service management
      Requirement: conditional
      Reason: Applies where transitional services remain in place after Legal Day 1.
    -
      Name: Post-completion review
      Requirement: optional

title: Partial-business acquisition
text:
Id: partial-business-acquisition
Name: Partial-business acquisition
Side: acquisition
Perimeter: Operating component transfers, not independently operable
Description: The acquisition of part of a business, including selected operating components, but not a complete standalone business.
Detailed Definition: Absa acquires at least one genuine operating component, but the acquired perimeter is not independently operable. One or more core capabilities remain with the seller, must be supplied on an ongoing basis, must be built by Absa or require integration into Absa.
Characteristics:
  - The transaction direction is acquisition.
  - At least one genuine operating component transfers: people, technology, processes, licences, supplier relationships, IP or operational data.
  - One or more core capabilities needed for the principal offering are excluded.
  - Continuation requires Absa integration, an Absa build or continuing provision of an excluded capability.
Examples:
  - Acquisition of a client portfolio and its relationship managers, with clients migrated onto Absa systems.
  - Acquisition of a lending platform, intellectual property and customer contracts, while the seller retains the employees who operate it.
Lifecycle Status: in-development
Start Label: Start
End Label: Run

title: Full-business acquisition
text:
Id: full-business-acquisition
Name: Full-business acquisition
Side: acquisition
Perimeter: Complete operating business, independently operable
Description: The acquisition of a complete operating business, including the people, technology and other capabilities needed for it to continue operating.
Detailed Definition: Absa acquires an operating business that can continue delivering and servicing its principal offering without integration into Absa. Every core capability needed for continuity transfers, remains within the acquired entity or is available through an enforceable standalone arrangement at completion. Later integration is optional.
Characteristics:
  - The transaction direction is acquisition.
  - The principal offering and customer perimeter are identifiable.
  - All core capabilities required for continuity are available at completion.
  - Required licences, permissions, contracts, data and IP remain effective.
  - The business can continue without integration into Absa.
  - Any TSA is transitional and has a credible standalone exit.
Examples:
  - Acquisition of a banking subsidiary, including its employees, customers, systems, licences and operations.
  - Acquisition of a complete payments, insurance or wealth-management business.
  - Acquisition of a complete business receiving temporary payroll or infrastructure support under a time-limited TSA.
Lifecycle Status: in-development
Start Label: Start
End Label: Run

title: Balance-sheet divestment
text:
Id: balance-sheet-divestment
Name: Balance-sheet divestment
Side: divestment
Perimeter: No operating component transfers
Description: The sale of a defined portfolio of assets and specified liabilities, without transferring employees or the operating technology and capabilities needed to run a business.
Detailed Definition: Absa transfers one or more specified assets and liabilities but does not transfer a genuine core operating component or an independently operable business. Assets are not mandatory: a liabilities-only divestment can fall within this archetype.
Characteristics:
  - The transaction direction is divestment by Absa.
  - At least one specified asset, liability, right or obligation leaves the Absa perimeter.
  - No genuine operating component transfers.
  - Any records, customer contract rights, data, interfaces or servicing arrangements are required only to administer the transferred positions and do not themselves constitute a transferred operating capability.
Examples:
  - Sale of a loan, receivables or non-performing-loan portfolio without a servicing function.
  - Sale of selected receivables or investments.
Lifecycle Status: in-development
Start Label: Start
End Label: Separation complete

  - The business can continue outside Absa without integration into the buyer.
  - Any TSA is transitional and has a credible standalone exit.
Examples:
  - Sale of an Absa subsidiary or country business, including its employees, customers, systems, licences and operations.
  - Sale of a complete payments, insurance or wealth-management business.

End Label: Separation complete

text:
-
  Category: Coordinates
  Responsibility: Mobilise Functional Spokes and Regional Spokes, align workstream plans, surface critical-path risks and escalate unresolved trade-offs.
  Boundary: The Hub coordinates and challenges but does not become the accountable owner of specialist approvals.
-
  Category: Coordinates
  Responsibility: Interface with Corporate Development, Finance & Tax, Legal & CorpDev, deal teams and external counterparties to translate deal economics, Group Interchange requirements, SPA terms, conditions precedent and execution commitments into programme plans.
  Boundary: Corporate Development, Finance & Tax and Legal & CorpDev retain their own commercial, financial and legal mandates.
-
  Category: Functional Spoke owned
  Responsibility: Workstream-level decisions sit with the accountable functional authority.
  Boundary: The Hub records decisions and coordinates cross-workstream consequences.
-
  Category: Locally owned
  Responsibility: As much execution as feasible, local regulatory inputs, local customer impact and market operations are owned by Regional Spokes where maturity and delegated authority support local ownership.
  Boundary: Group policy, reserved approvals and transaction-wide decisions remain central.

title: Raci application note
text: Regional Spokes are the default accountable and responsible owners for workstream execution, delegated functional decisions, workstream reporting and escalation, RAID management, readiness evidence, testing, cutover and BAU handover. SA Functional Spoke provide standards, specialist challenge and hands-on support, and assume delivery accountability only where a documented assessment confirms that regional maturity, capability, capacity or delegated authority is insufficient. Function Authorities remain accountable for group standards, policy interpretation, specialist decisions and reserved approvals. The Central Hub remains accountable for integrated programme governance, consolidated reporting, cross-workstream dependencies and transaction-level escalation. The agreed ownership split and any exceptions must be recorded during mobilisation in the workstream charter, RACI and decision log.

title: Archetype shapes
text:
Balance sheet:
  Label: Balance-sheet transaction
  Implication: Use a proportionate programme focused on transferred assets and liabilities, completion mechanics, data, funds flow, reconciliation, retained servicing and control evidence.
Partial:
  Label: Partial-business transaction
  Implication: Add capability-gap management, client and employee impacts, data migration or separation, transitional services, supplier dependencies and missing-capability replacement.
Full integrated:
  Label: Full-business integrated transaction
  Implication: Add full operating-model integration or separation, technology, data, customers, employees, controls, suppliers, synergy delivery, stranded costs and comprehensive readiness testing.
Full standalone:
  Label: Full-business standalone transaction
  Implication: Prioritise continuity under new ownership, governance appointments, reporting, funding, control handover, licences, TSA operation and selective interfaces rather than assuming full integration.

title: Balance sheet acquisition
text: Heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

title: Activities
text:
- Support CorpDev and Finance & Tax to identify the in-scope assets, liabilities, seller servicing assumptions, client-data availability, premium-to-NAV drivers, tax constraints and finance reporting constraints that affect execution.
- Translate price adjustments, effective transfer date, funds flow, data sharing, records access and completion mechanics into the programme plan.
- Set the workstreams, governance rhythm, readiness criteria, decision routes and dependency controls needed for a proportionate balance sheet transfer.
- Build and maintain the integrated plan. Track portfolio-transfer milestones, seller information flow, data preparation, tax actions, risk acceptances and cross-workstream dependencies.
- Manage RAID and decision control. Keep risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies and decisions visible, owned and escalated through the right governance route.
- Support LD1 Readiness to scale onboarding only where clients, mandates or servicing obligations move
- Coordinate rehearsal of completion-critical activity. Test funds flow, data cut, reconciliation, file transfer, seller servicing hand-off and fallback where material.
- Prepare the go/no-go recommendation. Assemble readiness evidence, residual risks, unresolved client or data issues and completion evidence for decision.
- Run completion command centre. Coordinate funds transfer, balance recognition, data load or record transfer and first-day control checks.
- Support hypercare team to monitor reconciliations, servicing issues, retained obligations, seller performance, risk exceptions and lessons learned.

title: Hub key activities
text:
Partial business acquisition:
  Heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
  Basis: The above Balance Sheet Acquisition Activities, plus additional:
  Activities:
    - Confirm the partial acquisition perimeter. Separate the transferring operating components from the capabilities, services, people, data and controls that remain outside scope.
    - Coordinate workstreams to build the capability-gap log. Identify missing Absa capabilities, required build, seller support, client impacts, employee impacts and TSA dependencies.
    - Ensure transitional services, Group Interchange dependencies, recharge and buy-back assumptions, exit assumptions, service levels, data access, operational support and buyer-seller obligations are captured.
    - Bring in the Functional Spokes and Regional Spokes needed for missing-capability replacement, integration, onboarding, testing and cutover.
    - Track build activity, remediation, data migration, onboarding, TSA exit planning and cross-workstream dependencies.
    - Confirm testing shows missing capabilities have been replaced, integrated or supported through controlled transitional arrangements.
    - Bring together client onboarding, KYC / AML, operational readiness, employee readiness to drive quicker more efficient client onboarding ahead of LD1
    - Control go/no-go around partial acquisition risk. Present readiness against missing-capability closure, TSA dependency, client onboarding, residual risk and control acceptance.

title: Full business acquisition integrated
text:
Heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
Basis: The above Balance Sheet Acquisition Activities and Partial Business Acquisition, plus additional:
Activities:

title: Full business acquisition standalone
text:

Basis: Standalone activity set:

title: Activities
text:
- Support CorpDev team to confirm whether the acquired business can operate under Absa ownership across governance, licences, reporting, funding, controls, employees, suppliers and technology.

- Confirm decision rights, management forums, escalation routes, reporting packs, control attestations and Absa oversight requirements.
- Set the TSA, Group Interchange and retained-service model. Define the services needed to keep the business running, the recharge or buy-back mechanics, the evidence required, the exit conditions and the owner for each dependency.
- Track governance set-up, reporting integration, funding arrangements, control uplift, TSA management and selective system or data interfaces.
- Test governance, reporting, funding, access, controls, key services and selective interfaces without assuming full operational integration.
- Prepare client continuity, service communications, governance handover, control attestations, local management readiness and transitional service coverage.
- Present continuity readiness, control evidence, governance appointments, TSA risks, funding readiness and regulator commitments.
- Activate governance, reporting access, funding confirmation, TSA commencement and critical-service checks.

title: Activities
text: - Support standalone hypercare. Monitor service continuity, management information, control issues, funding, TSA performance, reporting quality and future integration options.

title: Balance sheet sale

title: Hub layers
text:
-
  Id: hub
  Name: Central Hub
  Description: The Hub steers the programme through programme management, education, support, and Quality Assurance, rather than owning every functional decision. It coordinates dependency management, readiness, governance and executive reporting.
-
  Id: functional
  Name: SA Functional Spokes
  Description: Spokes own functional standards, plans, decisions and readiness evidence, while aligning to the Central Hub programme model. They support in-country teams where maturity demands
-
  Id: regional
  Name: In-country Regional Spokes
  Description: In-country teams own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity. Local accountability expands as functional maturity increases, while central control remains for transaction-critical and group-wide matters.

title: Hub responsibilities
text:
-
  Id: education
  Title: Education
  Summary: Embedding best practice into programme execution and governance based on past experience
  Detail:
    - Define transaction methodology, standards, mobilisation templates, workstream charter requirements, readiness evidence standards and cutover governance.
    - Share methodology, templates and reusable playbooks so regional and functional teams can adopt and embed them.
    - Capture lessons learned, playbook updates and reusable knowledge for the next transaction.
-
  Id: programme-management
  Title: Programme Management
  Summary: Owns the programme plan, budget, and reporting to drive best in class governance and tracking
  Detail:
    - Mobilise the transaction, establish programme governance, maintain the integrated plan, own cross-workstream dependencies, manage central RAID and decision logs, and produce executive reporting.
    - Own the programme plan, budget, and governance artefacts to drive fast, efficient execution and decision making
    - Coordination and tracking of execution and governance across all functional and regional spokes
    - Coordinate Legal Day 1 readiness, dress rehearsals, go/no-go preparation, cutover command-centre operation, hypercare governance and lessons learned.

title: Hub responsibilities
text:
-
  Id: support
  Title: Support
  Summary: Leads mobilisation efforts, supporting the wider Absa community to actually stand up and M&A programme
  Detail:
    - Mobilise Functional Spokes and Regional Spokes, align workstream plans, surface critical-path risks and escalate unresolved trade-offs.
    - Decision making on key role appointments, such as Workstream leads alongside Accountable Executives
    - Interface with Corporate Development, Finance & Tax, Legal & CorpDev, deal teams and external counterparties to translate deal economics, Group Interchange requirements, SPA terms, conditions precedent and execution commitments into programme plans.
-
  Id: quality-assurance
  Title: Quality Assurance
  Summary: Checks and challenges reporting, thinking, and outputs from workstreams to ensure high standards are maintained across the programme
  Detail:
    - Set standards and QA completeness of workstream charters and L2 plans.
    - QA governance discipline, evidence quality and readiness packs.
    - Provide framework, challenge and integrated visibility over the regional maturity assessment and execution split.

title: Hub roles
text:
-
  Id: sponsor
  Name: Executive Sponsor
  Summary: Strategic direction and Absa-wide decisions.
  Detail: Provides overall strategic direction and makes Absa-wide decisions that materially affect the transaction. Approves the business case and programme budget.
  Purpose: Provides overall strategic direction and makes the Absa-wide decisions that materially affect the transaction.
  Responsibilities:
    - Owns the business case and the strategic rationale for the transaction
    - Approves the programme budget and material changes to it
    - Chairs or attends executive governance and resolves escalated trade-offs
    - Secures organisational commitment across business and control functions
  Mandate: Decides scope, budget, timing, risk appetite and the Legal Day 1 go or no-go recommendation put forward by the Transaction Director.
  Reports To: Absa executive committee and transaction governance forum.
  Boundaries: Does not run programme delivery and does not substitute for functional or country approvals.

title: Hub roles
text:
-
  Id: transaction-director
  Name: Transaction Director
  Summary: Accountable for successful transaction execution.
  Detail: Accountable for successful transaction execution. Translates strategic and contractual intent into an executable programme, mobilises the organisation, owns the integrated execution plan, leads governance and drives readiness, cutover and stabilisation.
  Purpose: Accountable for successful transaction execution, from mobilisation through completion and stabilisation.
  Responsibilities:
    - Translates strategic and contractual intent into an executable programme
    - Mobilises the required Functional and Regional Spokes
    - Owns the integrated execution plan and the critical path
    - Leads governance and drives readiness, cutover and stabilisation
    - Prepares the go or no-go recommendation for executive governance
  Mandate: Requires delegated budget authority, direct access to decision-makers and the ability to direct delivery resources across functions and countries.
  Reports To: Executive Sponsor.
  Boundaries: Does not approve functional design, policy interpretation or local regulatory positions.

title: Hub roles
text:
-
  Id: programme-manager
  Name: Programme Manager
  Summary: Runs the programme day to day.
  Detail: Runs the programme day to day. Owns the programme-management framework, integrated plan, dependencies, governance, reporting, RAID control, readiness coordination and PMO discipline.
  Purpose: Runs the programme day to day so the Transaction Director can lead externally and at executive level.
  Responsibilities:
    - Owns the programme-management framework and delivery standards
    - Maintains the integrated plan, milestones and dependency map
    - Runs the governance rhythm and reporting cycle
    - Controls RAID, actions and the decision log
    - Coordinates readiness evidence across functions and countries
  Mandate: Sets delivery cadence, reporting formats and escalation routes, and calls issues into governance without waiting for permission.
  Reports To: Transaction Director.
  Boundaries: Does not own functional deliverables and does not accept residual risk on behalf of the transaction.

title: Hub roles
text:
-
  Id: pmo
  Name: Central PMO Support
  Summary: Programme information, control artefacts and audit trail.
  Detail: Maintains plans, milestones, reports, RAID items, actions, decisions, governance materials and programme documentation. Provides the reliable information and audit trail required for effective programme control.
  Purpose: Provides the reliable programme information and audit trail required for effective transaction control.
  Responsibilities:
    - Maintains plans, milestones and the reporting pack
    - Logs and tracks RAID items, actions and decisions
    - Prepares governance materials and circulates outcomes
    - Maintains controlled programme documentation and version history
  Mandate: Sets and enforces the information standards that workstreams must meet when submitting plans, status and evidence.
  Reports To: Programme Manager.
  Boundaries: Does not make delivery decisions or negotiate positions with workstreams and counterparties.

title: Layer details
text:
Hub:
  Ownership: STEERS THE PROGRAMME
  Owns:
    - Education - embedding best practice into programme execution and governance based on past experience
    - Programme Management - owns the programme plan, budget, and reporting to drive best in class governance and tracking
    - Support - leads mobilisation efforts, supporting the wider Absa community to actually stand up and M&A programme
    - Quality Assurance - checks and challenges reporting, thinking, and outputs from workstreams to ensure high standards are maintained across the programme
  Does Not Own: The Hub steers the programme rather than owning every functional decision. Functional decisions remain with the relevant Functional Spoke or control function.
Functional:
  Ownership: OWNS FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP
  Owns:
    - Specialist functional leadership across the transaction
    - Functional standards, plans, decisions and readiness evidence
    - Support to in-country teams where maturity demands
    - Execution of workstream items where in-country teams are unable to
  Does Not Own: Does not own transaction-wide sequencing or executive reporting.

title: Layer details
text:
Regional:
  Ownership: OWNS LOCAL EXECUTION AT A MINIMUM
  Owns:
    - As much execution as is feasible based on local maturity, capability and capacity
    - Local regulatory inputs and local customer impact
    - Market operations and local business ownership
    - Country-level readiness evidence and local sign-off
  Does Not Own: Group policy, reserved approvals and transaction-wide decisions remain central. Local accountability expands as functional maturity increases.

title: Maturity views
text:
Low:
  Label: Country baseline
  Hub: Central Hub provides more hands-on programme coordination and escalation.
  Functional: SA Functional Spokes lead functional design, planning and evidence production.
  Regional: Regional Spokes primarily provide local facts, access, stakeholders and execution support.
  Points:
    - Central Hub provides more hands-on programme coordination and escalation.
    - SA Functional Spokes lead functional design, planning and evidence production.
    - Regional Spokes primarily provide local facts, access, stakeholders and execution support.
Medium:
  Label: More mature
  Hub: Central Hub maintains governance, integrated plan control and readiness integration.
  Functional: SA and Regional Spokes jointly deliver.
  Regional: Local teams lead defined activities and provide evidence for central review.
  Points:
    - Central Hub maintains governance, integrated plan control and readiness integration.
    - SA and Regional Spokes jointly deliver.
    - Local teams lead defined activities and provide evidence for central review.

title: Maturity views

High:

  Hub: Central Hub continues to own transaction-wide control, executive reporting, critical-path escalation and integrated go or no-go governance.
  Functional: SA Functional Spokes provide standards, challenge and specialist escalation.
  Regional: Regional Spokes lead more local execution within delegated authority.
  Points:

    - Central Hub continues to own transaction-wide control, executive reporting, critical-path escalation and integrated go or no-go governance.

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: Executive Sponsor (Accountable Exec, AE)
  Role: Provide overall strategic direction and drive decision making at the highest levels
  Responsibilities: Ultimately responsible for the strategic and commercial success of the transaction
  Mandate: Makes Absa-wide, transaction-level decisions which may materially impact the shape or success of the transaction
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to convene top decision makers at short notice
    - Must be empowered to make decisions which impact the strategic direction of the transaction as a whole
    - Must ultimately sign off on budget and business case

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: Transaction Director (TD)
  Role: Senior leader accountable for the successful execution of the transaction. Translates the strategic intent and contractual requirements into an executable programme, establishes the organisation and governance to deliver it, and drives towards successful Legal Day 1
  Responsibilities: Translating the deal into an executable transaction programme, mobilising the transaction, owning the integrated execution plan, and leading programme governance and decision-making
  Mandate: Makes transaction-level decisions which are vital for execution, assesses intra-transaction trade-offs, and provides execution-level strategic direction
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to make transaction-level decisions related to execution
    - Must own the budget, to ensure the programme is staffed correctly
    - Must own the maintenance of the business case, to ensure the programme is tracking effectively
    - Must be empowered to escalate to executives at short notice on urgent matters
  Boundaries:
    - Accountable but not responsible for driving execution (Prog. Manager)
    - Escalates to AE where decisions have a broader strategic impact
    - Functional decisions on execution-specifics (design decisions, etc.) are made by Workstream Execs

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: Programme Manager / Director
  Role: Drives the day-to-day management and control of the M&A programme. Acts as the central point of coordination across the transaction, ensuring that plans, dependencies, risks, decisions and readiness are managed consistently across the organisation.
  Responsibilities: Establishes and operates the programme management framework, owns and maintains the integrated programme plan, drives cross-workstream coordination and dependency management, runs governance, and decision support, leads the PMO and maintain delivery discipline
  Mandate: Makes programme-management related decisions, regarding the governance and execution of the plan (e.g. governance cadence, reporting structures, etc)
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to define the programme structure and governance
    - Must be empowered to hold execution teams accountable, regardless of seniority
    - Must drive plan creation, to ensure plan tracking is achievable and realistic
    - Must be empowered to escalate to the Transaction Director at short notice on urgent matters
  Boundaries:
    - Responsible for driving execution, but not the execution itself
    - Escalates to TD where decisions have a broader programme impact

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: PMO Support
  Role: Provides the programme management coordination, administration and control required to support delivery of an M&A deal
  Responsibilities: Maintains programme plans and milestone tracking, coordinates workstream reporting, maintains RAID logs, coordinates governance and programme forums, supports dependency and cross-workstream coordination, maintains programme documentation and controls
  Mandate: Limited decision mandate, may make decisions on escalations if execution is lacking
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to build relationships with Workstream Leads and hold them accountable, regardless of seniority
  Boundaries:
    - Responsible for coordinating execution, but not the execution itself
    - Escalates to Programme Manager where decisions must be made
-
  Title: Workstream Exec
  Role: Owns the success of the workstream outcomes and is ultimately accountable for their execution
  Responsibilities: Unblock workstream execution by providing SME input and decision making, support WSL with escalations and senior-level coordination, assure workstream trade-offs and major prioritisation decisions
  Mandate: Makes workstream-level prioritisation and trade-off decisions, signs off on key design decisions and workstream execution plan
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to define the strategic direction of the workstream, aligned to deal objectives
  Boundaries:
    - Accountable for workstream execution, not responsible
    - Escalates to AE / TD where trade-off decisions are programme-wide

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: Workstream Lead (WSL)
  Role: Defines and manages the backlog of work within their workstream, ensuring alignment with deal objectives
  Responsibilities: Own workstream scope, detailed plan, outcomes and deliverables. Develop and maintain the detailed workstream plan, mobilise and coordinate functional resources and SMEs, manage workstream risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies, drive functional decisions and escalate blockers promptly, report workstream progress, maintain and coordinate to the central PMO
  Mandate: Can determine workstream-level requirements, and make prioritisation decisions which do not impact overall delivery scope
  Prerequisites:
    - Must be empowered to define the detailed activities which sit underneath high-level milestones
    - Must be able to define resource requirements, and prioritise resource capacity
  Boundaries:
    - Responsible for driving workstream execution, and some of the execution itself
    - Escalate to Workstream Exec where trade-off decisions must be made

title: Role summaries
text:
-
  Title: Workstream Project Manager
  Role: Supports the Workstream Lead by providing project management discipline, including tracking progress, managing timelines, reporting risks and issues, and coordinating across teams
  Responsibilities: Act as facilitator between the Workstream Lead and technical or operational teams to ensure smooth execution, own the coordination of the L2 plan, own workstream-level governance activities, and preparing WSL to report into Central Hub
  Mandate: Minimal decision making mandate
  Prerequisites:
    - none
  Boundaries:
    - Responsible for coordinating workstream execution, and some of the execution itself
    - Escalates to Workstream Lead where any decisions must be made
-
  Title: Workstream Team Member
  Role: Completes execution tasks within a workstream, and flags RAID items for escalation
  Responsibilities: Leverage function-specific SME knowledge to execute an plan and milestones, input into requirements and planning, escalate into workstream governance where needed
  Mandate: Minimal decision making mandate
  Prerequisites:
    - none
  Boundaries:
    - Responsible for actual execution, not decision making

title: Change Management
text:
Key Role: Owns the business change approach needed to embed new or separated ways of working across impacted teams.
Responsibilities:
  - Conduct change impact assessments across roles, processes, controls, systems, clients and country teams.
  - Define the change strategy, adoption plan, training needs, engagement approach and business-readiness evidence.
  - Support HR with organisational impacts and Communications / Marketing with change narrative and stakeholder messaging.
  - Coordinate readiness interventions for teams adopting new processes, systems, hand-offs or control routines.
  - Measure adoption during testing, LD1 readiness and hypercare; drive corrective actions where take-up is weak.
  - Drive broader programme morale and sentiment
Boundary Items:
  - HR owns employment terms, consultation, onboarding and people-transfer obligations.
  - Communications / Marketing owns messaging channels and approved client content.
  - Operations & Servicing and Product own process and proposition design; Change owns adoption and behavioural readiness.
  - Change should hand over to business-unit change managers where available, and HR teams in other circumstances at the end of the programme
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns change adoption decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.

title: Change Management
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local change impacts, stakeholder engagement, training coordination, adoption activity, sentiment monitoring and issue resolution where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains change strategy, methodology, adoption standards, leadership narrative, central challenge and execution support where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from input and capacity support into delivery of change interventions, adoption evidence and handover activity, with Function Authority retaining central standards and specialist support.

title: Change Management
text:

  -

title: Change Management
text:
Capability Rows:
  -
    Category: Specific project manager required

  -
    Category: Baseline capabilities
    Content: Change impact assessment; Stakeholder engagement; Adoption measurement; Training needs analysis; Readiness intervention design
  -
    Category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity

title: Communications / Marketing
text:
Key Role: Owns the communication strategy and controlled messaging required to keep stakeholders, clients and employees informed before, during and after LD1.
Responsibilities:
  - Build an integrated communications plan covering internal stakeholders, clients, employees, regulators and external counterparties.
  - Collate communication requirements, restrictions and timing dependencies from all workstreams.
  - Support adjacent workstreams (Human Capital, People Change) with coordination, signoff, and sequencing of communications
  - Input into and coordinate approval of internal announcements, client notices, employee engagement packs and external statements.
  - Define messaging principles, tone, brand treatment and channel strategy for acquisition, divestment, integration and separation scenarios.
  - Coordinate communications readiness evidence for go/no-go governance and LD1 command-centre activity.
  - Manage issue communications during cutover and hypercare with Legal, Compliance, HR and Operations & Servicing.

title: Communications / Marketing
text:
Boundary Items:
  - People Change owns the change plan and remediation actions, including key messaging; Comms / Marketing owns the execution of communications and sequencing within the overall comms plan
  - HR owns employee communications content and strategy; Comms / Marketing owns the sequencing, tracking, and sending of these communications
  - Product (Business) owns the SME content required for client communications; Comms / Marketing coordinates, drives, and executes on these communications
  - Client readiness owns the sequencing and execution of onboarding comms; Comms / Marketing supports with oversight, governance, and messaging
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns communications and marketing decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.

title: Communications / Marketing
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local stakeholder mapping, channel coordination, language or market nuance, employee and client feedback, and execution of approved communications where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - SA Function Authority retains message principles, brand treatment, approval routes, restricted communications, group-level stakeholder narrative and hands-on support where regions do not yet have sufficient maturity, capability or capacity.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from factual input into drafting, channel execution, sign-off evidence and issue communications, with Function Authority retaining central standards, specialist challenge and escalation support.

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Communications and marketing strategy approved (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Define communications objectives, guiding principles, critical outcomes and the role of communications and marketing across the transaction.
    - Map regulator, client, colleague, media and other stakeholder groups by stage gate, then work backwards from the required stakeholder outcome. Gather inputs on required communications from all other workstreams
    - Align the strategy with the transaction narrative, customer proposition, programme plan, change approach and applicable regulatory restrictions.
-
  Name: Confidentiality, leak and crisis communications protocol established (3 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Confirm insider-list restrictions, what may be communicated at each stage and the approved response if information leaks before signing or approval.
    - Prepare holding statements, escalation routes, spokesperson responsibilities and rapid approval arrangements for reputational or service issues.
    - Test crisis scenarios with Legal, Compliance, Risk, the Central Hub and relevant regional leadership.

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Joint communications governance and approval route agreed (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Define who drafts, validates, approves and releases each communication type, including clear authority to speak to clients and employees.
    - Agree counterparty review timelines, version control, evidence requirements and escalation for delayed or duplicative approvals.
    - Maintain an integrated communications calendar linked to regulatory approvals, client readiness, cutover and LD1 milestones.
-
  Name: Stakeholder messages, content and channel plan completed (6 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Develop a single core narrative with tailored messages for regulators, clients, colleagues, media and other relevant audiences.
    - Sequence communications so audiences can absorb the information, prioritising critical messages rather than over-sharing, working with each impacted workstream to gather inputs and signoff
    - Select the appropriate mix of relationship-led, contact-centre, email, web, social, event, digital hub and self-service channels for each audience.
-
  Name: Client and colleague-facing teams briefed and equipped (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Prepare relationship-manager, leader, contact-centre and frontline briefing packs, FAQs, scripts and referral routes.
    - Use client-facing colleagues as subject-matter contributors and reassurance channels while maintaining approved-message controls.
    - Confirm query ownership, service escalation and rapid content-update processes with Operations, Product, Human Capital and Change Management.

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: LD1 communications and post-launch monitoring completed (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Execute regulatory, client, colleague, media and market communications in the approved sequence around cutover and LD1.
    - Monitor reach, engagement, questions, sentiment, service issues and reputational indicators across all channels during hypercare.
    - Refresh messages and content where audiences have not seen, understood or acted on the initial communications, then hand ongoing activity to BAU owners.

title: Compliance & Regulatory Approvals
text:
Key Role: Owns the compliance execution framework that makes the transaction controlled, regulator-ready and aligned to Absa policy.
Responsibilities:
  - Define applicable compliance obligations, approval paths, policy standards and completion evidence across the deal lifecycle.
  - Identify where conditions can be pre-agreed with regulators, and where data sharing can be agreed before full approval is received.
  - Identify compliance remediation, including regulatory approvals or notifications, policy exceptions, conduct risks, financial-crime controls, privacy constraints and outsourcing controls.
  - Advise on confidentiality, clean-room access, data sharing, client engagement, customer communications and restricted actions as the programme moves into execution
  - Validate local regulatory constraints that affect shared-service, Group Interchange, TSA and synergy assumptions with Finance & Tax, Legal & CorpDev and Regional Spokes.
  - Track compliance conditions, regulatory commitments, completion attestations and LD1 readiness evidence with the Central Hub.
  - Coordinate with Risk / Credit, KYC / AML, Data Migration, Product, Operations & Servicing, HR and Finance & Tax to embed compliance obligations in workstream plans.

title: Compliance & Regulatory Approvals
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Legal & CorpDev owns formal legal advice, transaction-document drafting, legal opinions and legal sign-off where required.
  - KYC / AML owns file-level due diligence, screening and remediation execution; Compliance sets policy interpretation, approval standards and control expectations.
  - Risk / Credit owns risk appetite and credit decisions; Central Hub owns programme coordination; Compliance owns compliance interpretation, approvals and readiness evidence.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns compliance execution decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local regulatory engagement, submission drafting, local control evidence, monitoring of local conditions and country compliance actions where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains group compliance interpretation, policy standards, financial-crime, conduct, privacy and outsourcing positions, central challenge and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into local approval execution and regulator-facing activity, with Function Authority retaining group standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

title: CRES
text: Key Role: Protects business continuity across the property estate while delivering the property, facilities and workplace changes required for integration, separation and longer-term estate optimisation. CRES confirms that critical premises and workplace services are operationally ready for LD1 and that property obligations are controlled through transition.

title: CRES
text:
Responsibilities:
  - Engage from due diligence to define the property and facilities perimeter, identify critical premises and surface long-lead estate dependencies before transaction terms and plans are fixed.
  - Assess owned and leased properties, occupancy, capacity, condition, utilisation, critical services, property contracts, costs, constraints and opportunities across the transaction perimeter.
  - Define the estate strategy and treatment for each location, including retain, transfer, assign, consolidate, relocate, fit out, share, sublet, terminate or dispose.
  - Develop property options, affordability assessments, business cases, capital and operating cost estimates, architecture input and governance submissions.
  - Manage leases, property agreements, landlord interfaces and facilities contracts with Legal, Procurement, Finance & Tax and in-country CRES teams.
  - Plan and deliver workplace design, construction, fit-out, moves, facilities mobilisation and long-lead procurement, allowing up to six months where new or materially changed premises are required.
  - Coordinate certifications, health and safety, physical security, access control, parking, utilities, workplace technology, cleaning, maintenance, catering and employee-facing workplace services.
  - Own the end-to-end workplace journey with Human Capital and Change Management, including employee impact,
  - Define and execute plans for branch and ATM rationalization and harmonization where required, driven by in-country teams

title: CRES
text:
Boundary Items:
  - CRES owns the property, workplace and facilities journey; Human Capital and Change Management own broader people impacts, communications and adoption with CRES input.
  - Procurement owns commercial sourcing and supplier process; CRES defines property and facilities requirements, technical specifications, service standards and acceptance evidence.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: CRES owns property, facilities and workplace decisions and evidence while the Central Hub integrates the estate roadmap into the programme plan, tracks long-lead dependencies and budget impacts, applies quality assurance and escalates readiness risks.
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including site surveys, landlord and supplier engagement, local approvals, facilities mobilisation, moves and readiness evidence where capability and capacity allow. Regional teams must own ATM and branch-related activities
  - Function Authority retains estate strategy, standards, architecture, affordability challenge, complex property decisions and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, ownership should expand from local evidence and coordination into end-to-end country estate delivery, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

title: Mandate Rows
text:
-
  Id: estate-perimeter-and-site-treatment
  Area: Estate perimeter and site treatment
  Spoke Authority:
    - Defines affected premises and recommends retain, transfer, consolidate, relocate, share, exit or dispose treatment for each site.

  Hub Role: Tests plan and budget impact, coordinates governance and tracks approved spend against the integrated plan.
  Governance: CRES investment governance, Finance & Tax, Procurement and accountable executive approvals.
  Escalation: Funding gap, approval delay, long-lead item or affordability issue threatens readiness.

  Governance: Programme SteerCo, accountable business owner, CRES and country leadership.
  Escalation: Critical premises, access, safety, facilities service or certification is not ready or evidenced.

title: CRES
text:
Capability Rows:
  -
    Category: Specific Project Manager required?
    Content: Maybe - for any material property change, multi-site transaction, workplace move or fit-out. Smaller transactions may use a named CRES delivery lead within the integrated programme plan.
  -
    Category: Baseline capabilities
    Content: Estate strategy; portfolio and occupancy analysis; lease and property management; workplace and facilities management; project management; affordability assessment; landlord and supplier coordination; health, safety and readiness control.
  -
    Category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity
    Content: Architecture and workplace design; construction and fit-out delivery; relocation planning; complex lease restructuring; multi-site and multi-country coordination; shared-site separation; property disposal; TSA service design; ATM rationalisation, Branch rationalisation
  -
    Category: Specialist capabilities triggered by deal characteristics
    Content: Property valuation; engineering and building condition; environmental assessment; physical security; fire and life safety; accessibility; data centre or specialist facility expertise; local certification and property-law support.

title: Data Migration
text:
Key Role: Owns the data migration delivery path from source-to-target mapping through cutover and reconciliation
Responsibilities:
  - Agree source and target data dictionaries, source-system access, target-system requirements and secure transfer protocols
  - Define source-to-target mapping, transformation logic, data cleansing, exception handling and reconciliation approach
  - Conduct data quality assessments, both on the structure and business usage of masked fields, and the detailed content of unmasked fields once received
  - Build and test migration routines, controlled extracts, mock loads, reporting data feeds and rollback
  - Coordinate data cuts, dress rehearsals, final data load, reconciliation and migration sign-off
  - Manage data migration defects, quality issues, lineage evidence and handover to BAU data owners.
Boundary Items:
  - Technology owns environments, interfaces and platform build
  - Independent Assurance independently validates migration design and results
  - Business workstreams own the business meaning and acceptance criteria for their data fields
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns data migration decisions and plan which should form the backbone of the programme plan owned by the Central Hub

title: Data Migration
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including source-data evidence, local data-owner sign-off, cleansing, reconciliation support, cutover steps and exception resolution where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains migration design, source-to-target standards, central tooling, reconciliation methodology, control evidence standards and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into data cleansing, reconciliation, mock-load support and cutover activity, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
External Dependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where timing, data, approvals or joint readiness affect LD1

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Data migration solution and data dictionary requirements defined (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Confirm data domains, source systems, target systems, field ownership, mandatory attributes and record-level controls for the transaction perimeter.
    - Agree data dictionaries, naming standards, reference data, data lineage expectations and evidence required for business acceptance.
    - Define transfer protocols, controls, permissions and storage locations for files
-
  Name: Data structure and usage assessment (2 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Work with counterparty to assess the structure of data tables and structures provided in a masked format, to understand key differences, gaps, and quality issues
    - Engage both Absa and Counterparty business stakeholders to understand what each field is actually used for, and whether there are any key differences between Absa and Counterparty practices
-
  Name: Source-to-target mapping conducted and business sign off secured (5 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Profile source data, identify quality gaps and map each source field to target fields, business rules and transformation logic
    - Confirm Product, Operations, Finance, Risk and Compliance acceptance for the business meaning of mapped fields
    - Track unresolved mapping decisions, assumptions and exclusions

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Data migration ETL solution design complete (6 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Design extraction, transformation, load, validation, exception handling and reconciliations
    - Define control totals, balancing checks, audit trail, rollback approach and defect severity rules
    - Confirm Technology environment, connectivity, storage and scheduling dependencies needed to run the ETL solution
-
  Name: Data migration ETL solution build complete (8 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Build ETL routines, migration scripts, validation reports, exception reports and reconciliation outputs.
    - Configure access, environments, run controls and source-file intake processes with Technology.
    - Complete unit testing and evidence capture before handing into SIT or mock-run cycles.
-
  Name: Data migration testing, including build, SIT, and mock runs (6 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Run build testing, SIT, data-quality testing and mock migration cycles against agreed success criteria.
    - Validate completeness, accuracy, record counts, balances, rejected records, exceptions and usability
    - Log defects, retest fixes and obtain acceptance for exceptions from data owners and business
-
  Name: Unmasked data quality assessment (1 week)
  Activities:
    - Conduct a full data quality assessment on unmasked data once received
    - Flag any material quality issues, structural differences, or unexpected deviations from masked data previously provided
    - Define remediation plan or operational workarounds for cutover

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Cutover planning conducted (2 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Build the data cutover runbook covering extracts, freezes, transfer windows, load sequence, validations, rollback and communications
    - Align cutover timing with Technology, Operations, E2E Testing, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Client Readiness.
    - Confirm owners, timings, dependencies, evidence and fallback decision points for final load
-
  Name: Dress Rehearsals led and assessed (3 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Run dress rehearsals using production-like data, production-like timing and agreed success criteria
    - Assess rehearsal outcomes for data quality, run duration, reconciliation, exception handling and downstream readiness.
    - Update migration design, cutover runbook and readiness evidence based on rehearsal findings.
-
  Name: Data Migration readiness assessed (2 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Issue a readiness view covering mapping, build, testing, reconciliation, exceptions, cutover plan and residual data risks.
    - Confirm no unresolved data-quality issue prevents go/no-go, regulatory evidence, customer outcomes or financial reporting.
    - Transfer open data actions to hypercare or BAU with clear ownership

title: E2E Testing
text:
Key Role: Owns end-to-end testing strategy, execution evidence, testing coordination, and defect governance across customer, colleague, data, technology, operations, supplier and readiness journeys.
Responsibilities:
  - Define end-to-end test strategy, test scope, entry criteria, exit criteria, evidence standards and defect governance.
  - Define success criteria for mock runs and dress rehearsals before execution, including data completeness, accuracy, reconciliation and operational acceptance.
  - Coordinate test journeys across Data Migration, Technology, Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Procurement, HR, Change and Legal dependencies.
  - Coordinate testing of customer, colleague, system, reporting, control, digital, cards, supplier, payment and servicing journeys that affect LD1 readiness.
  - Maintain defect triage, retest, acceptance, workaround and residual-risk evidence through readiness governance.
  - Provide test evidence into LD1 go/no-go, assurance, regulator, Internal Audit and post-LD1 hypercare decisions.

title: E2E Testing
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Technology owns technical build, environments and technical test execution; E2E Testing owns integrated journey coverage and evidence completeness.
  - Data Migration owns migration execution and reconciliations; E2E Testing validates that migrated data supports end-to-end business outcomes
  - Operations & Servicing owns operational process design and acceptance; E2E Testing validates that processes work across hand-offs.
  - Business, operations, and technology teams own the execution of testing, E2E Testing facilitates and coordinates
  - Risk and Independent Assurance challenge testing evidence, success criteria and residual risk acceptance.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: E2E Testing owns test design, execution evidence and defect governance while the Central Hub coordinates cross-workstream dependencies, decision cadence, issue escalation and readiness reporting.

title: E2E Testing
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including process walkthroughs, user acceptance support, local data and testers, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect retesting and local evidence production where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains test strategy, entry and exit criteria, evidence standards, integrated journey coverage, defect governance and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from test support into local execution, defect remediation and readiness sign-off, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

title: Coach boundary
text: The Experienced Coach helps people use prior deal experience to make better decisions on the current transaction. The Coach advises and challenges but does not enter the governance hierarchy, own delivery, approve outcomes or replace accountable leaders. The role is successful when knowledge is transferred, judgement improves and the Coach can step away.

title: Coach experience
Coach experience note
text: Coach experience note: Prior deal experience alone is not sufficient. The person must be able to transfer that experience in a way that strengthens the coachee's judgement and independence.

title: Coach involvement
text:
-
  Period: Role appointment and mobilisation
  Involvement: Targeted, moderate
  Level: 2
  Contribution: Clarify role expectations, share a small number of relevant start-up lessons, help the coachee prepare for mobilisation and agree how coaching will work.
  Why: Early support can prevent role confusion, but the Coach should not design the programme or mobilisation approach.
-
  Period: Detailed planning
  Involvement: Low
  Level: 1
  Contribution: Remain available for specific questions. Review an individual planning challenge only when requested. Do not attend routine planning workshops or draft the plan.
  Why: The workstream must own its plan. Deal-specific facts are still emerging, and too many experienced voices can create conflicting assumptions or premature solutions.
-
  Period: Plan agreed and early execution
  Involvement: High
  Level: 3
  Contribution: Work through the coachee's defined responsibilities, upcoming deliverables, decisions, stakeholder conversations and known pressure points. Test how the coachee plans to approach difficult items.
  Why: The coaching conversation is now grounded in a real plan, named ownership and specific outputs rather than general advice.
-
  Period: Routine execution
  Involvement: Moderate and pull-based
  Level: 2
  Contribution: Provide short advice before or after material decisions, escalations, governance sessions or difficult delivery moments. Reduce involvement where work is proceeding normally.
  Why: Coaching should sharpen judgement at points of need without becoming another layer of day-to-day delivery.

title: Coach involvement
text:
-
  Period: Testing and readiness
  Involvement: High at key points
  Level: 3
  Contribution: Challenge evidence, acceptance, defect treatment, dependencies, fallback thinking, readiness conditions and the quality of the recommendation.
  Why: Prior deal experience is valuable when teams must distinguish completed activity from credible operational readiness.
-
  Period: Dress-rehearsal and cutover planning
  Involvement: High
  Level: 3
  Contribution: Help the coachee anticipate sequencing problems, unclear authority, weak checkpoints, communications gaps, untested fallbacks and likely points of execution pressure. Dress rehearsals are referred to as DRs where an abbreviation is needed.
  Why: Cutover and DR planning benefit from pattern recognition and practical lessons from previous transactions. The accountable team still owns the runbook and decisions.
-
  Period: Live dress rehearsal or cutover
  Involvement: Low and on-call
  Level: 1
  Contribution: Remain available for a specific request, but do not join the command structure or offer unsolicited direction. Use the formal issue and decision routes.
  Why: Live execution needs clear authority and controlled communication. An additional advisory voice can slow decisions or confuse ownership.

title: Coach involvement
text:
-
  Period: Hypercare
  Involvement: Minimal
  Level: 0
  Contribution: Step in only for a defined capability need, a recurring pattern the team is struggling to resolve or preparation for handover. Do not attend routine hypercare calls by default.
  Why: Hypercare should be run by the accountable delivery and business teams. The priority is rapid operational ownership, not continued dependence on coaching.
-
  Period: Closure and lessons learned
  Involvement: Short, targeted
  Level: 2
  Contribution: Help the coachee reflect on decisions and capture approved, reusable lessons. Confirm whether any further development need remains.
  Why: A focused close-out completes the knowledge-transfer cycle without extending the assignment unnecessarily.

title: Coach involvement intro
text:
- Coaching should be targeted rather than continuous. The Coach is most useful when the coachee has a defined responsibility, deliverable, decision or upcoming event and can ask for advice against something specific.
- The Coach should be less involved while workstreams are still creating the detailed plan. Planning content and ownership must sit with the workstream, and important deal facts may still be unclear. Bringing previous-deal perspectives into every planning discussion can introduce too many voices, anchor the team to a different transaction and weaken ownership of the plan.
- Once the plan is sufficiently developed, the coachee has a specific list of activities, decisions and outputs. Coaching can then focus on how to approach those items, what problems to anticipate and how to test whether the planned response is strong enough.
- Use the following as the default involvement pattern. Adapt it where a specific capability gap or transaction risk justifies a different level.

title: Coach levels
text:
- in-country programme management office (PMO) teams
- Workstream Leads
- Workstream Executives
- Workstream Project Managers
- workstream team members

title: Coach mandate
Coach mandate
Coach not by default
text: Coach not by default: Do not involve the Coach by default simply because a meeting is taking place. Routine planning, status, governance, cutover and hypercare meetings should remain owned by the formal team.

title: Coach purpose
text:
- The Experienced Coach formalises how people with relevant deal experience support colleagues working on new transactions. The role makes previous lessons available at the point of need, rather than relying on informal networks or waiting for a retrospective after problems occur.
- The Coach helps the coachee understand what good looks like, recognise patterns, test assumptions and make better use of the M&A Capability Hub, operating model and programme resources. Advice must be adapted to the current transaction. A previous deal is evidence and experience, not a template that should be copied without challenge.

title: Coach responsibilities
text:
-
  Title: Transfer practical experience
  Items:
    - Share relevant lessons, decision patterns and examples from previous transactions.
    - Explain why an approach worked or failed, including the context and trade-offs.
    - Translate operating-model expectations into practical actions for the coachee's role.
    - Direct the coachee to current approved methods, resources and templates rather than creating personal alternatives.
-
  Title: Improve judgement
  Items:
    - Ask questions that test mandate, evidence, dependencies, timing, risk, value and decision authority.
    - Help the coachee distinguish routine delivery problems from matters requiring escalation.
    - Challenge optimism, unsupported status and assumptions that have not been tested.
    - Help frame credible options, consequences, recommendations and decision deadlines.
-
  Title: Anticipate recurring problems
  Items:
    - Highlight known pressure points before they become delivery issues.
    - Use the transaction archetype, lifecycle position and role context to focus attention.
    - Help the coachee recognise weak mobilisation, unclear ownership, capacity gaps, late dependencies, incomplete evidence and poor handover early.
    - Encourage proportionate controls rather than adding process by default.

title: Coach responsibilities
text:
-
  Title: Build role capability
  Items:
    - Agree a small number of practical development goals for the assignment.
    - Observe selected meetings, decisions or artefacts where this will improve coaching quality.
    - Give specific and timely feedback linked to live work.
    - Reduce support as the coachee demonstrates sound independent judgement.
-
  Title: Strengthen organisational learning
  Items:
    - Identify lessons that would help future transactions.
    - Separate reusable learning from transaction-confidential information.
    - Share agreed, anonymised lessons with the Central Hub capability owner.
    - Suggest improvements to learning pathways, role guidance or approved templates without changing controlled material directly.

title: Coach success
text:
-
  Title: Capability transfer
  Text: The coachee applies the role more confidently and requires less Coach input over time.
-
  Title: Judgement quality
  Text: Plans, status, decisions, escalations and readiness positions show clearer evidence, consequences and ownership.
-
  Title: Earlier action
  Text: Material dependencies, capacity gaps, risks and decisions are identified and raised while useful options remain.
-
  Title: Governance integrity
  Text: The coachee uses the correct decision and escalation routes. Coaching does not create shadow authority or dilute accountability.
-
  Title: Practical adoption
  Text: Relevant lessons and approved resources are used in live delivery, not only discussed in coaching sessions.
-
  Title: Independence
  Text: Support reduces as capability grows, and the assignment closes with the coachee able to perform the role independently.
-
  Title: Organisational learning
  Text: Useful lessons are captured in an approved, anonymised form and improve future role guidance, learning or mobilisation.

title: Coach summary
text:
-
  Field: Role
  Content: Experienced Coach
-
  Field: Purpose
  Content: Transfers practical mergers and acquisitions (M&A) experience from previous transactions into current delivery. Helps role-holders apply the operating model, anticipate common problems, strengthen judgement and build confidence without taking over their accountability.
-
  Field: Position in the model
  Content: An advisory capability outside the formal governance and delivery hierarchy. The Coach is not an additional approval layer and does not change any existing reporting line, decision right or accountability.
-
  Field: Reports to
  Content: No standing governance reporting line. Each assignment has a named Coaching Sponsor, normally the Transaction Director, Central Hub capability owner or relevant accountable leader, who agrees the purpose, access and escalation route. Coaching Sponsor means the owner of the coaching assignment and is not necessarily the transaction's Executive Sponsor.
-
  Field: Direct reports
  Content: None. A coaching relationship is not a line-management relationship.
-
  Field: Primary relationships
  Content: Named coachee or cohort; Coaching Sponsor; Central Hub or Inorganic Change capability team; relevant Programme Manager, Workstream Executive or country leader where agreed.

title: Coach summary
text:
-
  Field: Governance treatment
  Content: Do not assign the Coach accountable or responsible status in the transaction responsibility matrix. Where useful, record the Coach as an advisory contact or as consulted for a specific capability need. Attendance at a forum does not confer decision or approval rights.
-
  Field: Typical involvement
  Content: Targeted and event-based. Low during open-ended detailed planning; higher once a plan gives the coachee specific responsibilities and around testing, readiness, dress-rehearsal and cutover planning; low and on-call during live execution; minimal during routine hypercare.
-
  Field: Mandate
  Content: May advise, challenge, share relevant experience, review draft thinking, observe agreed delivery activity and recommend actions. May not approve, direct, sign off, reprioritise or own delivery on behalf of the coachee.
-
  Field: Core boundary
  Content: The coachee remains accountable for their decisions, outputs, escalation and performance. The Coach's success is measured by growing independent capability, not by becoming indispensable.
