title: Finance & Tax
text: Key Role: Owns finance and tax execution from deal economics through completion and LD1. Owns Group Interchange, TSA operation and BAU transition, and ensuring commercials, ledgers, liquidity, tax, reporting and controls remain operating

title: Finance & Tax
text:
Responsibilities:
  - Provide Finance input to the deal memo, pricing, costing, revenue, premium-to-NAV, goodwill, amortisation, stranded-cost, synergy and group P&L assumptions.
  - Define completion accounts, purchase price adjustments, funds flow, accounting treatment, tax exposures, funding, liquidity, settlement and FX requirements.
  - Own the finance side of Group Interchange and TSA service management, including service charging, recharges, buy-backs, cost recovery, invoicing and dispute controls
  - Define which finance-related services, reporting routines, payments, controls and processes must start, stop or continue across Absa, the acquired business, the seller or the buyer.
  - Align acquired or disposed business finance policies, ledgers, reporting standards, close calendars, account structures and control requirements to the agreed transaction model.
  - Coordinate Group Tax advice centrally while ensuring local tax, statutory reporting and regulatory finance requirements are captured through in-country teams.
  - Validate historic financial data, local ledgers, trial balances, management information, reconciliation approach and local reporting constraints with Regional Spokes.
  - Test finance data, ledgers, processes, payments, reports, P&L impacts, month-end close and reconciliation controls before LD1.
  - Confirm finance readiness for signing, completion, cutover, first close, hypercare and BAU handover.

title: Finance & Tax
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Legal & CorpDev owns transaction-document drafting and commercial negotiation route; Finance & Tax supplies costing, revenue, scenario planning, tax, accounting, completion mechanics, Group Interchange and TSA charging inputs.
  - Central Hub owns integrated programme governance and TSA dependency tracking; Finance & Tax owns financial design, recharge, buy-back, P&L and control evidence for Group Interchange and TSA services.
  - Procurement owns supplier contracting and third-party continuity; Finance & Tax owns spend baselining, payment-route design, cost allocation, stranded-cost analysis and supplier-related financial controls.
  - Technology and Data Migration own system build and data movement; Finance & Tax owns ledger mapping, finance data validation, accounting rules, reporting outputs and reconciliation requirements.
  - Regional Spokes own local finance evidence, local statutory reporting, close-calendar constraints and local regulatory finance nuance, with Group Finance and Group Tax retaining group-level standards and technical positions.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns finance and tax execution decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies, tracks TSA and Group Interchange critical path items, and escalates transaction-wide issues.

title: Finance & Tax
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local ledger evidence, statutory reporting inputs, local tax data, close-calendar constraints, reconciliations and first-close support where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains group accounting and tax positions, Group Interchange and TSA charging standards, completion accounts, group reporting, central review and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into ledger mapping, local reporting readiness, local tax execution and first-close activity, with Function Authority retaining group standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
External Dependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where timing, financial data, TSA charging, completion accounts, tax, approvals or joint readiness affect signing, completion or LD1.

title: Finance & Tax
text:
Capability Rows:
  -
    Category: Specific Project Manager required?
    Content: Maybe - dedicated Finance PM, TSA finance coordinator or Group Interchange lead is needed where completion mechanics, recharges, multi-country ledger mapping dependencies create risk
  -
    Category: Baseline capabilities
    Content: Deal economics, costing and revenue scenario planning; completion accounts; funds flow; treasury funding; liquidity and FX management; tax assessment; accounting policy; financial-control design; reporting and reconciliation control.
  -
    Category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity
    Content: Group Interchange and TSA charging; recharge and buy-back mechanics; stranded-cost and synergy tracking; purchase accounting; premium-to-NAV and amortisation modelling; multi-entity ledger mapping; local statutory and regulatory reporting alignment; close-calendar transition.
  -
    Category: Specialist capabilities triggered by deal characteristics
    Content: Group Tax and local tax advisory; transfer pricing, VAT, withholding tax and deferred tax; regulatory capital and liquidity; external audit engagement; complex-product accounting; cross-border finance reporting; service-pricing and dispute management.

title: Workstream Sessions
text:
Id: workstream-sessions
Index: 1
Name: Workstream Sessions
Short: Workstream Sessions
Kind: internal
Objective: Align on key RAIDs within the workstream, and items for escalation to the Transaction Working Group
Chair: Workstream Accountable Exec
Facilitator: Workstream Lead
Cadence: Weekly, 60 minutes
Decision Type: Decision making (WS Level items)
Attendees: Workstream AE, Workstream Lead, Workstream PM (as applicable)
Inputs: Workstream L2 Plan, Workstream level RAID log
Agenda:
  - Overview of L2 plan, and progress against activities
  - Review of workstream RAID log, assessment of each item
  - Agreement on items for escalation and key dependencies
  - Agreement on where workstream needs support, and items for AE to take away
Outputs:
  - Workstream Status Report
Success:
  - Continuously updated workstream-level RAID Log
  - Detailed L2 plan tracked consistently
  - alignment of which RIAD items must be escalated
  - clear mitigation plans for critical items and escalation paths

title: Workstream Sessions
text:
Remedial:
  - Rebuild or rebaseline the L2 plan where activities, dependencies, milestones or ownership are incomplete or no longer credible
  - Review overdue and off-track activities individually, agreeing recovery actions and revised delivery dates
  - Define clear thresholds for which RAID items should be managed within the workstream and which require escalation
  - Assign a named owner, target date and escalation route to every critical RAID item
  - Hold targeted working sessions for critical issues that cannot be resolved within the regular workstream meeting
  - Increase the frequency of progress reviews temporarily where the workstream is materially behind plan or carrying significant unresolved risk

title: Governance forums

Cadence: Fortnightly, 90 mins
Decision Type: Make decisions on transaction critical items, even if not usually in their remit under BAU (e.g., budget, resourcing)
Attendees: Absa Workstream Executives, TD, Prog. Manager, AE
Inputs: Joint SteerCo Pack + Ad Hoc Materials
Agenda:
  - Programme update
  - Progress against the plan and budget
  - Risks, Issues and Dependencies
  - Absa internal decisions
Outputs:
  - Items to focus on at Joint SteerCo
  - Internal Absa decisions
Success:
  - Decisions made in the room, based on materials provided
  - Deep engagement, questioning, and challenge from members
  - Cross-functional collaboration of executives to support decision making
  - Prioritised in busy diaries

title: Absa Internal SteerCo
text:
Remedial:
  - Contact members who are not engaging or attending to reconfirm expectations and understand any barriers to participation
  - Escalate persistent non-attendance or delegation to the Executive Sponsor
  - Request explicit views from relevant executives during the meeting where sufficient challenge or cross-functional input is absent
  - Assign named executive sponsors to decisions requiring coordination across multiple functions
  - Introduce delegated decision-makers where diary constraints repeatedly prevent the correct representation
  - Escalate decisions that remain unresolved beyond the agreed deadline, with the resulting impact on the transaction clearly stated

title: Joint SteerCo
text:
Id: joint-steerco
Index: 6
Name: Joint SteerCo
Short: Joint SteerCo
Kind: joint
Objective: To provide oversight of joint migration plan, assess readiness to progress to the next stage during programme tollgates, and resolve issues that have been escalated by the Joint Programme Management Office.
Chair: Absa and Counterparty Executive Sponsors
Facilitator: Absa and Counterparty Transaction Directors
Cadence: Fortnightly, 60 mins
Decision Type: Decision making (Joint, programme level items)
Attendees: Absa / Counterparty Executive Teams, TDs, Prog. Managers
Inputs: Joint SteerCo Pack
Agenda:
  - Action points
  - Programme progress and unresolved joint programme issues
  - Issues or risks requiring attention
  - Items for decision making
  - Change in overall implementation programme strategy if any
  - Changes in scope
  - Any other business
Outputs:
  - Joint programme decisions
Success:
  - Decisions jointly debated and made in the room
  - Robust but respectful debate - not anger or silence
  - Overall focus on the success of the transaction, rather than personal or entity-specific issues

title: Joint SteerCo
text:
Remedial:
  - Hold pre-alignment discussions between the two executive sponsors where contentious decisions are likely to prevent productive debate
  - Restate the shared transaction objectives and agreed decision principles where discussion becomes entity-specific or positional
  - Escalate unresolved decisions through the agreed transaction governance route, with clear options, risks and consequences of delay
  - Record the rationale for each joint decision to prevent previously resolved issues from being reopened without new evidence
  - Address persistent unconstructive behaviour directly with the relevant executive outside the forum and agree expectations for future meetings

title: Human Capital
text:
Key Role: Human Capital owns employee-transfer execution and people readiness, including terms, consultation, onboarding, payroll, benefits, reward, employee data, retention and people transition into BAU.
Responsibilities:
  - Confirm employee perimeter, roles, grades, contracts, terms, benefits, reward, payroll, pensions, unions, mobility, wellness and consultation obligations.
  - Bring employee legal into due diligence so Human Capital can plan transfer mechanics, consultation timing, S197 implications, CP dependencies and negotiation points early.
  - Define people-transfer approach, organisational design, leadership appointments, retention interventions, reward / REM decisions and onboarding requirements.
  - Plan and execute employee consultation, employee engagement, offer or transfer processes, union engagement and employee-data controls with Legal and Compliance.
  - Stand up or transition payroll, pension, benefits, HR systems, manager readiness, training and day-one access for transferring employees.
  - Coordinate strategic employee communications with Communications and Change
  - Track employee acceptance, resignations, key-person risk, wellbeing, cultural adaptation and post-LD1 people issues.

title: Human Capital
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Legal owns legal interpretation of employment-transfer obligations, commercial provisions and CPs that affect people activity.
  - Change Management owns adoption of new ways of working; Human Capital provides people expertise, employee readiness inputs and change impact detail.
  - Communications / Marketing owns channels, tone and approval flow; Human Capital owns employee content and consultations
  - Technology owns HR system access, employee data tooling and identity integration; Human Capital owns employee data requirements and people readiness
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: Human Capital owns people-transfer and HR readiness decisions and evidence while the Central Hub coordinates dependencies, decision timing, issue escalation and integration of people milestones into the wider programme plan.

title: Human Capital
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including employee data, local consultation steps, unions, payroll and benefits inputs, employee engagement, wellbeing actions and local HR readiness where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains people-transfer standards, consultation integrity, reward and REM decisions, central workforce planning, specialist HR support and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and local nuance into consultation support, people-readiness execution and hypercare activity, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Consultation and employee communications plan agreed and executed (6 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Define consultation steps, employee engagement route, leadership briefings and approval timing.
    - Agree with Change and Communications whether the current employer or new employer leads each communication.
    - Prepare strategic employee communications for late-stage uncertainty, wellness, retention and cutover emotion.
    - Execute and track consultations, assessing employee reactions and adapting where required
    - Hold individual one-to-one meetings where required to explain contract, level, and benefits
    - Work with seller to collate employee questions, and set up FAQs, as well as regular townhalls structured around a question theme
-
  Name: Cultural alignment analysis and remediation plan complete (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Assess key cultural differences between Absa and seller, and impact on operating model

    - Sequence, plan, and execute remediation activities, and conduct pulse surveys to track impact

title: Milestones
text:
-
  Name: Payroll, benefits, pension and employee-data readiness planned (8 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Define payroll stand-up or transition requirements, banking policy benefits, contractual benefits and reward decisions.
    - Confirm pension fund approval requirements and earliest permissible employee communication or process start date.
    - Agree employee data transfer requirements with Technology, including completeness, accuracy, privacy and system onboarding needs.
-
  Name: Organisational design complete (4 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Work with business and functional areas to discuss leveling and role cards for incoming employees
    - Map these roles into existing Absa structures and define reporting lines
    - Socialise these with both incoming employees and managers, and iterate where significant issues arise
    - Define the approach to transferring portfolios of client facing employees: kept as-is, adapted, or merged into Absa portfolios
-
  Name: Onboarding, training and people readiness evidenced (6 weeks)
  Activities:
    - Plan system onboarding, manager readiness, L&D compliance, functional training and technical training.
    - Track employee sign-offs, acceptance, resignations, key-person risks and readiness evidence.
    - Confirm Human Capital inputs to LD1 readiness and post-LD1 people monitoring

-
  Name: Post-LD1 people stability monitored (4 weeks)
  Activities:

    - Resolve people risks through hypercare with HR, Change, Communications, Technology and Finance.

title: Independent Assurance / External Audit
text: Key Role: External independent assurers provide objective assurance over whether programme governance, controls, migration, testing, cutover and readiness evidence are sufficient to support transaction decisions. They assess and report; they do not own delivery remediation or programme decision-making.

title: Independent Assurance / External Audit
text:
Responsibilities:
  - Perform independent assessment of programme governance, decision quality, delivery controls, issue escalation and readiness evidence.
  - Assess whether workstream plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions and evidence are sufficient to support signing, completion, LD1 and post-LD1 decisions.
  - Review control design and operating-readiness evidence across business, operations, technology, data, risk, compliance, finance, procurement and people activity.
  - Assess migration design, source-to-target mapping, ETL controls, data completeness, data accuracy, reconciliations, exceptions and fallback arrangements.
  - Assess test strategy, SIT, E2E testing, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect triage, retesting, accepted workarounds and test-exit evidence.
  - Assess cutover readiness, command-centre arrangements, contingency plans, hypercare entry criteria and BAU handover evidence.
  - Assess specific high-risk readiness areas such as digital delivery, cards production and fulfilment, customer communications, regulatory evidence and TSA controls where applicable.
  - Raise independent findings, recommendations, assurance opinions and residual concerns to the agreed programme governance forums.
  - Validate remediation closure evidence for agreed findings without taking ownership of delivery remediation.
  - Maintain an evidence trail that can support programme governance, Internal Audit, regulator-facing reviews and post-completion audit requirements.

title: Independent Assurance / External Audit
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Delivery workstreams own execution, remediation and evidence production; external independent assurers assess the adequacy of that evidence and the credibility of readiness conclusions.
  - The Central Hub owns programme governance, integrated planning, RAID tracking and evidence coordination; external independent assurers assess whether those controls are operating effectively.
  - Risk owns the 2LOD risk judgement and risk appetite route; external independent assurers provide independent evidence-based assurance over risk-related programme controls and readiness evidence.
  - Internal Audit provides 3LOD assurance where commissioned; external independent assurers provide the independent assurance procedures and opinions defined in their engagement scope.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Central Hub provides the integrated plan, governance materials, evidence owners, issue logs and access to workstreams; external independent assurers assess whether the programme evidence supports the required decisions and report findings through the agreed governance route.

title: Independent Assurance / External Audit
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including evidence collation, control-owner walkthroughs, local context, access facilitation and remediation evidence where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains assurance scope, testing approach, independent assessment, findings, opinions and central escalation where regional maturity, evidence quality, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local teams should provide stronger self-evidencing and direct assurance responses, while Function Authority retains objective assessment, specialist challenge and independent reporting.
External Dependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where buyer, seller, country, regulator or third-party evidence is required for assurance procedures.

title: Mandate Rows
text:
-
  Id: programme-governance-and-decision-quality
  Area: Programme governance and decision quality
  Spoke Authority:
    - Assess whether governance forums, packs, decisions, RAID management, dependency tracking and issue escalation are effective and evidence-based.
  Hub Role: Provides governance materials, decision logs, RAID logs, plan data and access to programme forums.
  Governance: Programme SteerCo, accountable executive, Central Hub, workstream leads and Internal Audit where relevant.
  Escalation: Decisions are made without evidence, SteerCos are cancelled or ineffective, or material issues are not escalated in time.
-
  Id: controls-and-readiness-evidence
  Area: Controls and readiness evidence
  Spoke Authority:
    - Assess whether control design, control ownership, operating-readiness evidence, risk acceptances and remediation closure support the readiness conclusion.
  Hub Role: Coordinates evidence owners and tracks assurance findings through programme governance.
  Governance: Risk, Compliance, Operations, Technology, Finance, Procurement, HR and relevant business owners.
  Escalation: Control evidence is incomplete, remediation is not evidenced, or ownership remains unclear at go/no-go.

title: Mandate Rows
text:
-
  Id: migration-and-data-assurance
  Area: Migration and data assurance
  Spoke Authority:
    - Assess migration design, mapping, ETL controls, data completeness, accuracy, reconciliation, exceptions and fallback evidence.
  Hub Role: Coordinates data evidence, defect ownership and dependency escalation.
  Governance: Data Migration, Technology, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Data Governance.

title: Internal Audit
text: Key Role: Provides independent, risk-based third-line assurance over whether programme governance, risk management, controls and readiness evidence are designed and operating effectively across the transaction. Internal Audit reports findings and residual risk through its independent governance route; it does not own programme delivery, remediation or the go-live decision.

title: Internal Audit
text:
Responsibilities:
  - Engage early enough to assess the transaction risk profile, define a proportionate audit and assurance plan and allow management sufficient time to remediate findings before LD1.
  - Maintain independence from programme delivery while obtaining access to governance forums, plans, status reporting, RAID logs, budgets, decisions, testing evidence and accountable executives.
  - Assess whether programme governance, roles, decision rights, executive accountability, PMO disciplines, reporting and escalation routes are clear and operating effectively.
  - Review whether material transaction risks and controls are identified, owned, monitored, accepted and escalated through an effective three-lines model.
  - Perform risk-based deep dives across financial controls, regulatory delivery, technology, cyber, data migration, operations, customer outcomes, people, suppliers, TSA services and business readiness.
  - Review cutover planning, rollback and contingency, go/no-go criteria, readiness attestations, evidence quality and residual risk presented to decision-makers.
  - Issue findings in real time, agree accountable management actions and due dates, escalate overdue or material items and independently validate closure evidence.
  - Provide a clear independent view of residual risk entering LD1 and complete post-go-live review, handover and lessons learned where within approved scope.

title: Internal Audit
text:
Boundary Items:
  - The Central Hub and workstreams own governance and delivery controls; Internal Audit independently assesses them and does not design or operate remediation.
  - Risk owns second-line risk oversight and acceptance processes; Internal Audit provides third-line assurance over the adequacy and effectiveness of risk management and controls.
  - Independent Assurance / External Audit performs its commissioned external assurance scope; Internal Audit retains its own mandate, reporting line and professional judgement while coordinating coverage to reduce unnecessary duplication.
  - E2E Testing and Data Migration own test and migration execution and evidence; Internal Audit assesses governance, coverage, control performance, exceptions and readiness conclusions.
  - Accountable executives and programme governance make go/no-go and risk acceptance decisions; Internal Audit provides independent findings and a residual-risk view to inform those decisions.
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Central Hub provides integrated programme information, evidence access and remediation coordination; Internal Audit independently sets and executes its approved scope, reports findings through audit governance and escalates material concerns without becoming part of programme management.

title: Internal Audit
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own management responses, evidence production and remediation execution for in-country findings where they have the authority, capability and capacity.
  - Function Authority and Group Internal Audit retain audit scoping, methodology, rating, reporting, closure validation and specialist review where regional audit maturity, independence, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local Internal Audit teams may perform delegated fieldwork and follow-up, while Group Internal Audit retains consolidated coverage, quality review and reporting for transaction-wide risks.

title: Mandate Rows
text:
-
  Id: internal-audit-risk-assessment-and-scope
  Area: Internal Audit risk assessment and scope
  Spoke Authority:
    - Sets the risk-based audit scope, timing, methodology, skills and reporting route while preserving independence.
  Hub Role: Provides transaction context, integrated milestones, risk information and access to workstreams and evidence owners.
  Governance: Chief Audit Executive or Internal Audit governance and relevant Audit Committee oversight.
  Escalation: Material risk, scope limitation, late engagement, missing skill or timetable compression undermines adequate coverage.
-
  Id: finding-severity-and-reporting
  Area: Finding severity and reporting
  Spoke Authority:
    - Determines finding, root-cause, rating, residual-risk and reporting conclusions using Internal Audit methodology.
  Hub Role: Supports factual validation, identifies accountable management owners and integrates agreed actions into programme tracking.
  Governance: Internal Audit leadership, accountable executives and Audit Committee or equivalent governance as applicable.
  Escalation: Management disputes a material finding, restricts reporting or does not accept an adequate action.

  Area: Remediation and closure validation
  Spoke Authority:

  Hub Role: Tracks programme dependencies and due dates while management owners execute remediation.
  Governance: Accountable executive, Internal Audit and programme governance for delivery impacts.
  Escalation: Critical action is late, ineffective, unsupported by evidence or remains open near a decision gate.

  Spoke Authority:
    - Provides an independent view of material open findings, control effectiveness and residual risk entering LD1 without making the go-live decision.
  Hub Role: Presents the view alongside integrated readiness evidence, exceptions and management risk acceptance.
  Governance: Programme SteerCo, accountable executives, Risk governance and Audit Committee as applicable.
  Escalation: Readiness evidence is unreliable, critical findings remain open or residual risk is not transparently accepted.

text:
Key Role: Owns client financial-crime file assessment, remediation and acceptance input for onboarding or transfer.
Responsibilities:
  - Identify transferring clients, counterparties, beneficial owners, mandates and file populations requiring KYC / AML review
  - Assess counterparty documentation, risk ratings, sanctions, PEP, adverse media and enhanced due diligence needs
  - Define reliance, refresh, remediation, exclusion and onboarding approaches with Compliance and Risk
  - Track missing documentation, client outreach requirements, remediation progress and acceptance decisions.
  - Provide KYC / AML readiness evidence for client onboarding, LD1 readiness and go/no-go governance
Boundary Items:
  - Compliance owns policy interpretation and financial-crime approval
  - Operations & Servicing owns onboarding process operation and customer interaction
  - Legal owns data-sharing, clean-room and client-consent constraints
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns KYC and AML readiness decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.

title: KYC / AML
text:
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including file evidence, documentation remediation, screening inputs, client outreach, onboarding execution and local exception resolution where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains KYC / AML standards, reliance approach, remediation criteria, quality review, exception management and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from file evidence into remediation execution, client outreach and onboarding readiness, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
External Dependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where timing, data, approvals or joint readiness affect LD1.

title: Client Readiness
text:
Key Role: Owns integrated Client readiness orchestration and tracking with a focus on customer / client readiness including onboarding tracking, client outreach tracking, client training, and ensuring channels are set up
Responsibilities:
  - Track required client contact to receive requisite onboarding documentation
  - Track onboarding processes carried out by Operations teams
  - Support the preparation of client training materials, and track training delivery
  - Track Operations set up of clients on channels and platforms
  - Ensure that clients are ready to transact on LD1
Boundary Items:
  - Operations owns the execution of onboarding, training and set up activities, Client readiness acts as a centralized tracking layer
  - Risk and Independent Assurance challenge readiness evidence and residual risk; Client readiness integrates client readiness views into decision forums.
  - E2E Testing owns testing evidence and defects; Client readiness supports with organisation of friendly client testing where needed
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: Central Hub owns overall programme governance and go / no-go pack; Client readiness owns the tracking of client readiness

title: Client Readiness
text:

  - Regional operations Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including client outreach, setup, training, and maintenance
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from readiness evidence into cutover execution, local sign-off and hypercare support, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
  - Regional Client readiness spoke in specific unlikely to be in place - leverages Operations teams

title: Seventy-two hours to the programme readiness forum
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
Seventy-two hours to the programme readiness forum
text:
Title: Seventy-two hours to the programme readiness forum
Intro: The readiness forum is in three days. You know that:
Facts:
  - all workstreams report green, but a critical hand-off has been accepted by the sender and not the receiver;
  - a country control pack is complete but has not been reviewed by the specialist owner;
  - a supplier change would protect stability but uses programme contingency and delays one benefit; and
  - a conditional decision was given verbally and has not been recorded.
Close: Answer from your selected role.
Improved: You are now applying the Central Hub role through clear boundaries, one reliable programme view and well-routed decisions.
Review: You have completed the pathway. Review the highlighted module before using the playbook on a live transaction.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: view
  Question: How should the integrated programme position be represented?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Green, because every workstream reports green and no milestone is late.
      Feedback: An unaccepted critical hand-off means green is not supported.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Red, because several pieces of evidence are incomplete three days out.
      Feedback: Sets severity before testing whether the gaps can close in time.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: The supported forecast, showing the unaccepted hand-off, the unreviewed pack and what closes each.
      Feedback: Recommended. It shows the real delivery path, not the sum of ratings.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Green overall, with the open items listed in an appendix for reference.
      Feedback: Hides exceptions that affect the recommendation.
  Answer: c
  Reasoning: The programme view is useful when it reveals where one team's assumption changes another team's outcome.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: mandate
  Question: What should the Central Hub do about the hand-off and the control pack?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Accept the hand-off and the pack on the owners' behalf to keep the forum on track.
      Feedback: Acceptance and specialist review stay with their owners.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Get the receiver's acceptance and the specialist review, each with an owner and a date before the forum.
      Feedback: Recommended. The Hub coordinates and challenges; owners accept and approve.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Remove both items from the forum pack until they are complete.
      Feedback: Hides open conditions from the decision-makers.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Ask the country to confirm its own pack so the specialist review is not needed.
      Feedback: Bypasses a reserved specialist approval.
  Answer: b
  Reasoning: Create one reliable programme view while leaving functional and specialist decisions with their owners.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: decision
  Question: How should the supplier choice be prepared and routed?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Approve the change now, as stability matters more than one delayed benefit.
      Feedback: Uses contingency and moves value without the right authority.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Reject the change to protect contingency and the benefit date.
      Feedback: Decides the trade-off without testing it.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Leave the choice with the supplier's workstream, as it is their contract.
      Feedback: Contingency and benefits are programme-level effects.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Frame the options with stability, contingency and benefit effects and a recommendation, and route to the right authority.
      Feedback: Recommended. It makes the trade-off clear and keeps accountability with the right owner.
  Answer: d
  Reasoning: Challenge should make the decision clearer while keeping accountability with the right owner.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: control
  Question: What readiness recommendation and conditions should go to the forum?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Ready with conditions: name each open item, its owner and deadline, and record the verbal decision first.
      Feedback: Recommended. Accepted evidence, clear conditions and a recorded decision.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Ready, relying on the verbal decision to cover the open items.
      Feedback: An unrecorded decision cannot support a forum recommendation.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Not ready, and ask the forum to reschedule until every item is closed.
      Feedback: Pre-empts a decision that belongs to the forum.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: No recommendation, and let the forum judge the evidence itself.
      Feedback: The Hub should bring the evidence together into a recommendation.
  Answer: a
  Reasoning: Reliable reporting shows the supported forecast and unresolved choice, with decisions recorded before they are relied on.

title: Cutoff options
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
Pm:
  Answer: c
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Report both ratings as submitted and note the conflict in the commentary.
      Feedback: Leaves a negotiated picture, not the supported forecast.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Change Finance to amber yourself so the programme view is consistent.
      Feedback: The rating belongs to Finance; you must test the evidence with them.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Test both positions against evidence, show the critical-path effect and flag the decision needed.
      Feedback: Recommended. It reports the supported forecast and the unresolved choice.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Hold the programme report until the two workstreams agree a single date.
      Feedback: Delays senior visibility of a critical-path risk.
Pmo:
  Answer: b
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Change Finance to amber so the pack matches the Technology submission.
      Feedback: That is a management judgement, not a control action.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Record both submissions, flag the conflict and its critical-path link, and alert the Programme Manager.
      Feedback: Recommended. You make the conflict traceable and reach the right person in time.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Accept Finance's green because it arrived first and is inside the cut-off.
      Feedback: Timing of submission does not make information reliable.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Ask Technology to withdraw its update until Finance has confirmed it.
      Feedback: Suppresses a material risk.

Td:
  Answer: d

      Feedback: You own the execution message; test it first.
    -
      Id: b

      Feedback: Directs a result without testing options or consequences.
    -
      Id: c

      Feedback: Escalates before using your own authority.
    -
      Id: d

title: Five days to the programme working group
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
Five days to the programme working group
text:
Title: Five days to the programme working group
Intro: The working group is in five days. You know that:
Facts:
  - two workstreams use the same dependency date but describe different deliverables;
  - a country plan is green, although its customer-readiness evidence is incomplete;
  - a decision paper gives two options but does not quantify cost or schedule effects; and
  - a material change was agreed on a call but has not entered the decision or change record.
Close: Answer from your selected role. All three roles see the same facts but act within different authority.
Message: Several choices can look reasonable from a Hub seat. The modules show how integration, challenge, decision routing and control discipline decide the best response for your role.

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: mandate
  Question: Where is the boundary between the Hub and the two workstreams on the dependency?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: The Hub decides which deliverable is right and updates both workstream plans to match.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: The Hub makes the mismatch visible and has both owners agree the deliverable and acceptance.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: The Hub records the date as aligned, since both plans show it, and monitors it weekly.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: The Hub asks the functional spoke to take over both deliverables until they are aligned.
  Answer: b
-
  Capability: view
  Question: What must change before the programme view is reliable?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Average the workstream ratings so no single green or red distorts the overall picture.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Keep the country green and add the customer evidence gap to the commentary.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Reconcile the dependency and test the country rating against its customer-readiness evidence.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Move the whole programme to red until every workstream can evidence its status.
  Answer: c

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: decision
  Question: How should the decision be prepared and routed?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Send the paper as it is so the forum can ask for the missing effects if it needs them.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Pick the cheaper option on the forum's behalf, since the costs are likely to be similar.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Hold the decision until the next baseline cycle, when better cost data will exist.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Have the owner add cost and schedule effects, a recommendation and a deadline, then route it.
  Answer: d
-
  Capability: control
  Question: How should the change agreed on the call affect status, records and the baseline?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Record it in the decision and change logs, confirm who approved it, then update the plan and status.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Update the plan straight away, as the change was agreed, and add the record later.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Leave the plan unchanged until the change is raised again at a formal forum.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Note the change in the status narrative and let the workstream update its own plan.
  Answer: a

title: Lens notes
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
Pm:
  Role: As Programme Manager, you turn direction into an integrated programme view, test trade-offs and prepare recommendations. Wider programme decisions go to the Transaction Director.
  Scenario: As Programme Manager, you test the facts across workstreams, frame the options and recommend. You do not make the transaction-level decision.
  Playbook: Is there a clear recommendation, decision owner and deadline?
Pmo:
  Role: As PMO Support, you keep plans, logs, packs and records reliable. You flag gaps and inconsistencies, and take anything needing management judgement to the Programme Manager.
  Scenario: As PMO Support, you make the facts complete and traceable, flag what is missing and alert the Programme Manager before the deadline. You do not settle the judgement.
  Playbook: Has the matter reached the Programme Manager before the reporting or decision deadline?
Td:
  Role: As Transaction Director, you set execution direction and decide transaction-level matters within delegated authority. Reserved matters go to the Executive Sponsor or formal governance.
  Scenario: As Transaction Director, you decide within mandate or sponsor escalation. Functional and specialist approvals stay with their owners.
  Playbook: Is this decision within my delegated authority, or reserved for the Executive Sponsor, formal governance or a specialist?

text:

- Value effect: what does this choice do to cost, contingency, benefits or value?
- Owner: who owns the outcome, and who records and follows it through?
