B: Client Readiness plan: Customer data migration complete, 12 July. Customer letters issue from reconciled records on 13 July.

title: View options
breadcrumb: Central Hub Programme Management pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: Nothing material. Both plans share the milestone name and date.
  Feedback: Matching names and dates do not prove matching content.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Client Readiness expects reconciled records; Technology only commits to migration being complete.
  Feedback: Recommended. One team's assumption changes the other team's outcome.
-
  Id: c
  Text: Technology does not say what time on 12 July the migration completes.
  Feedback: A fair point, but less material than the content mismatch.
-
  Id: d
  Text: Client Readiness leaves only one day between migration and letters.
  Feedback: A tight gap, but the bigger issue is what 'complete' means.

title: Baseline steps
text:
-
  Step: Frame
  Focus: Set integration principles and require clear workstream charters, outcomes and constraints.
  Outcome: Teams understand their scope, interfaces and decisions.
-
  Step: Diagnose
  Focus: Bring together gaps, inventories, assumptions and readiness implications across workstreams.
  Outcome: Important unknowns are visible and owned.
-
  Step: Plan
  Focus: Challenge milestones, resources, costs, dependencies, acceptance criteria and risks.
  Outcome: Workstream plans hold together and can be delivered.
-
  Step: Integrate
  Focus: Resolve interfaces, align joint milestones and expose critical-path consequences.
  Outcome: The programme plan reflects the whole transaction.
-
  Step: Challenge and approve
  Focus: Coordinate assurance, review remaining risk, and approve the budget and baseline.
  Outcome: Governance authorises controlled delivery.

title: Boundary
text: Boundary: functional design, specialist approvals, local regulatory judgement, workstream delivery, source readiness evidence, legal interpretation, or the formal go or no-go decision.

title: Boundary owns
text: The Transaction Director owns maintenance of the execution case and integrated execution direction within the approved transaction strategy. The Hub owns making delivery inputs visible, connected, challenged and routed into timely decisions. It does not rewrite the deal rationale or take decisions reserved for the Executive Sponsor, formal governance or a specialist authority.

title: Control loop
text:
-
  Title: Gather current evidence
  Text: Receive workstream plans, status, RAID, decisions, dependencies, readiness evidence and cost inputs by the agreed cut-off.
-
  Title: Build the overall programme view
  Text: Reconcile milestones, hand-offs, assumptions and knock-on effects between workstreams. Spot where a workstream's own rating does not match the overall forecast.
-
  Title: Challenge quality and completeness
  Text: Check whether plans can be delivered, whether evidence supports completion, whether mitigations are credible, and whether decision papers show options and consequences.
-
  Title: Route decisions and escalation
  Text: Resolve programme-management matters within your authority. Send functional, local, specialist and senior matters to the correct authority before the last responsible decision date.
-
  Title: Run governance
  Text: Use forums to make decisions, resolve trade-offs and confirm accountability. Do not use them just to read out status, and do not delay urgent issues until the next meeting.
-
  Title: Record and follow through
  Text: Update the plan, logs, budget view and reporting narrative. Check that decisions turn into actions and that closure evidence is kept.

title: Core resources
text:
-
  Name: Hub and Spoke operating model
  Purpose: Sets out programme roles, ownership, who decides what, interfaces, and the central, functional and regional delivery model.
  When: During mobilisation, when designing accountability, and in any ownership or escalation dispute.
-
  Name: Mobilisation roadmap and toolkit
  Purpose: Gives the mobilisation sequence, gates, minimum controls, role standards and planning framework.
  When: Before signing where possible, and throughout mobilisation and baseline approval.
-
  Name: Lifecycle master and archetype guidance
  Purpose: Identifies transaction activities, considerations and documents that may apply to the deal.
  When: To tailor mobilisation, workstream activation and planning depth to the transaction.
-
  Name: Onboarding pack and rules of engagement
  Purpose: Explains deal context, confidentiality, governance, responsibilities and approved ways of working.
  When: At programme launch, and when new members join.
-
  Name: Programme organisation chart and interface directory
  Purpose: Records roles, contacts, deputies, counterpart interfaces and escalation routes.
  When: During mobilisation, and whenever accountabilities or people change.
-
  Name: Governance terms of reference and calendar
  Purpose: Sets out each forum's authority, purpose, attendees, inputs, outputs, frequency and production deadlines.
  When: When setting up or changing internal and joint governance.

title: Core resources
text:
-
  Name: Integrated programme plan
  Purpose: Connects transaction milestones, critical path, workstream plans, dependencies and decision dates.
  When: Maintain throughout planning, execution, readiness, cutover and closure.
-
  Name: Programme RAID, dependency, action, decision and change logs
  Purpose: Give traceable ownership, ageing, escalation and closure across the programme.
  When: Maintain continuously, and update after decisions or material changes.
-
  Name: Integrated status and executive reporting pack
  Purpose: Gives senior leaders a clear view of the forecast, material exceptions, costs and decisions needed.
  When: At the agreed reporting frequency, and whenever material conditions change.
-
  Name: Budget and business-case tracking inputs
  Purpose: Connect spend, forecast, costs, benefits, synergies and financial risks to delivery decisions.
  When: During baseline approval, change control and ongoing performance reporting.

title: Decide lens note
text:
Td: Makes execution-related, transaction-level decisions within delegated authority, including intra-transaction trade-offs, approved-budget deployment and key programme appointments. Escalates strategic, reserved or out-of-tolerance matters to the Executive Sponsor or formal governance.
Pm: Makes programme-management decisions about the integrated plan, how governance runs, dependency control and reporting. Prepares recommendations and escalates transaction-wide trade-offs, approved-budget allocations and wider programme decisions to the Transaction Director.
Pmo: Applies the agreed controls, keeps records accurate and manages production work. Flags gaps or inconsistencies, but escalates anything needing management judgement to the Programme Manager.

title: Decision flow
text:
-
  Title: PMO Support establishes the facts
  Text: Current plan, evidence, cost, risk, owner, deadline and decision record.
-
  Title: Programme Manager integrates the consequences
  Text: Cross-workstream effect, critical path, options, recommendation and correct authority.
-
  Title: Transaction Director decides or directs
  Text: Makes the execution decision within mandate, confirms the recommendation or requests further analysis.
-
  Title: Executive or specialist authority decides where required
  Text: Reserved strategic matters and specialist decisions remain with the named authority.
-
  Title: Programme Manager and PMO Support implement the outcome
  Text: Update the plan, budget view, logs, actions, communications and follow-through.

title: Decision flow warning
text: A senior role does not need to repeat the work of the role below it. It must test whether the information is sufficient, apply the judgement attached to its mandate and make or route the decision promptly.

title: Economics
Governance flow
text:
-
  Name: Workstream sessions
  Text: Workstream Executives and Leads resolve functional matters and flag items for programme escalation. The Central Hub sets standards and receives controlled outputs, rather than running the workstream itself.
-
  Name: Transaction Working Group
  Text: Gives a weekly view of workstream progress and raises important risks, issues and dependencies. The Transaction Director chairs it and the Programme Manager runs it.
-
  Name: Internal PMO
  Text: Resolves programme-management matters and flags items that need Internal SteerCo or joint escalation.
-
  Name: Joint PMO
  Text: Manages joint planning, delivery, dependencies and issue resolution with the counterparty programme.
-
  Name: Internal and Joint SteerCo
  Text: The Steering Committee gives senior direction and decides reserved internal or joint matters. Packs should focus on material exceptions, options, recommendations and decisions needed.

title: Hub functions
text:
-
  Name: Programme management
  Text: Own the integrated programme plan (the single plan that combines all workstreams and key dates), the critical path (the activities that directly determine the delivery date), programme controls, the budget view, governance and reporting to senior leaders.
-
  Name: Mobilisation support
  Text: Set up the programme. Appoint and brief the right leaders, agree ways of working, turn on controlled tools and connect the functional, regional and counterparty teams.
-
  Name: Quality assurance
  Text: Check and challenge plans, reports, evidence, risks and decision papers. This makes sure governance decisions are based on complete, credible and timely information.
-
  Name: Education and standards
  Text: Build good M&A delivery practice through common methods, templates, clear role definitions, lessons learned and standards suited to the deal.

title: Intensity
text:
-
  Period: Due diligence and legal preparation
  Intensity: Targeted
  Level: 1
  Text: Pull out delivery implications, obligations, constraints and information needed for mobilisation.
-
  Period: Mobilisation and planning
  Intensity: Highest
  Level: 4
  Text: Set up the organisation, governance, controls, integrated plan, budget and critical path.
-
  Period: Programme execution
  Intensity: Highest
  Level: 4
  Text: Keep one view of the whole programme, resolve dependencies, speed up decisions and govern performance.
-
  Period: Testing and readiness
  Intensity: High
  Level: 3
  Text: Coordinate evidence standards, defect escalation and overall readiness.
-
  Period: Dress rehearsals, go or no-go and cutover
  Intensity: Highest
  Level: 4
  Text: Govern rehearsals, build the overall recommendation and run control during execution.
-
  Period: Hypercare and handover
  Intensity: High
  Level: 3
  Text: Keep a view of stability, govern remaining actions, confirm business as usual (BAU, when ongoing ownership returns to normal teams) acceptance and capture lessons.

title: Learning outcomes
Lenses
text:
-
  Id: td
  Name: Transaction Director
  Short: Transaction Director
  Text: Owns successful execution of the transaction. Translates the deal into an executable programme, mobilises the leadership team, owns the integrated execution plan and readiness position, leads programme governance, manages the buyer or seller execution relationship and decides transaction-level matters within delegated authority.
-
  Id: pm
  Name: Programme Manager
  Short: Programme Manager
  Text: Drives day-to-day programme management. Runs and maintains the integrated plan, dependencies, governance, reporting and decision pipeline. Holds delivery teams to agreed standards and escalates wider programme decisions to the Transaction Director.
-
  Id: pmo
  Name: PMO Support
  Short: PMO Support
  Text: Maintains the plans, logs, reporting cycle, governance admin, documents and controls that make the programme reliable. Has limited decision authority and escalates decisions to the Programme Manager.

title: Lens warning
text: The Transaction Director sets execution direction and makes transaction-level decisions within mandate. The Programme Manager turns that direction into an integrated programme and recommendation. PMO Support creates a reliable control record. Functional and specialist authorities retain their own decisions, and the Executive Sponsor or formal governance retains reserved decisions.

title: Mandate
Mandate
Mandate
Matching
text:
-
  Need: Define who decides and what each forum produces
  Resource: Governance terms of reference
-
  Need: Understand whether a late workstream output affects transaction timing
  Resource: Integrated programme plan
-
  Need: Record a reserved decision and make sure it is followed through
  Resource: Decision log
-
  Need: Present the transaction-level readiness position
  Resource: Go or no-go scorecard and decision paper
-
  Need: Confirm whether the programme can leave mobilisation
  Resource: Mobilisation completion dashboard and gate pack

title: Mobilisation focus
text:
Td: Confirm the execution mandate with the Executive Sponsor, appoint and empower programme leadership, define the delivery model, secure capacity and approved funding, establish internal and joint governance, and decide whether mobilisation is ready to move into controlled planning.
Pm: Turn the mandate into a workable mobilisation plan, establish programme controls and reporting, connect workstreams and countries, integrate planning outputs, expose gaps and prepare the mobilisation-gate recommendation.
Pmo: Activate the controlled workspace, records, calendars, logs, packs and evidence trail; confirm access and submissions; maintain the mobilisation dashboard; and make gaps visible before the gate.

title: Playbook
text:
-
  Title: Before launching the programme
  Items:
    - Is the deal perimeter and mobilisation mandate clear enough?
    - Are leadership roles accepted, empowered and properly resourced?
    - Is the central, functional and regional delivery split clear?
    - Are the controlled workspace, limits and communication routes active?
    - Do forums have clear decision authority, inputs, outputs and deadlines?
    - Have the programme controls and escalation routes been tested?
-
  Title: Before integrating a workstream update
  Items:
    - Is the detailed plan current and linked to an agreed outcome?
    - Are milestone forecasts backed by evidence and acceptance criteria?
    - Are resource assumptions credible?
    - Are dependencies named, dated and accepted by both sides?
    - Does the status reflect forecast impact, not just completed activity?
    - Are the cost or readiness consequences visible?
-
  Title: Before a governance forum
  Items:
    - Which decisions are needed, and who owns them?
    - What are the options, consequences and recommendation?
    - What is the last responsible decision date?
    - Are the right authorities attending or available?
    - Have urgent issues already been routed, rather than saved for the meeting?
    - Will actions and decisions be recorded and added to the plan?

title: Playbook
text:
-
  Title: Before reporting the programme position
  Items:
    - Does the status reflect the integrated critical path?
    - Have conflicting workstream assumptions been reconciled?
    - Are material dependencies and exceptions clear?
    - Is accepted risk clearly separated from unresolved risk?
    - Are budget, benefits, costs and obligations linked to delivery changes?
    - Can a senior leader understand what changed and what is needed from them?
-
  Title: Before a readiness recommendation
  Items:
    - Are all required functional and local recommendations present?
    - Is the underlying evidence complete, accepted and traceable?
    - Have cross-workstream and counterparty dependencies been tested?
    - Are runbook tasks, checkpoints, fallbacks and authority workable?
    - Are conditions, exceptions and remaining risks clear?
    - Does the recommendation separate Hub judgement from formal governance authority?
-
  Title: Before programme closure
  Items:
    - Are remaining actions owned and governed in business as usual?
    - Is BAU acceptance evidenced across affected functions and countries?
    - Are TSA, Group Interchange and retained obligations still visible?
    - Is programme information kept in the controlled location?
    - Have lessons changed a template, standard or future mobilisation approach?
    - Is closure based on stable outcomes, rather than just the end of the reporting cycle?

title: Principles
text:
- Look at the whole transaction, not just the reports.
- Protect ownership while giving support and challenge.
- Make the critical path and dependencies clear.
- Route decisions to the authority that owns them.
- Escalate before options run out.
- Connect delivery choices to deal costs and value.
- Build readiness recommendations from accepted evidence.
- Turn decisions into controlled actions and lessons kept for next time.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: A Workstream Lead asks to move from weekly to fortnightly reporting because delivery is stable. The workstream supplies an input to another team every week, but no current milestone is late. What is the best Central Hub response?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Keep weekly reporting for every workstream, because one common frequency is needed for consistent programme control.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Check the dependency and the information need, then set a reporting frequency that fits: keep weekly visibility of the hand-off without requiring full reporting every time.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Let the Workstream Lead choose the frequency, because workstream governance sits with the functional owner.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask Internal PMO to approve the change, because reporting frequency is a programme-level governance decision.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: The Hub owns reporting discipline and can tailor it to fit. Consistency does not mean identical effort everywhere, when the needed programme information can be kept through a narrower check.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: Two technically valid control designs have the same programme timing. One is cheaper. The control function prefers the other because it is easier to run. The workstream asks the Programme Manager to choose. What should happen?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Pick the cheaper design, because the programme impact is otherwise the same and the Hub protects deal costs.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Pick the simpler design to run, because the control function has clearly said it prefers it.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Ask the Transaction Director to decide, because the options involve a cost and operating-model trade-off.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Make sure the cost and programme implications are visible, then route the design decision to the accountable functional or control authority.
  Answer: D
  Feedback: The Hub brings the consequences together but does not gain functional design authority just because the options affect programme reporting or cost.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: PMO Support receives three workstream updates using different RAG definitions shortly before the reporting cut-off. The underlying facts are available, but two ratings cannot be reconciled without management judgement. What is the best response?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Apply the agreed definitions to the factual information, flag the judgement gaps and escalate them to the Programme Manager before pulling the report together.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Keep each workstream's submitted rating and explain the inconsistency in the report to senior leaders.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Use the most cautious rating for the two uncertain workstreams, so the programme does not understate risk.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Return all three updates and delay programme reporting until the Workstream Leads provide compliant submissions.
  Answer: A
  Feedback: PMO Support should apply agreed controls to the facts, but should not invent management judgement. Escalating the unresolved ratings keeps both the timeline and the decision authority intact.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: Every workstream reports green, but a joint buyer dependency has no confirmed owner and sits on the critical path. The counterparty believes ownership can be agreed next week, within the remaining spare time (float). How should the programme position be presented?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Green, because the workstream evidence is complete and the dependency stays within available float.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Amber, because any unowned critical-path dependency automatically sets the programme's RAG status.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Based on the forecast effect, the available recovery window, and confidence in securing ownership, with the exception, owner deadline and consequence stated clearly.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Keep it green internally but present it as amber in the joint pack until the counterparty confirms ownership.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Programme status should reflect evidence and forecast, not a fixed rule. The unresolved critical-path ownership must stay visible, even if the current float may protect the date.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: The integrated readiness pack contains complete functional recommendations and one accepted, high remaining risk. Which division of responsibility fits best before the formal go or no-go forum?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: PMO Support decides the programme recommendation from the submitted evidence, and the Programme Manager presents it to formal governance.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: PMO Support confirms that evidence, conditions and approvals are complete; the Programme Manager forms the integrated assessment and options; the Transaction Director tests and sponsors the execution recommendation; authorised governance makes and records the decision.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: The Transaction Director makes the go or no-go decision because that role is accountable for successful execution, and the Executive Sponsor ratifies it after cutover.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: The Programme Manager presents the individual workstream positions and accepted risk without an integrated recommendation, because source evidence remains owned by the functions.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: PMO Support controls completeness and traceability. The Programme Manager integrates the evidence and consequences. The Transaction Director applies execution-level judgement and sponsors the recommendation. Formal governance keeps the go or no-go decision.

title: Relationships
text:
-
  Name: Executive Sponsor and executive governance
  Text: The Executive Sponsor provides strategic direction, empowers the Transaction Director and decides or sponsors matters beyond the Director's mandate. Executive governance, such as SteerCo (the Steering Committee), formally decides reserved changes to scope, budget, completion timing or risk appetite, and makes the formal go or no-go decision (whether the transaction is ready and safe to proceed).
-
  Name: Functional Spokes
  Text: The Functional Spoke is the central specialist team for a function. It owns functional expertise, design choices, policy interpretation, specialist approvals and proof that its area is ready.
-
  Name: Regional Spokes
  Text: The Regional Spoke is the country or regional team responsible for local input and delivery. It owns as much local planning, execution, evidence and decision-making as its experience, capability, capacity and delegated authority (the decisions it is formally authorised to make) allow.
-
  Name: Counterparty programme
  Text: Owns its own internal delivery. It connects to our programme through agreed joint forums, milestones, dependencies, obligations and escalation routes.

title: Relevant resources
text:
-
  Name: Testing governance and defect reporting
  Text: Brings together testing scope, evidence, defects, exit criteria and escalation, without moving test execution to the Hub.
-
  Name: Dress-rehearsal and cutover runbook
  Text: The runbook is the timed plan of cutover activities, owners, dependencies and fallback actions. It sequences transaction-critical actions, checkpoints, fallbacks, communications and authority.
-
  Name: Go or no-go scorecard and decision paper
  Text: Brings together functional and local recommendations, evidence, conditions, exceptions and remaining risk for formal governance.
-
  Name: Cutover checkpoint and command-centre status
  Text: Records progress, issues, decisions, ownership and escalation during live execution.
-
  Name: Hypercare RAID, stability dashboard and daily status
  Text: Gives one view of incidents, trends, remaining actions, service stability and BAU handover.
-
  Name: Lessons-learned record
  Text: Captures useful programme lessons and updates reusable standards and playbooks.

title: Reporting rules
Resource emphasis
text:
Td: Use the mobilisation mandate, organisation and authority records, integrated execution plan, governance terms, executive reporting, budget and business-case tracking, decision papers, joint-governance records, readiness recommendation and cutover control to direct the transaction and make timely decisions.
Pm: Use the integrated plan, programme logs, governance calendar, reporting pack, dependency view, economic forecast and readiness pack to maintain one coherent programme view and prepare recommendations.
Pmo: Use the controlled plans, submission calendar, logs, action records, pack templates, evidence locations, version rules and decision records to keep programme information complete, current and traceable.

title: Role prompts
text:
Td:
  Title: Transaction Director: before deciding or escalating
  Items:
    - Is the recommendation aligned with the deal rationale, contractual intent and approved execution direction?
    - What is the effect on the whole transaction, business continuity, customer outcomes, value and critical path?
    - Is this decision within my delegated authority, or is it reserved for the Executive Sponsor, formal governance or a specialist authority?
    - Have credible options, downside, reversibility, cost and the last responsible decision date been tested?
    - Does the decision protect the buyer or seller relationship without accepting uncontrolled execution risk?
    - What conditions, triggers, communications and follow-through must accompany the decision?
Pm:
  Title: Programme Manager: before making a recommendation
  Items:
    - Are the facts current, reconciled and supported by evidence?
    - Are cross-workstream, country, counterparty and critical-path consequences visible?
    - Do the options show cost, timing, risk, value and delivery effects?
    - Is there a clear recommendation, decision owner and deadline?
    - Can the decision be implemented and controlled immediately after it is made?

title: Role prompts
text:
Pmo:
  Title: PMO Support: before releasing programme information
  Items:
    - Is the source current, controlled and traceable?
    - Are owners, dates, status, evidence and closure conditions complete?
    - Do the plan, logs, budget view and pack tell the same story?
    - Are missing facts and judgement points clearly identified?
    - Has the matter reached the Programme Manager before the reporting or decision deadline?

title: Role table
text:
-
  Activity: Integrated execution plan
  Td: Owns the transaction-level plan and sets execution priorities and tolerances. Resolves transaction trade-offs within mandate.
  Pm: Builds and runs the integrated plan, tests coherence and recommends responses to planning conflicts.
  Pmo: Maintains the controlled plan, validates updates, records baseline changes and identifies inconsistencies.
-
  Activity: RAID and dependencies
  Td: Owns programme-level risk and ensures material barriers are resolved, accepted or escalated.
  Pm: Challenges treatment, prioritises programme attention and determines the escalation route.
  Pmo: Maintains complete records, ageing, owners, dates, evidence and follow-up.
-
  Activity: Governance
  Td: Leads programme governance, chairs key transaction forums and secures executive or specialist decisions.
  Pm: Designs the decision flow, facilitates programme forums and ensures the right authority is engaged.
  Pmo: Manages the calendar, inputs, packs, minutes, decisions, actions and record retention.
-
  Activity: Reporting
  Td: Owns the execution message to the Executive Sponsor and formal governance.
  Pm: Determines the integrated delivery narrative, programme status and decisions required.
  Pmo: Reconciles submissions, applies reporting standards and identifies missing or conflicting information.

title: Role table
text:
-
  Activity: Workstream challenge
  Td: Holds Workstream Executives to account for outcomes and resolves barriers across organisational boundaries.
  Pm: Holds delivery teams to credible plans, evidence, recovery and timely escalation.
  Pmo: Tests compliance with agreed controls and follows up gaps without inventing management judgement.
-
  Activity: Buyer or seller relationship
  Td: Leads the senior execution relationship and resolves or escalates joint trade-offs.
  Pm: Coordinates joint plans, dependencies, forums and decision preparation.
  Pmo: Maintains joint actions, records, packs and agreed information controls.
-
  Activity: Escalation
  Td: Decides within mandate and escalates strategic, reserved or out-of-tolerance matters with a clear recommendation.
  Pm: Frames options, consequences and a recommendation for the Transaction Director or relevant authority.
  Pmo: Makes the issue traceable, prepares the supporting facts and alerts the Programme Manager before deadlines are lost.

title: Role table note
text: PMO Support makes reliable judgement possible. The Programme Manager applies integrated programme judgement. The Transaction Director sets execution direction, decides transaction-level matters within mandate and takes reserved matters to the Executive Sponsor or formal governance.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: s1
  Title: Two plans, one dependency
  Situation: The Technology workstream reports green against its build milestone. Operations reports amber, because its procedure design depends on a Technology interface specification due next week. Technology says its build milestone is unaffected. The integrated plan has five days of spare time (float) before end-to-end testing, but the hand-off acceptance criteria are not explicit.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Keep both workstream ratings, describe the interface as a programme dependency, and use the available float before changing the overall forecast.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Change both workstreams to amber until the specification is accepted, giving one consistent signal for reporting to senior leaders.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Confirm the hand-off criteria and forecast jointly, assign a dated recovery plan, use the float openly, and set programme status based on the resulting effect on testing.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask the Programme Manager to set the specification date and direct both workstreams to align their plans to that decision.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C establishes the missing interface facts before deciding the overall consequence. Option A keeps local reporting but may understate the programme risk. Option B creates visibility but changes both ratings without separating their different outcomes. Option D uses programme authority to replace a delivery commitment that the owning teams must set.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: s2
  Title: A decision before the forum
  Situation: A new regulatory reading may affect client communications due to start on Monday. The relevant Compliance authority can meet today. The next Internal PMO is tomorrow, and SteerCo is next week. The communications workstream needs a decision by close of business to avoid supplier cancellation charges.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Take a provisional Central Hub decision today, let the activity continue, and get Compliance and governance to ratify it at the scheduled forums.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Hold the activity until Internal PMO can consider the programme implications and decide whether to escalate further.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Bring together the relevant Compliance and workstream authorities today, set out the options and consequences, record their decision, and use governance to deal with the resulting programme impacts.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Let reversible supplier preparation continue until SteerCo, because the cost of cancellation currently outweighs the assessed regulatory risk.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C sends the substantive decision to the correct authority without waiting for the governance calendar. Option A keeps momentum but goes beyond the Hub's specialist authority. Option B respects governance but delays a decision route that is already available. Option D weighs programme cost against a regulatory judgement the Hub does not own.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: s3
  Title: Quality assurance without takeover
  Situation: A Workstream Lead submits a detailed (L2) plan with named owners and dates, but the dependencies, acceptance criteria and resource assumptions are incomplete. The integrated baseline workshop is in four days. The Workstream Lead has strong functional knowledge but limited project support.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Ask the Central Hub PMO to rebuild the workstream plan so the integrated baseline can go ahead on time.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Reject the plan against the published standard and require the Workstream Lead to return a compliant version before the workshop.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Set out the specific gaps, agree a short fix plan, offer planning support where needed, and keep the Workstream Lead accountable for the content.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Bring the current plan into the baseline with clear assumptions, and require the missing detail during the first execution reporting cycle.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C combines support, quality assurance and clear ownership. Option A may solve the immediate planning problem but shifts functional planning into the Hub. Option B keeps accountability but may not fix a known capability gap. Option D keeps the timetable but risks approving a baseline that cannot yet be tested.

title: Using programme contingency
text:
Id: td4
Lens: td
Title: Using programme contingency
Situation: The approved programme budget contains R5 million of unallocated contingency within your delegated authority. The Programme Manager recommends using R3 million for an additional data rehearsal and R2 million for extended client-onboarding support. Finance has confirmed that the combined proposal remains within the approved budget and has shown the forecast effect. Both Workstream Executives argue that their original R3 million request should be funded in full. The Executive Sponsor is unavailable, and the preferred supplier slots expire today.
Options:
  -
    Key: A
    Text: Approve the recommended allocation, record the execution and value rationale, set any conditions or review points, and require the integrated plan, forecast and decision record to be updated.
  -
    Key: B
    Text: Divide the contingency equally because both risks are credible, then ask each Workstream Executive to manage the remaining exposure within the revised amount.
  -
    Key: C
    Text: Hold the allocation until the Executive Sponsor can arbitrate, because disagreement between senior workstream owners makes the decision material even though it remains within delegated authority.
  -
    Key: D
    Text: Authorise both suppliers to reserve their full scope, creating a temporary R1 million exposure, and seek approval for the excess before either commitment becomes payable.
Answer: A

title: Using programme contingency
text: Feedback: Option A uses the Transaction Director's delegated authority and bases the decision on the integrated programme recommendation rather than seniority or equal treatment. Option B is balanced but may not protect the transaction's most important outcomes. Option C gives away authority intended to keep execution moving. Option D protects optionality but creates an exposure beyond the approved allocation before that authority is confirmed.

title: A joint milestone under pressure
text:
Id: td5
Lens: td
Title: A joint milestone under pressure
Situation: The counterparty asks to move a joint migration rehearsal five days later. The revised date remains within the contractual window and does not move completion, but it reduces Absa's remediation period from six days to one. The counterparty says keeping the original date would displace a regulatory release and damage the working relationship. The Programme Manager presents two workable options: retain the date and require counterparty weekend cover, or accept the move and fund an Absa recovery team at an estimated R800,000 within the approved budget. Neither option removes all execution risk.
Options:
  -
    Key: A
    Text: Accept the later date because the counterparty has a regulatory conflict and the request remains within the contractual window.
  -
    Key: B
    Text: Retain the original date because preserving Absa's remediation period is the clearest way to protect readiness.
  -
    Key: C
    Text: Engage the counterparty Transaction Director, test the joint consequences and recovery commitments, agree the best transaction outcome within mandate, and record triggers for escalation if the protected conditions fail.
  -
    Key: D
    Text: Send both options to the next Joint SteerCo because any change to a joint milestone should be decided through formal joint governance.
Answer: C

title: A joint milestone under pressure
text: Feedback: Option C treats the matter as a joint execution trade-off and uses the senior relationship to reach a controlled decision while options remain open. Option A gives relationship considerations too much weight without securing recovery. Option B protects Absa's buffer but does not test the transaction-wide cost of the original date. Option D may be required if the trade-off exceeds delegated authority, but the facts do not yet show that formal escalation is necessary.

title: Competing uses of contingency
text:
Id: pm4
Lens: pm
Title: Competing uses of contingency
Situation: The approved programme budget includes R5 million of unallocated contingency under the Transaction Director's delegated authority. Data Migration wants R3 million to add a rehearsal. Client Readiness wants R3 million to extend onboarding support. Both requests reduce real risk and could be trimmed. Delaying the decision by a week loses the preferred supplier slots.
Options:
  -
    Key: A
    Text: Recommend giving R2.5 million to each workstream, so both risks get some funding within the approved budget.
  -
    Key: B
    Text: Ask both Workstream Executives to fund the activities from their own budgets, keeping programme contingency for unforeseen events.
  -
    Key: C
    Text: Compare the effect on critical path, customers, controls and value, build affordable options, and take a recommendation to the Transaction Director to decide within their authority.
  -
    Key: D
    Text: Escalate both requests to SteerCo, because combined demand exceeds the contingency, even though the final allocation can stay within the approved baseline.
Answer: C
Feedback: Option C is the Programme Manager's role: bring together the consequences and prepare a decision-ready recommendation for the Transaction Director. Option A looks balanced but does not test whether equal funding gives the best outcome. Option B may disconnect spend from programme priorities. Option D is right if the decision is beyond delegated authority, but the facts show an affordable option can stay within the baseline.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: pm5
  Lens: pm
  Title: Green sign-offs, incomplete integration
  Situation: All Workstream Executives have submitted green readiness recommendations. During final runbook review, the Programme Manager finds that ownership of one cross-workstream rollback checkpoint is unclear. The event is unlikely but would affect customer access if recovery were needed. The formal go or no-go forum is in 48 hours.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Keep the workstream recommendations, and add the checkpoint as an amber programme condition with an owner to be confirmed before cutover.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Change the affected workstreams to amber and ask their executives to resubmit readiness recommendations before the forum.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Resolve the checkpoint owner and decision route urgently, check whether the runbook can still be delivered, and reflect the remaining risk in the overall recommendation.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Present the green sign-offs unchanged and ask the formal forum to decide whether the cross-workstream gap matters to readiness.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C tests the overall control and gives decision-makers a current recommendation. Option A may end up being right, but ownership and deliverability must be confirmed first. Option B changes workstream positions before checking whose evidence is affected. Option D pushes an unresolved programme issue into the decision forum.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: pmo4
  Lens: pmo
  Title: Conflicting information at cut-off
  Situation: A Workstream Lead submits a green status. The latest controlled plan shows the key milestone moving by two days, but an email from the lead says the delay will be recovered. No recovery activity has yet been added to the plan. The report to senior leaders is due in 90 minutes, and the Programme Manager will be free in 30 minutes.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Use the Workstream Lead's green rating, add a note that recovery planning is in progress, and ask for the plan to be updated after it is circulated.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Keep the last approved status, because the revised plan and recovery position have not yet gone through the reporting-control process.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Reconcile the actual movement, prepare the exception and its possible impact, and ask the Programme Manager to decide the overall rating before the pack is finalised.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Apply amber, because the controlled plan currently shows a delay, issue the pack on time, and let the Programme Manager amend the rating at governance.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C keeps the facts, the deadline and the management decision separate and correct. Option A relies on an unsupported forecast. Option B keeps the previous status but hides newer, important information. Option D may be a reasonable stand-in, but PMO Support should not finalise management judgement when the Programme Manager is available before the pack goes out.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Id: pmo5
  Lens: pmo
  Title: A verbal decision
  Situation: During an urgent call, the Transaction Director indicates support for extending a supplier contract. The Programme Manager asks PMO Support to update the plan and tell Procurement. The call did not confirm the approved amount, any conditions, or whether the Transaction Director was acting within their delegated budget. Procurement needs confirmation today to keep the current commercial terms.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Record the extension as approved on the Programme Manager's instruction, update the baseline, and ask Procurement to confirm the final value later.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Draft the decision record with the missing amount, conditions and authority, get confirmation through the Programme Manager today, and update the controls only once the decision is complete.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Record the decision as provisional, let Procurement reserve the terms, and get formal confirmation at the next Internal PMO.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Route the extension to the next SteerCo, because the call did not produce a complete, auditable decision record.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Option B makes the decision complete and traceable without delaying it unnecessarily. Option A treats an incomplete verbal indication as approval. Option C keeps momentum but could create a commitment before authority and conditions are clear. Option D protects governance but escalates beyond the same-day decision route that is already available.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Confirm the mobilisation mandate
  Good: The core team understands the deal direction, type, perimeter (what is and is not included in the deal), objectives, target dates, any known legal or information limits, completion assumptions and the first mobilisation priorities.
  Evidence: Mobilisation mandate, controlling assumptions, initial information requests, limits, and named transaction leadership.
-
  Title: Set up programme leadership
  Good: The Executive Sponsor appoints and empowers the Transaction Director. The Transaction Director and Sponsor confirm the Programme Manager and accountable Workstream Executives, and the Director mobilises the Central Hub and in-country coordination. Workstream Leads are appointed with the right authority, capacity and deputies. Gaps have owners and dates to close them.
  Evidence: Programme organisation chart, role acceptance, decision mandates, capacity assessment, deputies and any unresolved appointments.
-
  Title: Define the delivery model
  Good: The required workstreams match the actual deal perimeter. The split between Central Hub, functional spokes and regional spokes is clear, and fits each country's experience, capability, capacity and delegated authority.
  Evidence: Workstream map, accountability matrix, initial delivery split, exceptions and reasons.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Set up the controlled environment
  Good: The core team has an approved workspace, controlled document locations and permitted communication channels. Confidentiality, insider, information-sharing and counterparty limits are understood.
  Evidence: Access records, NDA or legal-clearance records, workspace structure, version rules and any unresolved access issues.
-
  Title: Set up governance
  Good: Internal and joint forums have a clear purpose, attendees, authority, inputs, outputs and frequency. Submission deadlines, pre-reads, pack ownership, minutes, actions and record-keeping are assigned.
  Evidence: Governance terms of reference, calendar, reporting timetable, attendees and forum responsibilities.
-
  Title: Set up programme controls
  Good: RAID, decision, action, dependency and change controls use agreed fields, status definitions, RAG criteria (red, amber or green status), ageing rules, escalation thresholds and closure evidence. A sample issue and decision have been run through governance as a test.
  Evidence: Controlled logs, definitions, routing rules, test results and named control owners.
-
  Title: Connect the interfaces
  Good: Functional, regional and permitted counterparty contacts know who they work with, how to request information, where decisions are recorded, and how to escalate unanswered dependencies.
  Evidence: Interface directory, deputies, approved channels, permitted topics, joint milestones and escalation contacts.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Close the mobilisation gate
  Good: The Day 10 gate shows a clear view of appointments, capacity, tools, governance, controls, onboarding and open exceptions. Governance decides to proceed, proceed with conditions, or hold, with conditions and owners recorded.
  Evidence: Mobilisation completion dashboard, gate pack, decision record, open conditions and agreed next steps.

title: Success measures
text:
-
  - Mobilisation readiness
  - accountable leaders, capacity, tools, governance and interfaces are up and running.
-
  - Integrated plan quality
  - milestones, dependencies, critical path, assumptions and owners fit together.
-
  - Decision speed
  - issues reach the correct authority before options run out.
-
  - Control discipline
  - logs, reports, actions and evidence are current, traceable and controlled.
-
  - Dependency resolution
  - hand-offs and knock-on effects between workstreams are actively managed.
-
  - Reporting integrity
  - reports to senior leaders show the forecast, the evidence and material exceptions.
-
  - Readiness integration
  - workstream evidence adds up to a credible transaction-level recommendation.
-
  - Value protection
  - budget, benefits, costs, obligations and financial risks stay visible through delivery.

title: Template notice
text: The templates named in this module are not stored in the Capability Hub. Get the current approved versions from the programme team or the controlled programme workspace. Do not create an uncontrolled alternative where an approved template already exists.

title: Brief gaps

title: The final executive review before cutover
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
The final executive review before cutover
text:
Title: The final executive review before cutover
Intro: Cutover is days away. At the final executive review you learn that:
Facts:
  - the integrated plan remains on date, and customer migration evidence meets the agreed threshold;
  - one customer segment has a higher complaint forecast than assumed in the value case;
  - a control owner will accept the remaining risk only if enhanced monitoring is funded for eight weeks; and
  - the Transaction Director recommends proceeding with conditions, while one executive asks you to delay until every open item is closed.
Close: Answer as the Executive Sponsor.
Improved: You are now applying the Sponsor role through a clear mandate, protected delegation, enterprise alignment and evidence-based decisions.
Review: You have completed the pathway. Review the highlighted module before sponsoring a live transaction.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: evidence
  Question: What evidence should drive your challenge in the review?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Each workstream's detailed cutover task list, to confirm nothing has been missed.
      Feedback: Pulls you into task-level detail rather than the outcome and trade-off.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: The supported forecast for the affected segment, the value effect, the conditions and the fallback if they fail.
      Feedback: Recommended. It tests the outcome and trade-off, then enables a clear decision.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Confirmation that every workstream rating is green before the forum.
      Feedback: Ratings do not show the changed customer outlook or the value effect.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: A full list of every open item, so the delay request can be weighed properly.
      Feedback: Volume of open items is not the same as material risk.
  Answer: b
  Reasoning: Good executive challenge tests the outcome and trade-off, then enables a clear decision.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: resources
  Question: Do the monitoring cost and the changed customer outlook need a business-case decision?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: No. The monitoring is small and can be absorbed within the programme budget.
      Feedback: Treats a value-case change as a budget question only.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: No. The Transaction Director can fund it within delegated limits and report it later.
      Feedback: Funding may sit with the Director, but the value-case change needs your view.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Yes, but only once cutover is complete and the complaint forecast is proven.
      Feedback: Defers the decision until the useful options have gone.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Yes. Confirm who can approve the funding, and record the value-case change and its owner now.
      Feedback: Recommended. It makes the cost and value effect visible and owned before commitment.
  Answer: d
  Reasoning: Staying within total budget is not enough. The Sponsor must understand value, timing and the loss of future flexibility.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: delegation
  Question: How should the control owner's risk acceptance and your decision interact?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: The control owner accepts the risk within their authority; you test it and sponsor a recommendation, and the forum decides.
      Feedback: Recommended. Each level adds the judgement attached to its mandate.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Your acceptance replaces the control owner's, since you own the transaction outcome.
      Feedback: Material consequences do not transfer specialist authority.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: The control owner's acceptance settles readiness, so no Sponsor view is needed.
      Feedback: Risk acceptance is not the go or no-go decision.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Ask the Transaction Director to accept the risk, since it is an execution matter.
      Feedback: Formal risk acceptance sits with the named authority.
  Answer: a
  Reasoning: Keep specialist decisions with the specialist authority while the Sponsor manages the transaction consequences.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: mandate
  Question: What readiness recommendation should you sponsor to the formal forum?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Delay until every open item is closed, as the executive asked.
      Feedback: Seeks complete certainty rather than proportionate readiness.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Proceed, as the plan is on date and migration evidence meets the threshold.
      Feedback: Ignores the changed customer outlook and the unfunded condition.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Proceed with conditions: funded monitoring, a complaint trigger, owners and a stop authority, recorded before cutover.
      Feedback: Recommended. A clear view with executable, owned conditions.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Present both views to the forum without a recommendation.
      Feedback: Passes the choice upward instead of sponsoring a clear view.
  Answer: c
  Reasoning: Stay accountable for direction and material choices, and sponsor a clear view rather than pass the choice upward.

title: A decision that cannot wait for the next committee
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
A decision that cannot wait for the next committee
text:
Title: A decision that cannot wait for the next committee
Intro: You are the Executive Sponsor. This week you learn that:
Facts:
  - a critical specialist is being withheld by their business area;
  - the Transaction Director proposes temporary external support that increases cost but protects the current date;
  - a functional executive argues that you should overrule a delegated design decision; and
  - the programme remains within tolerance, but the value case will weaken if a customer milestone moves by more than two weeks.
Close: Answer as the Executive Sponsor. Several responses are defensible; choose the strongest.
Message: Several choices can look reasonable from the Sponsor's seat. The modules show how mandate, delegation, enterprise alignment and evidence decide the strongest response.

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: mandate
  Question: Which of these matters should you direct, delegate or decide yourself?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Decide all three matters yourself this week, since each could affect the value case.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Leave all three with the Transaction Director, since the programme is within tolerance.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Resolve the withheld specialist yourself, leave the design with its owner and support the Director on the support proposal.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Refer all three to the next executive forum so the full committee can consider them together.
  Answer: c
-
  Capability: delegation
  Question: How do you respond to the request to overrule the delegated design decision?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Check it is within the delegated mandate and aligned to objectives, then support it unless new evidence changes the position.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Ask the executive and the Transaction Director to agree a compromise before execution continues.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Reopen the decision at the next forum, since senior functional disagreement signals a need for wider sponsorship.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Overrule it if the executive's option realises the approved benefits sooner and remains executable.
  Answer: a

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: resources
  Question: How should the specialist and external-support trade-off be resolved?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Approve the external support now, since it protects the date and sits inside tolerance.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Require the business area to release the specialist, whatever the effect on its own obligations.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Ask for a short option view of both obligations, cost and date effects, then use your authority to secure a commitment.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Ask the Transaction Director to absorb the gap, since workstream capacity is an execution matter.
  Answer: c
-
  Capability: evidence
  Question: What evidence do you need before sponsoring a material choice here?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: The supported forecast, the value effect of a two-week slip, the options' costs and the final useful decision date.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: A detailed task-level plan from each workstream showing how the specialist's work is allocated.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Confirmation from every affected executive that they agree with the recommended option.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: A fixed price for the external support and a revised plan approved by the Programme Manager.
  Answer: a

title: Paper options
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: The effect on the business case and benefit timing across the estimate range
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Staying inside total budget is not enough; you must see the value effect.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Genuine alternatives, such as a capped discovery phase before full commitment
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Options let you buy information while limiting exposure.
-
  Id: c
  Text: The final useful decision date and what becomes impossible after it
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Timing tells you whether you can wait for more certainty.
-
  Id: d
  Text: A task-level breakdown of the supplier's discovery activities
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Operational detail; it does not change the executive choice.
-
  Id: e
  Text: Agreement from every Workstream Executive that the supplier is the best option
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Consensus is not evidence and would slow the decision.
-
  Id: f
  Text: A fixed supplier price before any decision is taken
  Correct: false
  Feedback: The supplier cannot fix a price until discovery; demanding one creates avoidable delay.

title: Paper situation
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text: A supplier revises its estimate for a required separation activity from R18 million to between R23 million and R26 million. R8 million of central contingency remains. The paper asks you to approve the appointment but gives no value effect, no alternatives and no final useful decision date.

title: Playbook prompts
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
- Intended outcome: what must remain true for this transaction to succeed?
- Supported forecast: what outcome is now forecast, and what accepted evidence supports it?
- Value effect: what does this choice do to cost, benefits, customers, employees and timing?
- Risk owner: which material risk remains, and who has the authority to accept it?
- Decision required: what must be decided, by whom, and is it within my authority?
- Final useful date: what becomes harder or impossible if the decision waits?

title: Readiness options
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: Sponsor a proceed recommendation, since the risk owner has accepted the exposure and a checkpoint adds control.
  Feedback: May become the final view, but does not show the remaining exposure and checkpoint are executable.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Sponsor a hold until recovery beyond four hours has been demonstrated.
  Feedback: May become appropriate, but the facts do not yet show holding is the only proportionate response.
-
  Id: c
  Text: Test the failure consequence, monitoring, trigger, authority and fallback, then present a recommendation with conditions to the forum.
  Feedback: Recommended. It applies Sponsor judgement and preserves the formal forum's decision authority.
-
  Id: d
  Text: Present the Director's recommendation and the risk acceptance without a Sponsor view.
  Feedback: Passes information upward without the integrated Sponsor recommendation the forum expects.

title: Readiness situation
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text: All functional leaders recommend proceeding to Business Day 1. One high-severity operational risk remains: a tested manual process can maintain customer service for four hours if an automated hand-off fails, but recovery beyond four hours has not been demonstrated. The risk owner has accepted the exposure, and the Transaction Director recommends proceeding with a two-hour executive checkpoint. The formal forum is tomorrow.

title: Resource options
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: Confirm the transaction's priority and require Technology to retain both specialists until the gate.
  Feedback: Protects the transaction but assumes the other obligation can absorb the loss.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Ask for a time-bound enterprise option showing both obligations, capability, cost and deadlines, then secure the chosen commitment.
  Feedback: Recommended. It treats the conflict as an enterprise decision and creates the information to secure a workable commitment.
-
  Id: c
  Text: Accept the reassignment, as regulatory work comes first, and ask the Director to replan the gate.
  Feedback: Gives one valid priority automatic precedence without integrating the consequences.
-
  Id: d
  Text: Split each specialist's time equally between the programmes and require weekly reporting.
  Feedback: Looks balanced but may leave both programmes without enough focused capacity.

title: Resource situation
breadcrumb: Accountable Executive (Executive Sponsor) pathway — modules and exercises
text: Six weeks before a major readiness gate, the Technology Executive advises that two specialists committed to the transaction are needed for a regulatory remediation programme. Both initiatives have fixed external deadlines. The Transaction Director proposes moving one specialist and funding a contractor, but Technology believes the contractor will require too much supervision.

  Why: Changes beyond the Sponsor's mandate go to the correct formal forum, with the Sponsor's recommendation.
-
  Text: Run the governance cadence and cross-workstream issue resolution
  Answer: delegate
  Why: Governance operation and coordination are delegated to the Transaction Director.
-
  Text: Determine a regulatory interpretation that threatens a milestone
  Answer: escalate
  Why: The named specialist authority decides; the Sponsor accelerates the route and manages the consequences.

title: Authority guidance
text:
Sponsor: Sponsor intervention is likely required.
Specialist: Route the substantive decision to that authority while the Sponsor manages the transaction consequences.

title: Authority test
text:
- Does this change the approved strategic intent, business case or intended end-state?
- Does it change scope, budget, completion timing or risk beyond an agreed tolerance?
- Is enterprise authority needed to resolve a resource or leadership conflict?
- Does a specialist, country, regulatory, counterparty or Board authority own the substantive decision?
- Can the Transaction Director decide it within delegated execution authority?

title: Challenge questions
text:
- What outcome is now forecast, not merely planned?
- What accepted evidence supports that view?
- Which assumption would most change the recommendation?
- What are the consequences for customers, employees, controls, value and timing?
- Which option is recommended, and why is it better for the whole transaction?
- What becomes impossible if the decision waits?
- Who has authority, and is that person available?
- What conditions or triggers would change the decision?

title: Contributions
text:
-
  Title: Set direction
  Text: Define the strategic intent, success criteria, intended end-state and boundaries within which execution decisions can be made.
-
  Title: Empower leadership
  Text: Appoint the Transaction Director, agree key Workstream Executives and give leaders clear authority, access and escalation routes.
-
  Title: Secure commitment
  Text: Ensure functions and countries prioritise the transaction and release the people, funding and decisions required to deliver it.
-
  Title: Make material decisions
  Text: Decide within personal authority and sponsor decisions that require a formal senior forum, Board or other named authority.
-
  Title: Protect value and risk
  Text: Keep execution aligned to the business case, intended operating model, customer and employee outcomes, risk appetite and material transaction obligations.
-
  Title: Lead at key moments
  Text: Provide visible leadership during mobilisation, major decisions, readiness, go or no-go, cutover, stabilisation and closure.

title: Core resources
text:
-
  Name: Transaction mandate and deal-rationale summary
  Purpose: States the transaction intent, perimeter, target outcome, key dates, obligations and constraints.
  Use: Set direction and test whether execution remains aligned.
  Ask: What must remain true? Which assumptions are still open? What has changed since approval?
-
  Name: Approved business case and budget baseline
  Purpose: Records expected value, cost, benefits, timing, risks and approved funding.
  Use: Test value protection and decide or sponsor material changes.
  Ask: What moved, why, by how much and who owns recovery?
-
  Name: Target Operating Model or intended end-state
  Purpose: Describes how the business, services, controls, systems or organisation should operate after the transaction.
  Use: Prevent short-term execution choices from undermining the intended outcome.
  Ask: Is the decision a temporary transition or a permanent change? Who accepts the consequence?
-
  Name: Sponsor and Transaction Director authority statement
  Purpose: Records decision rights, delegated limits, reserved matters and escalation triggers.
  Use: Protect speed and prevent duplicated or unclear authority.
  Ask: Who owns this decision? Is the limit clear? Has new information changed the route?
-
  Name: Programme organisation, accountability matrix and capacity view
  Purpose: Records accountable leaders, role boundaries, deputies and committed capacity.
  Use: Resolve leadership and enterprise resource constraints.
  Ask: Are the right people empowered and available? Where is commitment weaker than the plan assumes?

title: Core resources
text:
-
  Name: Governance terms, calendar and decision map
  Purpose: Defines forum authority, attendees, inputs, outputs and decision routes.
  Use: Ensure material decisions reach the correct authority in time.
  Ask: Is this forum deciding or merely discussing? Can an urgent route be used sooner?
-
  Name: Integrated executive status and decision pack
  Purpose: Provides the current transaction forecast, exceptions, economics, readiness and decisions required.
  Use: Direct executive challenge and action.
  Ask: What changed? What is the forecast? Which decision cannot wait?
-
  Name: Material risk and readiness view
  Purpose: Connects material risks, mitigations, evidence, conditions and formal acceptance.
  Use: Test readiness and ensure risk reaches the correct authority.
  Ask: What remains after mitigation? Who can accept it? What happens if the assumption fails?
-
  Name: Change or decision paper
  Purpose: Sets out facts, options, cost, timing, risk, value, recommendation, authority and decision deadline.
  Use: Make or sponsor a traceable material decision.
  Ask: Are the options genuinely different? What is reversible? What becomes impossible after the deadline?
-
  Name: Go or no-go paper and decision record
  Purpose: Integrates readiness, conditions, exceptions, residual risk and the recommendation for a major event.
  Use: Sponsor an evidence-based formal decision.
  Ask: Are conditions executable? Who holds stop authority? Is the decision recorded at the correct level?

title: Core resources
text:
-
  Name: Executive stakeholder and communication plan
  Purpose: Coordinates senior alignment, decision preparation and controlled messages.
  Use: Maintain organisational commitment and prevent conflicting executive direction.
  Ask: Who could block or materially influence the outcome? What do they need to understand or decide?

title: Def
text:
Business case: The approved explanation of why the transaction should proceed, including expected value, cost, benefits and risks.
Critical path: The sequence of activities that determines the earliest possible completion date.
Delegated authority: A decision the Sponsor has formally allowed another role to make within stated limits.
Reserved decision: A decision that must remain with a named senior person or formal forum because of its material impact.
Executive governance: The formal senior forum that decides reserved matters. This may be an Executive Committee, Steering Committee or Board-level forum, depending on the transaction.
Risk appetite: The amount and type of risk the organisation is prepared to accept.
Residual risk: The risk that remains after planned controls or mitigations are applied.
Readiness evidence: Accepted proof that a required outcome, control or activity is complete and can operate as intended.
Go or no go: The formal decision to proceed with, conditionally proceed with, or stop a major transaction event.
Legal Day 1: The date legal ownership or control changes.
Business Day 1: The first day the agreed operating arrangements must work after the transaction event.
Stabilisation: The controlled period after launch or cutover when issues are resolved and operations are proven stable.
Condition: An action or restriction attached to a decision that must be met or monitored.
Tolerance: The agreed limit within which a role may act without seeking further approval.

title: Def
text:
Transition service: A temporary service supplied by one party to the other after the transaction event.
Handover: Formal transfer of continuing ownership from the programme into normal business teams.

title: Go flow
text:
- Workstreams and countries provide recommendations and accepted evidence.
- The Programme Manager integrates dependencies, conditions and programme consequences.
- The Transaction Director applies execution judgement and forms the integrated recommendation.
- The Executive Sponsor tests strategic alignment, business continuity, value and material risk.
- The authorised formal forum makes and records the go or no-go decision.

  Level: 4

-
