title: Resource notice
text: Resource notice: The templates named in this module are not stored in the Capability Hub. Get the current approved versions from the Central PMO, programme team or controlled programme workspace.

title: Roles
text:
-
  Id: pm
  Name: Workstream Project Manager
  Text: Maintains the plan and delivery controls. Coordinates updates, challenges gaps and prepares reliable workstream reporting.
-
  Id: lead
  Name: Workstream Lead
  Text: Owns the workstream outcome, scope, priorities and functional decisions. The Project Manager provides the facts needed for those decisions.
-
  Id: members
  Name: Workstream Team Members
  Text: Complete assigned activities, provide specialist input and produce evidence. The Project Manager coordinates their plan updates and follows up actions.
-
  Id: exec
  Name: Workstream Executive
  Text: Makes major workstream choices, removes senior blockers and approves matters that need executive authority.
-
  Id: pmo
  Name: Central PMO
  Text: Maintains the single programme view across all workstreams. The Workstream Project Manager provides controlled workstream information and receives programme dates, standards and decisions.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: A changed priority
  Situation: The Workstream Lead asks the team to pause a lower-priority activity for one week. The change releases a specialist for a critical milestone. It does not change the workstream scope or any programme date. The request is made during a call and is not yet recorded.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Update the plan immediately because the Workstream Lead owns workstream priorities, then record the reason at the next meeting.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Confirm the decision and affected owners with the Workstream Lead, record it and update the plan and actions.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Ask the Workstream Executive to approve the change because it moves an activity from the current baseline.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Keep the plan unchanged until the Central PMO confirms that the integrated programme is unaffected.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Option B respects the Workstream Lead's authority and keeps the control record complete. Option A updates the plan before the decision is traceable. Option C raises a change that remains within the Lead's stated authority. Option D asks the Central PMO to approve a workstream priority it does not own.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: Ninety per cent complete
  Situation: An activity owner reports that a deliverable is 90% complete. The remaining work is approval from a control owner. No meeting is booked, and the planned completion date is three days away. The control owner normally needs five days to review.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Keep the date because most of the production work is complete and request an urgent review from the control owner.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Change the status to amber, move the completion date by two days and ask the Workstream Lead to accept the delay.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Confirm the approval requirement and review time, secure a response plan and report the forecast based on whether approval can still be achieved.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Record production as complete and track control approval as a separate action after the planned completion date.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C tests the remaining work against the actual acceptance condition. Option A relies on percentage complete rather than forecast. Option B may prove correct but changes status and date before testing recovery. Option D separates required approval from the definition of completion.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: A cross-workstream dependency
  Situation: Your workstream needs an approved data file from another workstream before testing. Its Project Manager provides a working date but cannot confirm the acceptance standard. The integrated programme plan still shows the earlier date used during mobilisation.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Use the working date in your detailed plan and ask the Central PMO to update the integrated programme plan.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Retain the approved programme date until the supplying Workstream Lead confirms a formal change.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Agree the required file, acceptance conditions and forecast with the supplying team, then show any remaining programme effect through both Workstream Leads and the Central PMO.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Add schedule contingency to your testing activity so the workstream can absorb either delivery date.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C resolves both the date and what must be delivered before updating the programme view. Option A may spread an unconfirmed assumption. Option B protects the baseline but ignores newer information. Option D may help recovery but does not resolve the dependency or its ownership.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: Pressure to keep green
  Situation: The Workstream Lead believes a missing evidence pack will arrive before the reporting deadline and wants to retain green status. The evidence owner has not committed to a date. Current activities are otherwise on plan.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Retain green because the Workstream Lead owns status and expects recovery before the deadline.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Set amber because the evidence date is not confirmed and allow the Workstream Lead to override the rating.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Show the evidence gap, forecast effect and required decision date, then ask the Workstream Lead to confirm the status against the agreed definitions.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Keep green in the workstream report but flag the uncertainty separately to the Central PMO.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C gives the Workstream Lead a clear evidence-based decision. Option A records optimism without a committed recovery. Option B makes the Project Manager the status decision-maker. Option D creates two different versions of the workstream position.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: A supplier change
  Situation: A supplier identifies an additional requirement during delivery. It may add R600,000 and one week. The Workstream Lead agrees the requirement is useful, but it is not in the approved scope. The supplier needs direction within two days.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Add the requirement to the plan because the Workstream Lead supports it, then raise a budget request for the extra cost.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Keep it outside the plan until cost and timing are fixed, avoiding an uncertain change request.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Record the proposed change, show its cost, timing, value and dependency effects, and prepare it for the agreed approval route.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask the supplier to begin the work at risk so the programme does not lose the available week.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C creates a decision-ready change request without treating support as approval. Option A changes the baseline too early. Option B protects control but may waste the two-day decision window. Option D creates cost and scope exposure before authority is confirmed.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Understand the workstream outcome
  Confirm: Read the workstream charter and confirm the scope, required outcomes, main constraints and important transaction dates.
  Good: You can explain what the workstream must deliver and which decisions remain open.
-
  Title: Agree how you will work with the Workstream Lead
  Confirm: Agree how often you will review the plan, who approves status, which decisions need the Lead and how urgent issues will be raised.
  Good: Planning support and functional accountability are clearly separated.
-
  Title: Build the detailed plan
  Confirm: Create the detailed workstream plan, also called the L2 plan. Include activities, owners, dates, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
  Good: Each owner understands the task, due date and proof required for completion.
-
  Title: Connect to the programme plan
  Confirm: Confirm the programme milestones, critical path and required hand-offs. The critical path is the work that directly determines the overall delivery date.
  Good: The workstream plan supports the programme dates, and every important interface has an owner.
-
  Title: Establish the control logs
  Confirm: Set up the agreed records for actions, decisions, and RAID. RAID means risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies.
  Good: Each item has a clear description, owner, date, response and route for raising it if needed.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Set the reporting and meeting rhythm
  Confirm: Confirm meeting dates, update deadlines, report format, status definitions, pack ownership, minutes and action follow-up.
  Good: The team knows when information is due and the Workstream Lead has time to review it before programme reporting.
-
  Title: Set up evidence and change control
  Confirm: Agree where evidence is stored and how scope, date, cost or acceptance changes will be assessed and approved.
  Good: The team can trace the approved plan, each change and the evidence behind reported completion.

title: Weekly cycle
text:
-
  Title: Gather updates
  Text: Collect progress, evidence, new dates, actions, decisions and changes from each owner.
-
  Title: Test the forecast
  Text: Check whether the remaining work, capacity and dependencies still support the planned dates.
-
  Title: Update the controls
  Text: Update the detailed plan, actions, decisions, RAID and evidence links. Keep one controlled version.
-
  Title: Challenge gaps
  Text: Ask for evidence, clearer owners, realistic recovery actions and decisions where information is weak.
-
  Title: Prepare the workstream meeting
  Text: Show what changed, which outcomes are at risk and what the Workstream Lead or Executive must decide.
-
  Title: Publish and follow through
  Text: Issue the agreed status and actions. Update the records after decisions and follow up before the next meeting.

title: The evening before cutover rehearsal

text:
Title: The evening before cutover rehearsal
Intro: Rehearsal starts tomorrow morning. You notice that:
Facts:
  - your task is marked complete, but its evidence link points to an older version of the output;
  - a dependent team has moved its delivery time by 30 minutes and says the runbook need not be updated;
  - a defect appeared once in your last test and cannot be reproduced; and
  - a senior colleague asks for a customer-data extract through an unapproved channel so they can investigate quickly.
Close: You have a couple of hours before the rehearsal briefing.
Improved: You are now applying the Team Member role through clear results, controlled information, usable evidence and early escalation.
Review: You have completed the pathway. Review the highlighted module before your next live task.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: evidence
  Question: What must be confirmed before your task's completion stands?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Nothing further. The task was accepted, and the older link can be fixed after the rehearsal.
      Feedback: Acceptance of the wrong version does not prove the current output is ready.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: That the current version was checked and accepted, and the evidence link points to it. If not, tell the owner it is not yet complete.
      Feedback: Recommended. Completion depends on accepted proof of the right version.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Replace the link with the current version yourself so the record is correct before the rehearsal.
      Feedback: Fixes the link but claims acceptance of a version nobody has checked.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Mark the task incomplete in the plan and redo the work so the output and evidence match.
      Feedback: Too much. The output may be fine; what is missing is confirmed acceptance of it.
  Answer: b
  Reasoning: Work is complete when the agreed result is accepted and the proof can be found for the version in use.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: result
  Question: How should you handle the 30-minute timing change?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Adjust your own start time by 30 minutes so your task still lines up with their delivery.
      Feedback: Changes the runbook informally. Other tasks and checkpoints may depend on the original timing.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Accept their view, because 30 minutes is within normal tolerance for a rehearsal.
      Feedback: Deciding the runbook does not need updating is not your call, or theirs alone.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Raise the change with the runbook owner so it can be assessed and approved, and follow the current runbook until then.
      Feedback: Recommended. It keeps the change controlled and visible to everyone it affects.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Ask the dependent team to deliver at the original time to protect the approved runbook.
      Feedback: Protects your task, but the timing may have changed for a good reason that others need to know.
  Answer: c
  Reasoning: Timing and sequence change only through the approved runbook and its owner, not through an informal message.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: raise
  Question: How should the one-off defect be recorded and raised?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Log it with the evidence you have, the conditions when it appeared and the likely effect, and flag it before the briefing.
      Feedback: Recommended. An unreproduced defect is still a fact others need to weigh.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Keep testing tonight and log it only if it happens again, to avoid a false alarm before the rehearsal.
      Feedback: May waste the time others need to respond, and hides a real result.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Mention it verbally at the briefing so the team is aware, without adding it to the defect log.
      Feedback: Visible, but not recorded, owned or traceable.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Record it as closed, because it could not be reproduced and the test later passed.
      Feedback: Closing it without a cause or fix removes the evidence of a real failure.
  Answer: a
  Reasoning: Record the actual result, not the expected one. Raise the fact and its effect while there is still time to respond.

title: Capstone decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: information
  Question: How should you respond to the senior colleague's data request?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Send it, since they are senior and the investigation is urgent, and note the request in your records.
      Feedback: Seniority does not make an unapproved channel acceptable.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Send a smaller extract with only the fields they need, to lower the risk.
      Feedback: Still moves customer data through an unapproved route.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Offer to share it through the approved system if they are authorised, and raise the access need with your Lead.
      Feedback: Recommended. It helps the investigation without creating a data risk.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Refuse and wait until after the rehearsal to discuss the investigation.
      Feedback: Protects the data, but leaves a real investigation without a route forward.
  Answer: c
  Reasoning: Use only approved channels and authorised people. Raise access problems instead of creating a workaround.

title: Completion compare
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
Weak: I finished the reconciliation.
Strong: Reconciliation v1.3 is complete. It matches the approved account mapping, the Finance Control Owner checked it on 12 August, and the signed check and results are stored in the controlled workspace, folder 04.

title: Cutover options
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: Start at 00:30, because the previous owner has confirmed completion and the change adds contingency.
  Feedback: Relies on one person's message. The checkpoint has not released your task.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Prepare to start, but confirm the change through the authorised checkpoint before you execute the task.
  Feedback: Recommended. It keeps control while letting the command centre use the time gained.
-
  Id: c
  Text: Wait until 01:00, because an approved runbook should never change during live execution.
  Feedback: Protects the plan but may ignore a valid, controlled change.
-
  Id: d
  Text: Ask the technical lead to record the change in the team chat, then start once that record exists.
  Feedback: Creates a record but not the authority to change the runbook.

title: Cutover situation
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text: The approved runbook says your task starts at 01:00 after a checkpoint. At 00:25, a technical lead messages that the previous activity finished early and asks you to start at 00:30. The command centre has not issued a revised instruction.

title: A task that looks complete
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
Title: A task that looks complete
Intro: You have been asked to update a customer process before testing starts. Then:
Facts:
  - two versions of the requirement are circulating, and a colleague says to use the newer one, although its approval is unclear;
  - your change works in one test but fails in another;
  - the deadline is tomorrow; and
  - someone outside the approved team asks for the test extract to help investigate.
Close: You need to decide what to do next.
Message: Several choices can look reasonable under deadline pressure. The modules show how the required result, approved access, evidence and early escalation decide the best response.

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: result
  Question: How should you confirm which requirement to build to?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Use the newer version, as it is more likely to reflect the latest position, and note that choice in your update.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Ask the task owner which version is approved and confirm the acceptance conditions before you continue.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Build to the older version, because it is the last one you know was formally shared with the team.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Build to both versions so the output can be switched quickly once someone confirms the approved one.
  Answer: b
-
  Capability: information
  Question: How should you handle the request for the test extract?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Share a masked version of the extract, since removing names lowers the risk while still helping the investigation.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: Share the extract through the approved system, because they are trying to help fix a real problem.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: Decline for now and ask your Workstream Lead or Project Manager whether the person can be authorised.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Send it once your manager confirms by email that the request is reasonable and time-critical.
  Answer: c

title: Diagnostic decisions
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Capability: evidence
  Question: When could you report the change as complete?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: When the change passes at least one test and the remaining test is logged as a follow-up action.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: When you are satisfied the change is built and the Project Manager has marked it done in the plan.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: When it meets the approved requirement, the agreed checks pass, and the evidence is stored and accepted.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: When the change is deployed to the test environment and the deadline has been met.
  Answer: c
-
  Capability: raise
  Question: When and how should you raise the failing test?
  Options:
    -
      Id: a
      Text: Now, stating what failed, the likely effect, what you have tried and the help needed before the deadline.
    -
      Id: b
      Text: After another day of investigation, so you can report the cause as well as the symptom.
    -
      Id: c
      Text: At the next status meeting, where the owner can weigh it against other delivery priorities.
    -
      Id: d
      Text: Only if it fails again, since one failure may be caused by the test environment rather than your change.
  Answer: a

title: Evidence options
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: The test record showing the actual result against the expected result, with a screenshot
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Shows what happened, not what was expected.
-
  Id: b
  Text: The reviewer's acceptance, linked to the version they checked
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Ties acceptance to the right version.
-
  Id: c
  Text: The output stored in the approved location with its version number
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Others can find and rely on the exact output.
-
  Id: d
  Text: A message from you saying the output is ready for use
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Your statement is useful, but it is not proof.
-
  Id: e
  Text: The plan showing the task at 100% complete
  Correct: false
  Feedback: A plan update shows progress, not that the result was accepted.
-
  Id: f
  Text: A working copy saved on your laptop in case it is needed
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Uncontrolled copies cannot be relied on and may breach storage rules.

title: Moments
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Title: Testing
  Text: Follow the approved steps. Record the actual result and evidence. Log a defect when the result does not match.
-
  Title: Rehearsals
  Text: Run the task as it will be run for real. Record timings and anything that did not work.
-
  Title: Cutover
  Text: Use the current approved runbook. Start only when the checkpoint allows. Stop and raise any condition that is not met.
-
  Title: Hypercare
  Text: Resolve early issues through the hypercare log. Hand over accurate records to the normal team.

title: Playbook prompts
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
- Required result: what must my output achieve, and who accepts it?
- Approved version: am I using the current approved requirement, runbook or test steps?
- Evidence: what proof shows the result was met, and where is it stored?
- Current problem: what could stop me, what is its effect, and when does it matter?
- Person to contact: who answers questions, and who makes decisions outside my task?

title: Raise options
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: The supplier file may be late, which could affect testing. I am chasing and will update at Friday's meeting.
  Feedback: Visible, but it has no date, effect or request, and Friday is after the problem lands.
-
  Id: b
  Text: Supplier file now due Thursday, not Tuesday. Testing starts Wednesday, so rework and extra cost are likely. I have asked for a partial file. I need a decision on test order by Monday.
  Feedback: Recommended. It states the fact, effect, action taken, help needed and deadline.
-
  Id: c
  Text: Supplier file delayed by two days. I have asked the supplier to confirm a firm date and will raise it if Thursday also slips.
  Feedback: Reasonable follow-up, but it waits for a second slip before anyone can act.
-
  Id: d
  Text: Supplier is two days late. Please ask Procurement to escalate to the supplier's account manager to recover the date.
  Feedback: Proposes one fix but not the effect on testing, cost or the decision date.

title: Raise parts
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
- The fact
- Its effect
- When it matters
- What you have already tried
- The help or decision needed
- The last date a response is still useful

title: Raise situation
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
- Your task needs a supplier file by Tuesday. The supplier now says Thursday.
- Testing starts on Wednesday, so a Thursday file means rework and a likely extra supplier charge.

title: Raise types
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Title: Risk
  Text: Something that may happen and would affect your task or its outcome.
-
  Title: Issue
  Text: Something that has happened and is affecting your task now.
-
  Title: Dependency
  Text: An input, decision or activity that your task relies on.

title: Sort items
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Text: Use a faster sequence that leaves the result, cost, controls and deadline unchanged
  Answer: do
  Why: A normal working decision within your task. Record any material change to how it was done.
-
  Text: Fix a clear mistake in your own output using the agreed method
  Answer: do
  Why: Correcting your own work is yours when the solution is clear and authorised.
-
  Text: Tell another team they can have your output two days later
  Answer: check
  Why: Committing a date that others rely on needs the Workstream Lead or Project Manager.
-
  Text: Skip a review step because the change is small
  Answer: check
  Why: Agreed tests, reviews and approvals are not yours to remove.
-
  Text: An input you need has not arrived and the deadline is now at risk
  Answer: raise
  Why: Raise a missing dependency while there is still time to recover.
-
  Text: You spot a possible customer impact outside your task
  Answer: raise
  Why: You do not need to own it to make it visible.

title: Start brief
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text: Start brief: Prepare the reconciliation of migrated account balances by Friday. Use the account extract from Data Migration. Send your results to the Finance workstream.

title: Start gaps
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Id: a
  Text: You do not yet have approved access to the account extract, and a colleague offers to forward it from their inbox
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Access must be approved before work starts. Forwarding creates an unapproved copy of confidential data.
-
  Id: b
  Text: The brief does not say what a reconciled result must show or who accepts it
  Correct: true
  Feedback: Without acceptance conditions you cannot tell when the work is complete.
-
  Id: c
  Text: You are not sure which spreadsheet layout the Finance team prefers
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Worth asking, but it can be settled once the result and access are clear.
-
  Id: d
  Text: You would like a second person to check your formulas
  Correct: false
  Feedback: Good practice, and easy to arrange during the work rather than before it.

title: Task parts
breadcrumb: Workstream Team Member pathway — modules and exercises
text:
-
  Title: Required result
  Text: What the output must achieve, not just what you will do.
-
  Title: Owner
  Text: The person who assigned the work and will accept it.
-
  Title: Acceptance conditions
  Text: The conditions that must be met before the work counts as complete.
-
  Title: Due date
  Text: When the output is needed, and what depends on it.
-
  Title: Your decisions
  Text: Choices you may make yourself because they leave the result, cost, timing and controls unchanged.
-
  Title: Route for questions
  Text: Who answers questions and who makes decisions outside your task.

title: Boundary
text: change programme scope, approve budget, accept material risk, interpret legal or regulatory requirements, change policy, provide formal readiness approval or make the final go or no-go decision. A go or no-go decision is the formal decision on whether the transaction is ready and safe to proceed.

title: Confidential items
text:
- Use only approved systems and communication channels.
- Share information only with authorised people.
- Do not send transaction information to personal email or storage.
- Do not contact a counterparty unless the communication route is approved.
- Raise access problems instead of creating an informal workaround.

title: Cutover items
Decision test
text:
- Is this within my assigned task?
- Does it follow the agreed process and standard?
- Does it leave the agreed outcome, cost, timing and controls unchanged?
- Am I authorised to use the information and make this choice?

title: Economics
Evidence checks
text:
-
  - Complete
  - it covers the full agreed task.
-
  - Accurate
  - the data and statements have been checked.
-
  - Current
  - it reflects the latest approved position.
-
  - Traceable
  - another person can see the source and what changed.
-
  - Approved
  - the right person has reviewed or accepted it.
-
  - Controlled
  - it is stored in the correct location and version.

title: Glossary
text:
-
  Term: Acceptance criteria
  Def: The conditions that must be met before work is accepted as complete.
-
  Term: Scope
  Def: The work and outcomes included in an agreed task or workstream.
-
  Term: Dependency
  Def: An input, decision or activity that another task relies on.
-
  Term: RAID
  Def: Risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies.
-
  Term: Readiness evidence
  Def: Proof that people, processes, technology, data and controls are ready.
-
  Term: Dress rehearsal
  Def: A practice run before live execution.
-
  Term: Cutover
  Def: The controlled move from the current state to the new operating state.
-
  Term: Runbook
  Def: The timed plan of cutover tasks, owners, dependencies and fallback actions.
-
  Term: Hypercare
  Def: The period of extra monitoring and support immediately after cutover.
-
  Term: Escalation
  Def: Raising a matter to someone with the authority or support needed to resolve it.
-
  Term: Business as usual
  Def: The normal work performed outside the transaction programme.
-
  Term: Counterparty
  Def: The buyer or seller organisation on the other side of the transaction.
-
  Term: Checkpoint
  Def: A planned point when progress is checked and permission is given to continue.
-
  Term: Business case
  Def: The expected costs, benefits and value of the deal.
-
  Term: Go or no-go
  Def: The formal decision on whether the transaction is ready and safe to proceed.

title: Playbook
text:
-
  Title: Before starting a task
  Items:
    - Can I explain the required result?
    - Do I know the deadline and acceptance criteria?
    - Do I have the right information, access and tools?
    - Are my dependencies named and dated?
    - Do I have enough time and the right skills?
    - Do I know who can answer questions and make decisions?
-
  Title: Before reporting completion
  Items:
    - Does the output meet the agreed result?
    - Have I checked accuracy and completeness?
    - Is the evidence stored in the approved location?
    - Has the right person accepted the output?
    - Are open points and assumptions recorded?
    - Is the next task owner ready to receive it?
-
  Title: Before raising a problem
  Items:
    - What happened or may happen?
    - Which task or outcome is affected?
    - What evidence do I have?
    - What is the likely customer, control, cost or timing effect?
    - What have I already tried?
    - What help or decision is needed, and by when?
-
  Title: Before testing or rehearsal work
  Items:
    - Am I using the current approved steps?
    - Do I understand the expected result?
    - Am I recording the actual result and evidence?
    - Have I logged every failed or unexpected result?
    - Has the fix been retested?
    - Could the fix have affected another process?

title: Playbook
text:
-
  Title: Before a cutover task
  Items:
    - Am I using the current approved runbook?
    - Has the authorised checkpoint released my task?
    - Are the required inputs complete?
    - Do I know the fallback and escalation route?
    - Am I recording the actual timing and result?
    - Have I confirmed hand-off to the next owner?

title: Principles
text:
- Understand the outcome before starting the activity.
- Work within the agreed method and your authority.
- Record evidence as the work is completed.
- Raise missing inputs and risks early.
- Protect confidential information.
- Do not change acceptance criteria to fit the result.
- Follow controlled instructions during live execution.
- Make customer, cost and timing effects visible.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: You can complete a task faster by changing its sequence. The result, cost, control and deadline stay the same. What should you do?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Use the better sequence and record any material change to how the task was completed.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Ask the Workstream Executive because all changes to planned activity need senior approval.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Ask the Project Manager to make the decision because the sequence appears in the plan.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Follow the original sequence because Team Members should not change an assigned task.
  Answer: A
  Feedback: You can make normal working decisions within your task when the agreed outcome and controls remain unchanged.
-
  Q: When should a Team Member first raise a missing dependency?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: When the due date has passed and the delay can be measured accurately.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: When there is enough evidence that the missing input may affect the task or reduce recovery time.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: At the next scheduled status meeting, so the issue follows the agreed reporting route.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: After trying every available workaround within the team.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Early escalation preserves recovery choices. State what is known, what is uncertain and when a decision is needed.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: An activity has been performed successfully. When should it normally be reported as complete?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: When the person doing the work is satisfied with the result.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: When the activity is finished and any remaining evidence is listed as a follow-up action.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: When the agreed result and acceptance criteria are met and the required evidence is stored.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: When the Project Manager updates the activity to complete in the plan.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Completion is based on the agreed result, evidence and acceptance, not the activity or plan update alone.
-
  Q: You find that a supplier delay may add cost, but the amount is not yet confirmed. What should you do?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Wait for a confirmed amount so the programme receives accurate financial information.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Raise the likely cost and delay, explain the source and state what remains uncertain.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Record only the delivery delay because Finance owns cost reporting.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask the supplier to absorb the cost before reporting a possible business-case effect.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Your role is to make the delivery fact visible. The right owners can then assess and manage the financial effect.

title: Questions
text:
-
  Q: An authorised person asks you to use an unapproved channel because the normal system is unavailable. What matters most?
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Whether the file is encrypted before it is sent.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Whether the delivery deadline is more important than the temporary access issue.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Whether the sender and receiver both agree to the temporary method.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Whether the method itself is approved for the information being shared.
  Answer: D
  Feedback: A person's authority does not make an unapproved channel acceptable. Raise the access problem through the agreed route.

title: Raid items
Relevant resources
text:
-
  Name: Test script and evidence template
  Text: Records test steps, expected results, actual results and proof.
-

  Text: Records a failed result, its impact, owner, action, retest and closure evidence.
-
  Name: Readiness checklist or evidence index
  Text: Shows what proof is needed before the workstream can confirm readiness.
-
  Name: Cutover runbook or task checklist
  Text: Provides the approved timing, order, ownership, checkpoints and fallback actions for cutover.
-

title: Roles
text:

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: Two versions of the task
  Situation: The Project Manager asks you to update a customer data map by Friday. The process owner asks you to add a new field that is not in the agreed requirements. The acceptance criteria do not mention the field. Adding it would take half a day and would not move Friday's date.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Add the field because the process owner understands the business need and the deadline is unaffected.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Follow the agreed requirements and record the extra field as a possible improvement after Friday.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Clarify the required result with the Workstream Lead while completing the parts that are not affected by the question.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Include both versions in the Friday hand-off and ask the receiver to choose which one to accept.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C keeps progress moving and sends the scope decision to the person who owns it. Option A may introduce an unapproved requirement. Option B protects the agreed requirements but could ignore a valid need. Option D passes an unresolved decision to the receiver and weakens the hand-off.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: An intermittent test result
  Situation: A process fails twice during 20 test runs. The deadline remains achievable, and the technical team expects a one-day fix. The failure affects a small number of customer records.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Complete more test runs to determine whether the failure rate is high enough to record as a defect.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Record the defect and evidence, explain the customer effect and tell the test owner before the completion decision.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Allow the technical team to apply the fix first, then record only the final passing result if the retest succeeds.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Mark the test as conditionally passed because the deadline and wider test result are still within plan.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Option B preserves the real result and allows the right owner to assess its importance. Option A may provide useful analysis but delays defect control. Option C removes the audit trail. Option D makes an acceptance decision that sits outside the Team Member's role.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: An urgent information request
  Situation: An authorised counterparty contact needs a client file today. Their controlled workspace access has failed. They ask you to send the file to their personal email and promise to upload it once access is restored.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Send an encrypted copy because the person is authorised and the programme deadline is at risk.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Ask the contact to confirm the request in writing, then send the file using password protection.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Do not send the file through an unapproved channel. Raise the access failure through the agreed route and confirm the deadline impact.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Send only the minimum fields needed today and provide the full controlled file after access is restored.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C protects the information and makes the delivery risk visible. The recipient's authority does not make a personal email an approved channel. Options A, B and D reduce the amount or exposure but still use an unapproved route.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: The output works, but evidence is missing
  Situation: You complete a system change and confirm that it works. The test log was not saved because the session closed unexpectedly. Repeating the test will take two hours. The hand-off is due at the end of the day.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Mark the task complete because you observed the successful result and repeat the test only if the reviewer requests evidence.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Hand over the change with a note that evidence is pending, then complete the test log the next morning.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Tell the owner that evidence is missing, repeat the test and submit the output when the result can be checked and accepted.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask another attendee to confirm the result by email and use that message as the completion evidence.
  Answer: C
  Feedback: Option C protects the acceptance standard and makes the timing effect visible. Option A relies on memory. Option B separates completion from required evidence. Option D may support what happened, but it does not replace the agreed test record.

title: Scenarios
text:
-
  Title: An informal cutover change
  Situation: The approved runbook says your task starts at 01:00 after a checkpoint. At 00:25, a technical lead messages that the previous activity finished early and asks you to start at 00:30. The command centre has not issued a revised instruction.
  Options:
    -
      Key: A
      Text: Start at 00:30 because the previous owner has confirmed completion and the change creates extra contingency.
    -
      Key: B
      Text: Prepare to start, but confirm the change through the authorised checkpoint before executing the task.
    -
      Key: C
      Text: Wait until 01:00 because an approved runbook should not change during live execution.
    -
      Key: D
      Text: Ask the technical lead to record the change in the team chat, then start once that record exists.
  Answer: B
  Feedback: Option B preserves control while allowing the command centre to use the time gained. Option A relies on one person's message. Option C protects the plan but may ignore a valid controlled change. Option D creates a record but not the required authority.

title: Start steps
text:
-
  Title: Understand the deal context
  Confirm: Understand what is and is not included in the deal, why your work matters and which transaction outcome it supports.
  Good: You can explain the purpose of your task in plain language and know who to ask about missing context.
-
  Title: Confirm confidentiality and access
  Confirm: Know which information you may access, where it must be stored, who may receive it and which communication channels are approved.
  Good: Your access works and you do not need to move information into an unapproved location to complete the task.
-
  Title: Agree the required result
  Confirm: Agree the output, owner, deadline and acceptance criteria. Acceptance criteria are the conditions that must be met before work is accepted as complete.
  Good: You and the person accepting the work share the same understanding of ‘done’.
-
  Title: Confirm inputs and dependencies
  Confirm: Identify every input, decision or activity that your task relies on. These are your dependencies.
  Good: Each important dependency has an owner, due date and route for raising a delay.
-
  Title: Check time and capability
  Confirm: Check whether you have the time, knowledge, support and tools needed alongside your normal business-as-usual work.
  Good: Any capacity or skill gap is visible before it affects the deadline.
-
  Title: Know how to report and raise problems
  Confirm: Know how progress is reported, where evidence is stored and who receives risks, issues or decision requests.
  Good: You can raise a problem quickly without waiting for the next meeting.

title: Task cycle
text:
-
  Title: Confirm
  Text: Restate the required result, deadline and acceptance criteria before starting.
-
  Title: Prepare
  Text: Gather the required information, tools, approvals and inputs. Check that your dependencies are still on track.
-
  Title: Complete
  Text: Perform the work using the agreed method. Record important assumptions and choices.
-
  Title: Check
  Text: Review accuracy, completeness, control requirements and customer or operational effects.
-
  Title: Evidence
  Text: Store proof of the result in the approved location. Readiness evidence is proof that the required people, processes, technology, data and controls are ready.
-
  Title: Hand over
  Text: Give the output to the named receiver. Confirm that it has been accepted or record what remains open.

title: Legal & CorpDev
text: Key Role: Legal & CorpDev own the pre-signature process, including DD and legal drafting, as set out in current Absa processes. During execution, CorpDev tracks the business case, Legal tracks CPs and obligations, and both advise the programme on how signed deal terms affect completion, LD1 and post-close delivery.

title: Responsibilities
text:
- Run the pre-signing transaction process with the deal sponsor, including origination support, non-binding offer, governance route, advisor mobilisation and deal-team cadence - as per existing processes
- Develop and maintain the business case with Finance & Tax, including commercial rationale, strategic benefits, counterparty performance updates, valuation assumptions and value-tracking implications - as per existing processes
- Provide ultimate signoff on DD, owned by business areas - as per existing processes
- Own the transaction-document route across NBO, SPA, BSA, TSA, disclosure letter, CP schedule, warranties, covenants, indemnities, completion deliverables, standard-template deviations and related legal instruments - as per existing processes
- Translate DD mitigations and functional execution requirements into transaction documents. Bring in the Inorganic Change team pre-signature to ensure the migration plan reflects execution reality.
- Track CPs, approvals, litigation stays, legal consents, disclosure items, template reviews, product-specific documentation and post-signing obligations through an integrated obligations log.
- Track the progress against the business case post-signing through to completion, and escalate risks
- Provide legal advice and assurance to Central Hub, programme leadership and functional workstreams on what is permissible under signed documents and applicable country law.

title: Responsibilities
text:
- Coordinate external counsel, local counsel and accounting-firm support where specialist depth, jurisdictional nuance or capacity is required, with clear turnaround expectations and escalation paths.
- Hand over signed obligations, legal constraints, residual risks, open issues, document deviations and lessons learned to Central Hub, the business owner and BAU Legal / CorpDev owners after completion or LD1.

title: Legal & CorpDev
text:
Boundary Items:
  - Business workstreams own integration or separation execution; Legal & CorpDev supports by converting DD issues and execution requirements into legal terms and advising on signed-document constraints.
  - Compliance owns compliance interpretation, regulatory approval standards and regulatory-condition execution; Legal owns legal drafting, CP interpretation and legal obligation tracking, with Compliance as a critical dependency on regulatory CPs.
  - Finance & Tax owns valuation inputs, accounting, tax, completion accounts, funds flow, Group Interchange, TSA charging and financial-control evidence; CorpDev owns the business case and transaction-governance route with Finance input.
  - Central Hub owns integrated programme discipline, dependency management, weekly stakeholder reporting and Client readiness; Legal & CorpDev owns transaction-document content, CP interpretation and legal readiness evidence
  - Central Hub owns programme planning, mobilisation, and execution governance post-signature; Legal & CorpDev own pre-signature planning, governance, and mobilisation
  - Country Legal provides local legal nuance, local counsel coordination, local evidence, local drafting review and local-law advice; SA Legal leads as transaction SME where central drafting, governance and negotiation control are required.
  - Central Hub should be engaged during DD on acquisitions and early in complex or big-bang disposals so people, customer and operating-model implications are visible before legal terms are finalised.

title: Legal & CorpDev
text:
Central Hub Relationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Functional Spoke owns Legal and CorpDev transaction decisions, legal interpretation, CP tracking and business-case control while the Central Hub sets programme standards, maintains integrated dependency visibility, coordinates weekly stakeholder reporting and escalates transaction-wide issues.
Regional Relationship:
  - Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local DD evidence, local-law advice, local counsel coordination, local drafting review, approvals evidence and local execution constraints where they have capacity and delegated authority.
  - Function Authority retains transaction drafting, negotiation control, CorpDev deal governance, legal interpretation, CP tracking, business-case control and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.
  - As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and local-law input into delegated local counsel decisions, local approval execution and legal readiness activity, with Function Authority retaining transaction consistency, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

    Content: Maybe - CorpDev & Legal teams decide what the deal team looks like pre signing. Post-signing, a PM may be required where significant legal remediation is required
  -

    Content: Banking M&A legal expertise; competition and regulatory approvals; company secretarial and Board governance; employment, tax, data privacy, IP, technology and supplier-contract advice; litigation management; external counsel and accounting-firm coordination.

The operating-model requirement is limited to involving the relevant Business Area, country, integration and functional specialists at the appropriate point, subject to confidentiality, and handing DD risks and obligations into execution.

title: Balance-sheet acquisition
text:
Archetype Id: balance-sheet-acquisition
Archetype Name: Balance-sheet acquisition
Source Title: Balance Sheet Acquisition

title: Due Diligence
text:
Id: due-diligence
Index: 01
Title: Due Diligence
Purpose: Determine whether the acquisition creates value, what you are actually buying, and what needs to be protected contractually. Legal & CorpDev lead; other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key items for the integration team to consider during this process, they do not override current DD processes
Role:
  - Extract information from the DD process necessary to properly plan and run the implementation
  - Act as M&A SMEs to provide oversight, bringing a practical, Absa oriented lens which goes beyond financials and ensures nuances are identified and caught based on previous experience
Timeline: 1 – 3 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Deal perimeter (broader perimeter requires more detailed review)
  - Product complexity (more complex products are harder to model and project)
  - Maturity of DD teams (experienced teams can work through a DD checklist in a very short period)
  - Seller availability (heavily reliant on seller supporting in providing materials)

title: Due Diligence
text:
Necessary:
  - Ensure virtual data room set up to access confidential documentation and ensure it persists after deal signature
  - Ensure an NDA process to wall-cross those who need access to confidential information is set up
  - Understand the acquisition perimeter: which assets and liabilities transfer, how will we interact with what we are not buying, how does not having a full balance sheet impact the financials?
  - Understanding what the hurdle rates are: what EBITDA, NII, NIM, revenue, operating leverage, ROC, ROE, MOIC, will create a go-decision for deal signing?
  - Understanding the factors which influenced these hurdle rates, as well as what other non-financial factors may influence decision making (new capabilities, strong brand loyalty, etc)
  - Build an initial view of project implementation costs, leveraging comparable deals. All assumptions in planning costs must be defensible and informed by functional experts
  - Build or oversee build of a detailed business case comparing forecasted benefits to project costs and continued running costs
  - Ensure tax implications have been assessed and remediation planned
Conditional:
  - Understand the product set, the nuances of this product set, what other assets / liabilities are being sold to other buyers, and how this might impact execution (whether data sets are disentangled, whether coordination with other buyers will be required, etc)
  - Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

title: Due Diligence
text:
Optional:
  - Benchmark estimated performance against previous deals
  - Review lessons learnt from previous deals
  - Engage a subset of seller clients to assess current pain points and identify any potential deal red flags (e.g. compliance issues, pricing mismatches, in-scope technology issues)
  - Engage other buyers of seller business to understand key seller-specific pain points to avoid (e.g., data sharing issues, client communication issues)
Nuances:
  - DD must account for economies/diseconomies of scale inherent in taking part but not all of a business (e.g., cost base may not be halved by taking half the balance sheet)
  - DD must account for business line synergies inherent in taking part but not all of a business (e.g., potential to net off FX flows, fly-wheel inherent in having complementary businesses such as deposits and transaction banking)
Artefacts:
  - Previous transaction materials and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - Business case (Absa transaction specific)

title: Legal Drafting & Signature
text:
Id: legal-drafting-signature
Index: 02
Title: Legal Drafting & Signature
Purpose: Ensure the Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) reflects reality of programme delivery, and enables execution. Legal & CorpDev lead, other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key integration considerations, they do not overwrite the current processes.
Role:
  - Ensure legals reflect execution reality, and timelines are realistic
  - Ensure legals include provisions which will support execution, such as data sharing
  - Ensure any go-live dates are based on realistic assumptions around regulatory approval and client onboarding timelines
  - Leverage lessons learned from previous deals to ensure legals address any historic pain points
Timeline: 1 – 2 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Deal complexity (complex deals require additional protections and conditions)
  - Pre-signing alignment (pre-agree valuations and completion mechanisms will speed up drafting)
  - DD quality (high quality DD will allow defensible assumptions to be made in the legals, otherwise these will have to be assessed during this phase)
  - Regulatory complexity (multiple regulators across multiple jurisdictions increases complexity in drafting legals)

title: Legal Drafting & Signature
text:
Necessary:
  - Engage external lawyers to lead SPA drafting and negotiation, informed by internal legal opinion
  - Convert DD findings into agreed transaction terms including valuation, adjustment principles, completion mechanisms, and payment terms
  - Ensure price, adjustments and effective transfer date are agreed
  - Coordinate and confirm the signing sequence between Absa, the seller and other parties
  - Set out which items will transfer from seller to Absa automatically under agreed regulatory processes (e.g., Section 54), and which will have to be manually transferred
  - Detail novation processes for items not automatically transferring, whether independent legal opinions on contracts are required, and where liability sits during transfer
  - Set out the joint governance mechanisms across buyer and seller at a high level (e.g., the scheduling of joint Steering Committees, appointment of Transaction Directors from each party)
  - Set out joint escalation mechanisms for programme-level issues, as well as dispute resolution mechanisms
  - Set out conditions precedent for completion, including funds transfer, assets/liabilities transfer, regulatory approval, and board approval
  - Agree signatures required on each side
  - Set out completion date precedent on regulatory approval date(s), rather than a pre-agreed specific date

title: Legal Drafting & Signature
text:
Conditional:
  - Set out stipulations and timings for the sharing of client data, including whether business cases are required, and what can and can't be shared ahead of regulatory approval
  - Set out a joint communications plan to clients from both buyer and seller, including timelines for when buyer can engage the clients
  - Detail FX payment mechanisms, including adjustments for FX risk and longer settlement times
  - Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution
Optional:
  - Set SPA change control mechanisms
  - Set up SPA access mechanisms for project team members
  - Socialise with functional leads ahead of signature
Nuances:
  - Clients may not necessarily transfer with assets and liabilities. This must be assessed as a follow up question if not obvious from deal materials, and conditional activities related to clients made necessary
Artefacts:
  - DD summary and agreed deal decisions (Absa deal specific)
  - M&A lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
Templates:
  - NDA template

title: Mobilisation & Planning
text:
Id: mobilisation-planning
Index: 03
Title: Mobilisation & Planning
Purpose: Define the key activities which must take place to enable LD1 to take place on the agreed date, and surface dependencies
Role:
  - Inorganic Change team should lead the mobilisation effort across Absa: briefing functional leads / AEs, onboarding teams, executing the NDA process, creating onboarding materials, briefing teams on detailed plan creation, leading joint planning workshops, translating workshop outputs into a programme plan
Timeline: 4- 6 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Deal complexity (complex deals need more workstreams to execute)
  - Geographical scope (multiple geographies require more coordination)
  - Existing knowledge (teams familiar with these deals can draft a detailed plan much faster, and understand dependencies)
  - Available resource (resource constraints mean activities take longer)

title: Necessary
text:
- Set up mobilisation hierarchy:
  - Board appoints executive sponsor for the deal
  - Executive sponsor appoints Transaction Director
  - Transaction Director and Executive Sponsor agree Accountable Executives for each function / workstream
  - AE selection should be informed by their expected responsibilities, detailed in the Hub and Spoke Operating Model
  - AEs appoint functional workstream leads, who appoint in-country leads
  - Transaction Director mobilises central Inorganic Change team and in-country coordinators
  - Buyer and Seller Inorganic Change teams share lists of functional leads to enable joint planning
  - Joint and individual governance established based on Mobilisation Toolkit
- Define key workstreams required based on the deal-archetype and SPA specifics, including rough size of each workstream
- Define workstream charters per workstream, setting out objective, purpose, success metrics, key personnel, skills, and ownership
- Jointly carry out workstream bricks across buyer and seller, laying out each business process related to the workstream, which the seller will stop, which the buyer will start, and which will carry on as is
- Define key milestones required to enable these process and achieve a seamless cutover at Legal Day 1 (LD1)
- Support each workstream to define a detailed, L2 plan below this to enable the meeting of these milestones
- Hold joint workshops across buyer and seller to discuss and agree on these milestones
- Identify milestones with key dependencies across workstreams, and document these dependencies in detail

title: Necessary
text:
- Identify the critical path, and dates/factors will have a material impact on completion, and which of these can be controlled (e.g., regulatory approval or bank-wide change freezes cannot be controlled, data migration solution build and test is critical to LD1 success, etc)
- Translate the milestones into an overarching project plan to be tracked weekly
- Agree initial LD1 readiness criteria per workstream (key performance indicators which will enable cutover, e.g., for Data Migration, all source-to-target mapping complete)
- Agree on internal governance cadence which will sync with joint governance laid out in the SPA, including:
  - Internal and joint Inorganic Change meetings weekly / bi-weekly to align on priorities and joint risks/issues
  - Working group / workstream led sessions to discuss key risks, issues, and progress
  - Internal Steering Committee sessions to escalate Absa-specific risks and issues, and receive guidance on key decisions
  - Joint Steering Committee sessions to discuss joint risks and issues, and coordinate cross-party solutions
- Translate DD findings and governance structures into onboarding materials which clearly articulate the purpose and objectives of the deal, how execution will run day to day, roles and responsibilities, and escalation pathways

title: Mobilisation & Planning
text:
Conditional:
  - Submit a version of the programme plan to the regulator alongside the request for approval
  - Set up TSA exit team and define timeline for complete TSA exit
Optional:
  - Translate the project plan into project management software (e.g., Jira, MSP)
  - Link governance into bank-level governance such as Board meetings, StratCos, etc
Nuances:
  - Acquired components cannot operate independently, so missing capabilities must be available by Day 1
  - Different components may require different transfer or implementation dates
  - Multiple regulators may have to be engaged if multiple elements of the business are transferring (e.g., FSCA for client experience considerations, PA for prudence/capital considerations)
Artefacts:
  - TSA agreements (Absa transaction specific)
  - Regulatory commitments and approval timelines (Absa transaction specific)
  - Previous transaction playbooks with lessons learned (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - Mobilisation toolkit
Templates:
  - Workstream bricks
  - High-level transaction plan template
  - Detail excel project plan
  - Governance forums Terms of Reference

title: Programme Execution
text:
Id: programme-execution
Index: 04
Title: Programme Execution
Purpose: Execute on agreed milestones, run governance cadence, and build required technical/data solutions
Role:
  - Inorganic Change Team acts as the central hub in the execution phase, driving workstream level execution, tracking RAID items, defining SteerCo material, and holding those responsible for execution accountable
Timeline: 12 – 18 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Regulatory approval timelines
  - Deal perimeter and scope
  - New product build (additional product build requires more delivery time)
  - Data complexity (Complex structures require a more nuanced data migration solution)
  - Seller cooperation (early sharing of data, and daily cooperation speeds up timelines)

title: Necessary
text:
- Conduct programme management activities: run governance processes including workstream sessions, Exec SteerCos, and Joint Buyer/Seller SteerCos; set up and track risks and issues in a central RAID log, and escalate to SteerCo as appropriate
- Ensure product gap analysis is conducted to identify which product decisions must be made
- Ensure new product build decisions are made, leveraging detailed business cases on revenue, strategic, and client experience opportunities vs cost to build to New Product Authorities
- Drive development of new products through regular touchpoints led by Technology Workstream leadership and fed into programme governance
- Provide regular updates to the Board and Bank Leadership Forums on progress against plan, key risks and issues, and LD1 viability
- Engage the regulator regularly to update progress and assess approval timelines
- Conduct contingency and scenario planning for if approvals arrive later than anticipated, and define final possible date for receipt before LD1 must move
- Request that the seller shares a data dictionary detailing data structures across source systems
- Ensure source-to-target mapping across all systems is conducted to enable build of core data migration solution
- Drive the build of the data migration solution to Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) solution across all source systems into target systems
- Ensure the data migration solution is tested using dummy data aligned to the data dictionary, or where possible, real client data

title: Necessary
text:
- Agree with the buyer what data can be transferred ahead of LD1, and load it into Absa systems early to avoid cutover complications
- Define success criteria across all workstreams, and continually measure progress against these
- Work with the buyer to receive regularly updated financials, update the business case, and track that the deal remains aligned to strategic objectives

title: Programme Execution
text:
Conditional:
  - Set up a Clean Room to conduct KYC/AML checks, which should be entirely 'airgapped' - agree on Clean Room protocols with the seller
  - Onboard external KYC/AML experts to expedite the Clean Room process
  - Build out detailed client communication plan across buyer and seller, and keep clients updated on the progress of the programme, and when they can expect to be onboarded
  - If TSAs are in place, monitor service delivery and exit planning
Optional:
  - Engage friendly clients during the process to assess key value proposition and ensure project execution remains aligned
  - Conduct change management activities for project execution teams to drive continued buy-in and morale (e.g., team socials, rewards, etc)
Nuances:
  - Buyer execution must align with seller carve-out plans
  - Clients may not necessarily transfer with assets and liabilities. This must be assessed as a follow up question if not obvious from deal materials, and conditional activities related to clients made necessary
Artefacts:
  - Detail project plan built out from mobilisation and planning stage (Absa transaction specific)
    - With associated excel programme plan
  - Previous project playbooks with lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - Mobilisation toolkit
Templates:
  - Workstream status report template
  - Joint buyer and seller status report template
  - Programme RAID log template with added SteerCo escalation if necessary

title: Business Testing
text:
Id: business-testing
Index: 05
Title: Business Testing
Purpose: Check that acquired products and functionality works correctly
Timeline: 1 – 3 months (concurrent with execution, post-build)
Timeline Drivers:
  - Scale of business process change
  - Testing expertise in-house (testing SMEs within each team means scripts require less review and testing can happen faster)
  - Capacity within teams to accommodate testing (needs to be balanced with BAU, build, other deal-related work)
  - Complexity of process change (complex new products require significant testing)
  - Downstream systems (impact of changes on multiple downstream systems requires more extensive end-to-end testing)

title: Business Testing
text:
Necessary:
  - Work with BAU teams and functional / product SMEs to detail every business process impacted by changes the programme has made
  - Work with technology teams to understand the requirements for testing environments, including end-to-end environments
  - Book these environments well in advance, or flag if suitable environments do not yet exist and must be built
  - Drive execution of test scripts by the business
  - Conduct negative testing to ensure controls are functioning as expected
  - Once individual processes are validated, test every process end-to-end, including the feed into downstream systems like AML, finance, and reporting systems
  - Set up a testing-specific defect log to track issues to closure
  - Re-test issues post closure end-to-end, to ensure the fix has not created additional issues
  - Conduct Production Validation Testing to check that new functionality works in production as well as in test environments
  - Set up testing-specific governance, and feed into programme governance
  - Secure executive and business sign off on testing closure, with any open items clearly detailed
  - Test that only data in the scope of the deal is coming across, and data related to products outside of the perimeter is filtered out
Conditional:
  - Based on deal size and complexity set up an independent testing team to liaise with business and technology to drive test script creation and sign off
  - Based on deal size and complexity, designate a testing lead within each workstream responsible for coordinating and executing tests assigned to them

title: Business Testing
text:
Optional:
  - Conduct friendly client testing to ensure that end-to-end flows work in a real world scenario
Nuances:
  - Testing must check that out of scope data is not being transferred
  - Testing must check that the remaining Absa business is not impacted by the additional elements being transferred
Artefacts:
  - Previous business testing programmes with lessons learnt, including a scenario-based risk mitigation plan (Absa transaction specific)
  - Business testing process flows and customer journeys (Absa transaction specific)
Templates:
  - Detailed business testing plan template

title: LD1 Readiness
text:
Id: ld1-readiness
Index: 06
Title: LD1 Readiness
Purpose: Communicate requirements and functionality with clients, and prepare for the cutover
Role:
  - Oversee the standing up of an LD1 Readiness stream, and tracking its progress and risks as part of programme management to assess critical risks to LD1
Timeline: 1 – 3 months (concurrent to execution)
Timeline Drivers:
  - Client transfer (Clients transferring require communication and training)
  - Complexity of product mix (complex products and multi-product portfolios increase time to onboard)
  - Availability of client data (high-quality client contact data removes time spent on remediation)
  - Client responsiveness (heavily reliant on clients responding to outreach and providing documentation)
Necessary:
  - Build training materials on new products / functionalities, working closely with business SMEs
  - Build out materials outlining the value proposition of Absa to clients, including for products which they do not yet have to drive cross-sell opportunities
  - Set up client accounts, profiles, products, permissions, and mandates ahead of time to enable Dress Rehearsals and testing
  - Define and test the updated service model
  - Define the Hypercare model for post go-live, including detailed roles and responsibilities

title: LD1 Readiness
text:
Conditional:
  - Assess in detail the client onboarding process, understand timelines, and define a 'drop-dead date' for when onboarding must begin
  - Assess which onboarding processes must be done BAU, and which can be adapted to suit deal context and timelines
  - Detail all client documentation required to enable onboarding
  - Perform gap analysis to understand which information can be sourced from the seller, and which clients must provide directly
  - Ensure client contact details are shared by seller as early as possible, and track client outreach
  - Conduct risk assessment to understand which clients are high risk, and which some documentation can be obtained post-LD1
  - Confirm required KYC / AML documentation in place across transferring clients
  - Set up sessions to train clients on bank systems and channels
Optional:
  - Discuss with the seller the potential for onboarding clients ahead of LD1 to de-risk the cutover weekend
  - Conduct friendly-client testing with these new to bank clients
Nuances:
  - This phase may be significantly reduced if no clients are transferring (only assets / liabilities), as onboarding would not be required
Artefacts:
  - Client onboarding playbook (Absa transaction specific)
  - Client training materials (Absa transaction specific)

title: Dress Rehearsals
text:
Id: dress-rehearsals
Index: 07
Title: Dress Rehearsals
Purpose: Testing end-to-end approach to cutover in order to raise and resolve any issues which would prevent a successful transfer
Role:
  - Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the Data Migration team in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Data Migration Coordinators (DMCs).
Timeline: 8 – 12 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Time remaining post build and test (if build and test finishes well ahead of LD1, more DRs can take place)
  - Number of Dress Rehearsals (DRs) (more DRs require a longer timeframe)
  - Down-time between DRs (minimum 2 weeks between DRs is recommended)

title: Dress Rehearsals
text:
Necessary:
  - Work with the Data Migration and Technology teams to define cutover plan which details every activity down to the minute required to carve out assets/liabilities at the seller and stand up these within Absa
  - Hold runbook run-through sessions with all activity owners and back-ups to ensure everyone is clear on expectations
  - Define success metrics for DRs, with a clear understanding of what is acceptable in the first DR vs the final DR
  - Agree which data sets will be dummy / anonymised, and which will be real client data
  - Define roles and responsibilities across DRs and Cutover, including Data Migration Controllers running the runbook
  - Execute logistical support required to enable 24/7 DRs to take place such as building access, food requirements, accommodation, travel, Wi-Fi, security, facilities, and back-up plans
  - Define the governance processes to take place during DRs including the command centre, regular executive updates, escalation pathways, war room protocols, issue resolution processes, and continency decision making
  - Collate a DR playbook summarising success criteria, logistical information, key contacts, governance processes, and timelines
  - Run a minimum of 4 DRs across weekends, with at least 2 weeks in between each
  - Each DR should execute the runbook end-to-end, and track issues which arise for remediation
  - Hold DR retros to note lessons learnt and iterate into subsequent DRs
  - Track the remediation of issues ahead of subsequent DRs

title: Dress Rehearsals
text:
Conditional:
  - If Absa has existing assets / liabilities on the balance sheet the same as are being transferred, ensure that DRs test that existing balances, rates, pricing, and funding rates are not impacted
  - If these assets / liabilities form new products to Absa, ensure DRs assess that these have no impact on the wider balance sheet (e.g., funding issues)
Optional:
  - Hold a 'Technical DR' before the true DRs take place, to test only the migration solution, and ensure this is not a blocker to future DRs
Nuances:
  - DRs may need to account for new-to-bank products, or validate no impact on existing products enhanced by the assets/liabilities transferring
Artefacts:
  - Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)
  - Previous DR completion records with timestamps, success measure results and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Runbook template
  - DR defect template
  - DR checkpoint template
  - DR retro template

title: Go/No-Go
text:
Id: go-no-go
Index: 08
Title: Go/No-Go
Purpose: Formally discuss and approve/disapprove whether all workstreams and parties are sufficiently ready to proceed with transfer
Role:
  - Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.
Timeline: 1- 2 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
  - Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
  - SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

title: Go/No-Go
text:
Necessary:
  - Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
  - Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place
  - Discuss residual risks and mitigation plans across each workstream, with each AE laying out in turn testing results, DR success, and residual risks related to their area
  - For each residual risk, lay out the potential risk to go-live, likelihood, and mitigation plans
  - Gather evidence that key conditions have been met such as:
    - Regulatory approval
    - Data extraction and reconciliation in DRs
    - Financial settlement success in DRs
    - Absa and seller obligations as stipulated in the SPA
  - Gather all AEs / SteerCo members to formally make and document the Go/No-Go decision internally, allowing any reservations to be noted and addressed
  - Gather buyer and seller AEs to formally make the joint Go/No-Go decision
  - Formally document go/no position with the Seller and communicate to clients, employees, and regulators
Conditional:
  - Gather evidence that additional conditions have been met such as:
    - Client onboarding
    - Account set up
    - Client and contract novations / consents
  - Include a Go/No-Go decision related to employee readiness, including the completion of key conditions such as consultations
  - Include additional regulatory requirements, such as the registration of certain employees with regulatory bodies (e.g., FAIS registration of trading employees)

title: Go/No-Go
text:
Optional:
  - Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)
  - Brief the media on the decision, with a series of prepared remarks
Nuances:
  - Go/No-Go may need to account for client onboarding should clients be in scope for transfer
Artefacts:
  - Go/No-Go criteria (owned by Inorganic Change Team to use throughout this decision making process)
  - M&A Learning Academy materials on governance and decision rights
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Go/No-Go decision scorecard/paper

title: Cutover
text:
Id: cutover
Index: 09
Title: Cutover
