  - Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover
Nuances:
  - Cutover for a deal of this type will be the most complex and high-risk, given the full integration of a bank. It could be staged, therefore, rather than 'big bang'
Artefacts:
  - Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke Operating Model
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Cutover checkpoint template

title: Hypercare
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant A · Buyer integrates the business)
text:
Id: hypercare
Index: 10
Title: Hypercare
Purpose: Stabilise the Absa group business as required, ensure TSAs are active as required, resolve any residual issues from cutover, and support buyer Hypercare.
Role:
  - Monitor a consolidated view of incidents post cutover, and monitor the Hypercare team's triage and remediation efforts
  - Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
  - Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
  - Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes
Timeline: 1 – 2 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Number of clients transferring (additional clients means Additional time required to triage and resolve issues)
  - Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
  - Complexity of transfer (a transfer of complex clients with complex products likely requires more dedicated service time)
  - Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

title: Hypercare
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant A · Buyer integrates the business)
text:
Necessary:
  - Set up a dedicated team to monitor residual cutover issues, retained business issues, and any post-cutover data corrections or additions required
  - Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
  - Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
  - Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
  - Set up dedicated client communications teams to ensure retained clients remain in the loop post LD1
  - Gradually hand off servicing to BAU teams by transitioning issue resolution and triage into the BAU process, prioritising only the most serious issues for Hypercare as time passes
  - Track divestment objectives such as cost, asset/liability transfer, volumes, etc. as soon as LD1, and provide updates to executives on progress against objectives
  - Hold daily touchpoints with AEs to flag the most important issues and discuss remediation plans
  - Hold regular touchpoints with client-facing teams to discuss client sentiment and assess action plans
  - Conduct completion-account and purchase-price true-ups
  - Ensure closure of intra-group accounts and interfaces
  - Confirmation of buyer data-return or deletion obligations
  - Ensure post-completion support is within the bounds of SPA and TSAs

title: Hypercare
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant A · Buyer integrates the business)
text:
Conditional:
  - Support the buyer's Hypercare for systems which have transitioned from Absa to buyer
  - Monitor TSA performance, track progress towards exit, and remove remaining entanglements
  - Resolve any transfer exceptions or data inaccuracies
  - Monitor warranties, indemnities, and potential claims
Optional:
  - Reach out to clients directly to assess sentiment
Nuances:
  - Absa knowledge may be required to support buyer Hypercare for transferred systems/technologies
Artefacts:
  - Transferred portfolio of clients (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - M&A Learning Pathways
Templates:
  - Hypercare RAID Log
  - Daily Hypercare status report template
  - TSA service dashboard and exit plan

title: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Archetype Id: full-business-divestment
Archetype Name: Full-business divestment
Variant Label: Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone
Source Title: Full Business Sale B (Buyer runs the business as standalone)

title: Due Diligence
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: due-diligence
Index: 01
Title: Due Diligence
Purpose: Determine whether the acquisition creates value, what you are actually buying, and what needs to be protected contractually. Legal & CorpDev lead; other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key items for the integration team to consider during this process, they do not override current DD processes
Role:
  - Extract information from the DD process necessary to properly plan and run the divestment
  - Act as M&A SMEs to provide oversight, bringing a practical, Absa oriented lens which goes beyond financials and ensures nuances are identified and caught based on previous experience
Timeline: 1 – 3 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Product complexity (more complex products are harder for a seller to model and project)
  - Maturity of DD teams (experienced teams can pre-empt buyer questions and data requests ahead of time)
  - Buyer availability (heavily reliant on buyer capacity to review and assess materials)

title: Due Diligence
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Necessary:
  - Ensure virtual data room set up to share confidential documentation and ensure it persists after deal signature
  - Ensure an NDA process to wall-cross those who need access to confidential information is set up
  - Ensure buyer has the requisite information access controls set up to protect Absa confidential information
  - Build an initial view of project divestment costs, leveraging comparable deals, including TSA costs. All assumptions in planning costs must be defensible and informed by functional experts
  - Build or oversee build of a detailed business case comparing forecasted benefits of divestment to project costs and continued running costs
  - Ensure services the divested business currently receives from Absa are identified
  - Ensure tax implications have been assessed and remediation planned
  - Ensure the complete legal entity, subsidiary and branch structure is understood
  - Ensure ownership of assets, intellectual property and licences is reviewed
  - Ensure assessment of seller-group dependencies which must be terminated, replaced or covered by TSAs has taken place
Conditional:
  - Ensure that the value of intangible assets is also considered and assessed, and that this informs the sale price
  - Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

title: Due Diligence
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Optional:
  - Review lessons learnt from previous deals
  - Engage a subset of buyer clients to assess current pain points and identify any potential deal red flags (e.g. compliance issues, pricing mismatches, in-scope technology issues)
Nuances:
  - DD must account for business line impact inherent in selling all of the business (e.g., capital, funding, and liquidity impact on Absa group)
Artefacts:
  - Previous transaction materials and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - Business case (Absa transaction specific)

title: Legal Drafting & Signature
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: legal-drafting-signature
Index: 02
Title: Legal Drafting & Signature
Purpose: Ensure the Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) reflects reality of programme delivery, and enables execution. Legal & CorpDev lead, other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key integration considerations, they do not overwrite the current processes.
Role:
  - Ensure legals reflect execution reality, and timelines are realistic
  - Ensure legals include provisions which will support execution, such as data sharing
  - Ensure any go-live dates are based on realistic assumptions around regulatory approval and client onboarding timelines
  - Leverage lessons learned from previous deals to ensure legals address any historic pain points
Timeline: 1 – 2 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Deal complexity (complex deals require additional protections and conditions)
  - Pre-signing alignment (pre-agreed valuations and completion mechanisms will speed up drafting)
  - DD quality (high quality DD will allow defensible assumptions to be made in the legals, otherwise these will have to be assessed during this phase)
  - Regulatory complexity (multiple regulators across multiple jurisdictions increases complexity in drafting legals)
  - TSA requirements (complex and numerous TSA requirements will increase the complexity of resulting legals)

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Engage external lawyers to lead SPA drafting and negotiation, informed by internal legal opinion
- Negotiate transaction terms including valuation, adjustment principles, completion mechanisms, and payment terms
- Ensure price, adjustments and effective transfer date are agreed
- Coordinate and confirm the signing sequence between Absa, the buyer and other parties
- Set out which items will transfer from Absa to the buyer automatically under agreed regulatory processes (e.g., Section 54), and which will have to be manually transferred
- Detail novation processes for items not automatically transferring, whether independent legal opinions on contracts are required, and where liability sits during transfer
- Set out the joint governance mechanisms across buyer and seller at a high level (e.g., the scheduling of joint Steering Committees, appointment of Transaction Directors from each party)
- Set out joint escalation mechanisms for programme-level issues, as well as dispute resolution mechanisms
- Set out conditions precedent for completion, including funds transfer, regulatory approval, and board approval
- Agree signatures required on each side
- Set out completion date precedent on regulatory approval date(s), rather than a pre-agreed specific date
- Set out a joint communications plan to clients from both buyer and seller, including timelines for when buyer can engage the clients
- Place clear obligations on the buyer for regulatory approvals, onboarding and operational readiness
- Set out transfer of shares and legal title, and regulatory change of control requirements

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text: - Detail technology maintenance requirements of Absa, and stipulations on major changes

title: Legal Drafting & Signature
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Conditional:
  - Detail FX payment mechanisms, including adjustments for FX risk and longer settlement times
  - Define ownership and licensing of shared Intellectual Property
  - Establish TSAs, service levels, pricing, liabilities, and exit dates
  - Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution
Optional:
  - Set SPA change control mechanisms
  - Set up SPA access mechanisms for project team members
  - Socialise with functional leads ahead of signature
Nuances:
  - SPA is likely to be a Share Purchase Agreement, given the full divestment of a legal entity
  - Regulatory approval is focused on change of control of licences, as well as competition approval
Artefacts:
  - DD summary and agreed deal decisions (Absa deal specific)
  - M&A lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
Templates:
  - NDA template

title: Mobilisation & Planning
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: mobilisation-planning
Index: 03
Title: Mobilisation & Planning
Purpose: Define the key activities which must take place to enable LD1 to take place on the agreed date, and surface dependencies
Role:
  - Inorganic Change team should lead the mobilisation effort across Absa: briefing functional leads / AEs, onboarding teams, executing the NDA process, creating onboarding materials, briefing teams on detailed plan creation, and supporting the buyer to lead joint planning efforts
Timeline: 2- 4 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Deal complexity (complex deals need more workstreams to execute)
  - Geographical scope (multiple geographies require more coordination)
  - Existing knowledge (teams familiar with these deals can draft a detailed plan much faster, and understand dependencies)
  - Available resource (resource constraints mean activities take longer)

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Set up mobilisation hierarchy:
  - Board appoints executive sponsor for the deal
  - Executive sponsor appoints Transaction Director
  - Transaction Director and Executive Sponsor agree Accountable Executives for each function / workstream
  - AE selection should be informed by their expected responsibilities, detailed in the Hub and Spoke Operating Model
  - AEs appoint functional workstream leads, who appoint in-country leads
  - Transaction Director mobilises central Inorganic Change team and in-country coordinators
  - Buyer and Seller Inorganic Change teams share lists of functional leads to enable joint planning
  - Joint and individual governance established based on Mobilisation Toolkit
- Each asset, process, capability, should be classified as either:
  - Transfer
  - Retain
  - Duplicate
  - Terminate
  - Replace by the buyer
  - Provide temporarily through a TSA
- Set up a Transaction and Exit Management Office run by the Inorganic Change Team to lead the separation from Absa's side
- Define minimum required workstreams to provide buyer with sufficient information to run the business at separation, and define key roles and responsibilities
- Define key milestones ahead of Legal Day 1 (LD1), focused on information and set up required by the buyer to run the business in isolation
- Support each workstream to define a detailed, L2 plan below this to enable the meeting of these milestones
- Hold joint workshops across buyer and seller to discuss and agree on these milestones

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Identify milestones with key dependencies across workstreams, and document these dependencies in detail
- Define a stranded cost remediation plan
- Set up a buyer-obligation and dependency tracker to ensure buyer is held accountable for conditions precedent
- Identify the critical path, and dates/factors will have a material impact on completion, and which of these can be controlled (e.g., regulatory approval or bank-wide change freezes cannot be controlled, etc)
- Translate the milestones into an overarching project plan to be tracked weekly
- Agree on internal governance cadence which will sync with joint governance laid out in the SPA, including:
  - Internal and joint Inorganic Change meetings weekly / bi-weekly to align on priorities and joint risks/issues
  - Working group / workstream led sessions to discuss key risks, issues, and progress
  - Internal Steering Committee sessions to escalate Absa-specific risks and issues, and receive guidance on key decisions
  - Joint Steering Committee sessions to discuss joint risks and issues, and coordinate cross-party solutions
- Translate DD findings and governance structures into onboarding materials which clearly articulate the purpose and objectives of the deal, how execution will run day to day, roles and responsibilities, and escalation pathways
- Define a Day 1 control-handover plan, and Board and governance transition plan
- Set up a Seller-group dependency map and an Intra-group balance and contract exit plan

title: Mobilisation & Planning
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Conditional:
  - Submit a version of the programme plan to the regulator alongside the request for approval
  - Create a detailed workstream plan for employee / tech transfer
  - Define a TSA service catalogue and exit plan
  - Set up TSA exit team and define timeline for complete TSA exit
Optional:
  - Translate the project plan into project management software (e.g., Jira, MSP)
  - Link governance into bank-level governance such as Board meetings, StratCos, etc
Nuances:
  - The business is being run standalone, so reduced scope of planning can take place, focused on providing the buyer the required information ahead of LD1, supporting with any additional set up, and disentangling the business from within Absa
Artefacts:
  - TSA agreements (Absa transaction specific)
  - Regulatory commitments and approval timelines (Absa transaction specific)
  - Previous transaction playbooks with lessons learned (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - Mobilisation toolkit
Templates:
  - High-level transaction plan template
  - Detail excel project plan
  - Governance forums Terms of Reference
  - TSA service catalogue
  - Buyer obligations tracker

title: Programme Execution
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: programme-execution
Index: 04
Title: Programme Execution
Purpose: Maintain the value and stability of the business, disentangle it from the wider Absa group, and execute the activities required to transfer ownership and control.
Role:
  - Inorganic Change Team acts as the central hub in the execution phase, driving workstream level execution, tracking RAID items, defining SteerCo material, and holding those responsible for separation accountable, whilst ensuring the buyer is making significant progress
Timeline: 6 – 12 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Regulatory approval timelines
  - Data complexity (Complex structures require a more nuanced data migration solution)
  - TSA service plan (High number of TSAs can lead to faster initial completion, with work backloaded into TSA execution and exit)

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Conduct programme management activities: run governance processes including workstream sessions, Exec SteerCos, and Joint Buyer/Seller SteerCos; set up and track risks and issues in a central RAID log, and escalate to SteerCo as appropriate
- Separate financial reporting, ledger, controls, and regulatory reporting from the Absa group
- Separate data, interfaces, and applications from Absa group
- Ensure the divested business' value is maintained ahead of LD1, to avoid complications in completion and valuation
- Remediate stranded costs within the retained organisation
- Plan for and execute any required funding, capital, and liquidity changes needed on Absa's side
- Execute disentanglement of Absa's financial and regulatory reporting from the business being sold
- Track buyer obligations, flag issues, and escalate to Joint SteerCo as appropriate
- Novate, assign or replicate contracts which will be transferring to the buyer
- Provide regular updates to the Board and Bank Leadership Forums on progress against plan, key risks and issues, and LD1 viability
- Engage the regulator regularly to update progress and assess approval timelines
- Conduct contingency and scenario planning for if approvals arrive later than anticipated, and define final possible date for receipt before LD1 must move
- Build out detailed client communication plan across buyer and seller, and keep clients updated on the progress of the programme
- Define success criteria across all workstreams, and continually measure progress against these

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Provide the buyer with regularly updated financials to track the progress of the divested business
- Replace Absa funding, capital or liquidity support
- Establish standalone financial and regulatory reporting where required
- If TSAs are in place, monitor service delivery and exit planning

title: Programme Execution
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Optional:
  - Conduct change management activities for project execution teams to drive continued buy-in and morale (e.g., team socials, rewards, etc)
Nuances:
  - As the business is being run as standalone by the buyer, execution from Absa's side will focus on disentanglement and ensuring minimal impact on the wider Absa group
Artefacts:
  - Detail project plan built out from mobilisation and planning stage (Absa transaction specific)
    - With associated excel programme plan
  - Previous project playbooks with lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - Mobilisation toolkit
Templates:
  - Workstream status report template
  - Joint buyer and seller status report template
  - Programme RAID log template with added SteerCo escalation if necessary
  - TSA service catalogue

title: Business Testing
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: business-testing
Index: 05
Title: Business Testing
Purpose: Confirm that the business will continue operating under its new owner and that Absa can operate safely after the target is removed from the group.
Role:
  - Inorganic Change Team role is to coordinate and govern testing across business and technology teams, not to perform testing itself.
Timeline: 0 – 2 months (concurrent with execution, post-build)
Timeline Drivers:
  - Scale of business process change
  - Testing expertise in-house (testing SMEs within each team means scripts require less review and testing can happen faster)
  - Capacity within teams to accommodate testing (needs to be balanced with BAU, build, other deal-related work)
  - Complexity of process change (complex new systems or products require significant testing)
  - Downstream systems (impact of changes on multiple downstream systems requires more extensive end-to-end testing)

title: Business Testing
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Necessary:
  - Ensure the buyer has detailed all business process changes occurring as part of the deal to be included in testing
  - Detail any business or technology changes impacting the retained business on Absa's side
  - Work with technology teams to understand the requirements for testing environments, including end-to-end environments
  - Ensure retained business regression test scripts are created which ensure:
    - Retained applications and interfaces continue functioning
    - Regulatory and fin-crime reporting remains working as expected
  - Book these environments well in advance, or flag if suitable environments do not yet exist and must be built
  - Set up a testing-specific defect log to track issues to closure
  - Re-test issues post closure end-to-end, to ensure the fix has not created additional issues
  - Secure executive and business sign off on testing closure, with any open items clearly detailed
  - Test financial deconsolidation, and buyer consolidation processes
Conditional:
  - Test that TSAs and service levels are functioning as expected
Optional:
  - Set up an independent testing team to liaise with business and technology to drive test script creation and sign off
  - Set up testing-specific governance, and feed into programme governance
  - Designate a testing lead within each workstream responsible for coordinating and executing tests assigned to them

title: Business Testing
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Nuances:
  - As the buyer will run the business as standalone, testing can be narrower in scope, and focus on regression testing Absa's group reporting and applications remain functioning as expected once the separation occurs
Artefacts:
  - Previous business testing programmes with lessons learnt, including a scenario-based risk mitigation plan (Absa transaction specific)
  - Business testing process flows and customer journeys (Absa transaction specific)
Templates:
  - Detailed business testing plan template

title: Client Continuity & LD1 Readiness
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: client-continuity-ld1-readiness
Index: 06
Title: Client Continuity & LD1 Readiness
Purpose: Communicate plans and functionality with clients, and set up an orderly transfer to the buyer
Role:
  - Oversee the standing up of an LD1 Readiness stream, and tracking both Absa and buyer progress and risks as part of programme management to assess critical risks to LD1
Timeline: 2 – 4 weeks (concurrent to execution, alongside buyer)
Timeline Drivers:
  - Scale of client transfer (more clients require additional communications alongside the buyer)
Necessary:
  - Allocate responsibility for each client interaction between seller and buyer
  - Share Absa risk profiles of clients, to enable the buyer to understand which clients are high risk, and which some documentation can be obtained post-LD1
  - Share existing required KYC / AML documentation across transferring clients
  - Define Absa's role in the Hypercare model for post go-live, and how much support the buyer requires from Absa experts
  - Identify client contracts with change-of-control provisions
  - Confirm how complaints and conduct issues will be handled
  - Monitor client attrition and reputational risk
  - Communicate any brand, ownership or contact changes
Conditional:
  - Prepare client-facing employees transferring by ensuring clients have their new contact details for once they have transferred to the buyer

title: Client Continuity & LD1 Readiness
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Nuances:
  - Dedicated LD1 Readiness capacity on the buyer and seller side is less critical if the business is being run as standalone, as clients generally remain with the same legal entity and do not require full buyer onboarding. Focus is instead on clear communication of timelines, and monitoring attrition risk

title: Dress Rehearsals
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: dress-rehearsals
Index: 07
Title: Dress Rehearsals
Purpose: Testing end-to-end approach to separation in order to raise and resolve any issues which would prevent a successful separation
Role:
  - Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the operations and legal teams in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Migration Coordinators (MCs).
Timeline: 4 – 8 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Number of Dress Rehearsals (DRs) (more DRs require a longer timeframe)
  - Down-time between DRs (minimum 2 weeks between DRs is recommended)

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Ensure that runbook activities include provision for testing of continued regulatory and financial reporting, as well as financial reconciliation on the buyer's side
- Hold runbook run-through sessions with all activity owners and back-ups to ensure everyone is clear on expectations
- Define success metrics for DRs, with a clear understanding of what is acceptable in the first DR vs the final DR
- Define roles and responsibilities across DRs and Cutover, including Data Migration Controllers running the runbook
- Execute logistical support required to enable 24/7 DRs to take place such as building access, food requirements, accommodation, travel, Wi-Fi, security, facilities, and back-up plans
- Define the governance processes to take place during DRs including the command centre, regular executive updates, escalation pathways, war room protocols, issue resolution processes, and continency decision making
- Collate a DR playbook summarising success criteria, logistical information, key contacts, governance processes, and timelines
- Confirm after each DR that retained data has not been transferred
- Run a minimum of 2 DRs across weekends, with at least 2 weeks in between each
- Each DR should execute the runbook end-to-end, and track issues which arise for remediation
- Hold DR retros to note lessons learnt and iterate into subsequent DRs
- Track the remediation of issues ahead of subsequent DRs
- Include DR activities which test legal completion, transfer of ownership, and purchase price settlement

title: Necessary
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
- Assess financial deconsolidation and treasury and funding transition during DRs
- Assess continuity of regulatory reporting within Absa group during DRs

title: Dress Rehearsals
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Conditional:
  - Include DR activities which relate to the set up of brand new systems or migration of Absa technology into buyer environments
  - Include DR activities which simulate TSA activation
Optional:
  - Hold a 'Table-top DR' before the true DRs take place, to run through the full runbook with all owners, without having to execute each step in the proper environments
Nuances:
  - As the buyer will run the business as standalone, scale of DRs can be significantly reduced, and driven by the level of operational change occurring.
  - A tabletop rehearsal plus one full completion rehearsal may be sufficient where the entity continues on its existing systems
Artefacts:
  - Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)
  - Previous DR completion records with timestamps, success measure results and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Runbook template
  - DR defect template
  - DR checkpoint template
  - DR retro template

title: Go/No-Go
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: go-no-go
Index: 08
Title: Go/No-Go
Purpose: Formally discuss and approve/disapprove whether all workstreams and parties are sufficiently ready to proceed with separation
Role:
  - Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.
Timeline: 1- 2 weeks
Timeline Drivers:
  - Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
  - Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
  - SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

title: Go/No-Go
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Necessary:
  - Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
  - Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place
  - Discuss residual risks and mitigation plans across each workstream, with each AE laying out in turn testing results, DR success, and residual risks related to their area
  - For each residual risk, lay out the potential risk to go-live, likelihood, and mitigation plans
  - Gather evidence that key conditions have been met such as:
    - Regulatory change-of-control approval
    - Financial settlement success in DRs
    - Buyer obligations as stipulated in the SPA
    - Board and governance transition readiness
    - TSA readiness
    - Funding and liquidity readiness
    - Agreement and acceptance of residual separation risks
  - Gather all AEs / SteerCo members to formally make and document the Go/No-Go decision internally, allowing any reservations to be noted and addressed
  - Gather buyer and seller AEs to formally make the joint Go/No-Go decision
  - Formally document go/no position with the Buyer and communicate to clients, employees, and regulators
  - Include a Go/No-Go decision related to employee readiness, including the completion of key conditions such as consultations
Conditional:
  - Distinguish between:
    - Legal completion readiness
    - Operational separation readiness
    - TSA-supported Day 1 readiness

title: Go/No-Go
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Optional:
  - Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)
  - Brief the media on the decision, with a series of prepared remarks
Nuances:
  - Go/No-Go should focus on the buyer's readiness to run the business independently, and Absa's assurance that no continuing operations will be impacted, distinguishing legal completion readiness from any longer-term buyer integration activity
Artefacts:
  - Go/No-Go criteria (owned by Inorganic Change Team to use throughout this decision making process)
  - M&A Learning Academy materials on governance and decision rights
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Go/No-Go decision scorecard/paper

title: Legal Completion & Control Handover
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: legal-completion-control-handover
Index: 09
Title: Legal Completion & Control Handover
Purpose: Execute the controlled separation of the full business while maintaining continuity, and legally pass ownership to the buyer
Role:
  - Coordinate the logistical preparation of the cutover, based upon successful DR. Support the execution of the cutover
  - Run the central control function, coordinating Absa activities and linking in with the buyer, and overseeing workstream execution against approved runbook.
  - Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies and stakeholder communications through the cutover timeline.
Timeline: 24 to 72 hours
Timeline Drivers:
  - Scale of activity required over cutover
  - Length of individual activities (some activities may last 24 hours + depending on their nature)
  - Length of time the bank can shut down without impacting service (some jurisdictions have payments flowing over the weekend, others do not)

title: Legal Completion & Control Handover
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Necessary:
  - Define the final cutover plan, iterated during DRs
  - Ensure required legal documents are signed over cutover to formally transfer legal and operational control to the buyer
  - Ensure Absa system access to divested business is revoked or modified
  - Walk through the plan again with teams to confirm understanding, roles, and responsibilities
  - Sign off final cutover plan with all AEs
  - Coordinate contingency planning across all workstreams, gathering scenarios and planning for potential issues which may arise over the cutover
  - Define any additional governance to be in place during cutover vs DRs (e.g., additional executive updates, final decision gates, etc)
  - Execute on cutover plan, including agreed-upon governance gates
  - Execute on testing activities planned in the runbook to ensure all remaining Abse-group systems are working as planned
  - Hold final checkpoint to assess success of the cutover, ensure retained systems continue to function, and assess Absa support required in mitigation plans for issues
  - Continue to communicate with the buyer to assess issues and provide support where needed
  - Execute purchase-price settlement and transfer shares and legal title.
  - Complete Board resignations and appointments and transfer governance and delegated authorities
  - Replace Absa funding and guarantees
  - Confirm that the target and remaining Absa group are operational

title: Legal Completion & Control Handover
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Conditional:
  - Communicate any residual issues to clients which remain post-cutover, and detail timelines for remediation
  - Activate TSAs and begin to track towards exit
Optional:
  - Brief the media on a successful cutover, with pre-prepared executive remarks
  - Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover
Nuances:
  - Cutover for a deal of this type will be the least complex, focused largely on transfer of legal ownership, as the business should largely continue running as previously, with only the ownership structures, reporting, and liquidity management changing
Artefacts:
  - Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)
  - Hub & Spoke Operating Model
  - DR and cutover playbook
Templates:
  - Cutover checkpoint template

title: Hypercare
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Id: hypercare
Index: 10
Title: Hypercare
Purpose: Support a stable transition of ownership, resolve residual seller obligations and complete Absa's exit from the business.
Role:
  - Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
  - Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
  - Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes
Timeline: 0 – 2 months
Timeline Drivers:
  - Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
  - Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

title: Hypercare
breadcrumb: Full-business divestment (Variant B · Buyer runs the business standalone)
text:
Necessary:
  - Set up a dedicated team to monitor residual cutover issues and retained business issues
  - Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
  - Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
  - Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
  - Gradually hand off servicing to BAU teams by transitioning issue resolution and triage into the BAU process, prioritising only the most serious issues for Hypercare as time passes
  - Track divestment objectives such as cost, asset/liability transfer, volumes, etc. as soon as LD1, and provide updates to executives on progress against objectives
  - Hold daily touchpoints with AEs to flag the most important issues and discuss remediation plans
  - Conduct completion-account and purchase-price true-ups
  - Ensure closure of intra-group accounts and interfaces
  - Confirmation of buyer data-return or deletion obligations
  - Ensure post-completion support is within the bounds of SPA and TSAs
Conditional:
  - Monitor TSA performance, track progress towards exit, and remove remaining entanglements
  - Monitor warranties, indemnities, and potential claims
Nuances:
  - Detailed, specific Hypercare capacity may not be required from the Absa side if the buyer is running the business as standalone with minimal operational and technical change
Artefacts:
  - Hub & Spoke operating model
  - M&A Learning Pathways

  Id: principles
  Number: 02
  Title: Mobilisation Principles
  Purpose: Understand the core principles that should govern mobilisation on every transaction.
  Short: Six principles that govern every mobilisation.
  Group: Understand the roadmap
  Icon: compass
  Blocks:
    -
      Kind: principles
      Items:
        -
          Title: Prepare before signing
          Body: Mobilisation readiness is built ahead of signature, so day one is a start rather than a scramble.
        -
          Title: Plan from outcomes and readiness
          Body: Plans are built backwards from the outcomes and readiness required, not forwards from available activity.
        -
          Title: Time-box planning
          Body: Planning is bounded, so mobilisation converges on a credible plan rather than expanding indefinitely.
        -
          Title: Make accountability explicit
          Body: Every workstream, output and decision carries a named accountable owner.
        -
          Title: Facilitate the work
          Body: Mobilisation is facilitated with the teams doing the work, rather than written on their behalf.
        -
          Title: Build challenge into mobilisation
          Body: Structured challenge is part of the process, so weak plans are surfaced before execution begins.

title: Establish mobilisation authority
text:
Day: 1
Title: Establish mobilisation authority
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Mobilise core transaction leadership, and identify broader leadership requirements

title: Activities
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- Confirm the transaction archetype, perimeter, effort size and complexity.
- Confirm critical transaction dates to confirm the planning window (Days 11 – 20), including the date of regulatory approval submissions (and whether a migration plan must be attached to these), the LD1 date as envisioned in the SPA or agreed alongside Counterparty, and other critical dates impacting planning (change freezes, legal constraints, long-stop dates, etc).
- Name the Executive Sponsor, Transaction Director, and Programme Manager.
- Across each of these roles agree on core responsibilities in mobilisation, decision rights and escalation triggers, and the mobilisation phase reporting cadence.
- Accountable Executive responsible for contacting & mobilising broader programme leadership, communicating the strategic intent of the deal, as well as interfacing with Absa leadership committees (Board, StratCo, etc).
- Transaction Director responsible for onboarding and selecting programme leadership (Workstream Execs) alongside AE based on SME knowledge, defining required governance structures, and leading reporting.
- Programme Manager responsible for standing up chosen governance, defining planning requirements, organising logistics, and supporting WS Execs in onboarding broader team members.
- Work with the legal team to draft or amend an NDA which can be used to onboard people into the insider list.

title: Activities
text:
- Based on deal archetype, perimeter, complexity, and those involved in DD, TD and AE draft a list of required Workstreams, and socialise with CorpDev and Business stakeholders involved in DD for validation.
- Structure onboarding materials for these stakeholders, as well as broader team members to be onboarded in future.
- Contact the counterparty to understand their programme leadership structure, and set up regular touchpoints.
- Create an information request and assumptions log to track key information and inform planning.

title: Establish mobilisation authority
text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: Mobilisation alignment
  Participants:
    - Executive Sponsor
    - Transaction Director
    - PMO lead
    - Legal, where information-sharing permissions require confirmation
Ownership:
  Lead: Transaction Director
  Support:
    - Executive Sponsor
    - Programme Manager / PMO lead
    - Legal
Information Required:
  - Transaction archetype and perimeter
  - Effort size and complexity
  - Principal transaction dates
  - Proposed leadership and key stakeholders
  - Transaction status and legal permissions
  - Known confidentiality restrictions
Completion Gate:
  - Named mobilisation leadership
  - Draft list of Workstream Execs
  - Defined responsibilities, decision and escalation route
  - Documented information-sharing permissions, restrictions, and NDA
  - Initial information-request and assumptions log

title: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
breadcrumb: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
text:
Day: 2
Title: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Convert the Day 1 appointments into a functioning core mobilisation team with accepted roles, protected capacity and owned coverage gaps.
Activities:
  - Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
  - Define the minimum core-team roles needed to run mobilisation, including PMO coordination, Legal or Compliance, technology access administration, people or resourcing support and communications support.
  - Nominate a named individual for each core-team role, using interim cover where a permanent resource is not yet available.
  - Issue a concise role card to each core-team member covering mobilisation responsibilities, authority, required availability, escalation route and immediate deliverables.
  - Obtain explicit acceptance from each core-team member and record any conditions, start-date constraints or delegated responsibilities.
  - Check availability across Days 2 to 10 against BAU deadlines, leave, regulatory commitments and other change activity.
  - Agree release, backfill or reprioritisation actions with the relevant line managers where committed capacity is insufficient.
  - Allocate ownership and response dates for the information requests and assumptions opened on Day 1 without assessing or resolving their substantive content.
  - Place the agreed mobilisation reporting cadence into calendars and confirm who prepares, reviews and circulates each update.

title: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
breadcrumb: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: Core-team mobilisation huddle led by the Transaction Director, followed by targeted capacity discussions with line managers for any role that is not fully released

    - Core mobilisation team
    - Line managers

  Lead: Transaction Director
  Support:
    - Programme Manager / PMO lead
    - Line managers

  - Day 1 decision rights, escalation triggers and reporting cadence
  - Current organisation charts and resource availability
  - Known BAU deadlines, leave and competing change commitments
  - Available backfill, contractor and specialist-support routes
  - Day 1 information-request and assumptions log
Completion Gate:
  - Accepted core-team roster with named deputies and contact details
  - Issued role cards and recorded acceptance conditions
  - Day 2 to Day 10 capacity view, including BAU release and backfill actions
  - Owned vacancy and capacity-exception list with resolution dates
  - Allocated information requests and assumptions
  - Published mobilisation meeting and reporting calendar

title: Activate technology and collaboration mechanisms
text:
Day: 3
Title: Activate technology and collaboration mechanisms
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Provide the core team with a secure, tested and controlled environment for communication, document management and mobilisation records.

title: Activate technology and collaboration mechanisms
text:
Activities:
  - Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
  - Translate the Day 1 information-sharing permissions into role-based access groups for internal, joint and restricted material.
  - Select the approved collaboration, document-management, meeting and task-tracking tools that will be used during mobilisation (Virtual Data Room, etc).
  - Create the controlled workspace sharepoint structure, including folders or channels for governance, legal material, people records, mobilisation logs, meeting packs and onboarding evidence.
  - Apply naming, version, status, ownership, retention and approval conventions to the workspace and publish them at the point of use.
  - Create programme distribution lists, Teams channels, meeting links and shared calendars using the Day 2 roster, and assign an owner to update these as the programme expands.
  - Set up an NDA tracker to ensure those who are engaging with the programme are on the insider list.
  - Raise access, licence, device and guest-account requests for all core-team members and track each request to completion.
  - Load the Day 1 information-request and assumptions log into the controlled location and confirm edit, review and approval rights.
  - Test access, document upload, version recovery, meeting entry and notification flows.
  - Issue a one-page working guide and require each core-team member to acknowledge that access works and the control rules are understood.

text:

Completion Gate:
  - Live controlled workspace and approved collaboration channels
  - Published naming, versioning, retention and approval conventions
  - Live distribution lists, shared calendars and meeting channels
  - Live NDA tracker

title: Confirm workstream leadership & mobilisation capacity
text:
Day: 4
Title: Confirm workstream leadership & mobilisation capacity
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Appoint the broader programme leadership and confirm that each active workstream has sufficient authority and capacity to begin mobilisation.

title: Activities
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- TD and AE to jointly agree on Workstream Executive appointments per Workstream and socialise these with the relevant Group Exec.
- Confirm that each Workstream Exec appointee accepts accountability for the workstream outcomes.
- Support the Workstream Exec to appoint a Workstream Lead (WSL) using the Workstream Lead role card, the key capabilities required as laid out in the Operating Model, AE and Workstream Exec's knowledge of individuals' skill and capabilities, and TD's SME knowledge of previous transaction and lessons learnt.
- Provide final signoff on all Workstream Lead appointments and validate each appointee's availability through the mobilisation window, including known BAU deadlines, leave, regulatory commitments and competing change activity.
- Identify required BAU backfill, specialist support, external advisers or temporary capacity and record the route for securing each resource.
- Update the programme organisation chart, contact directory and accountability matrix, clearly marking vacancies and interim appointments.
- Support each WSL in engaging their broader team members, sharing key skills required by workstream.
- Support Workstream Execs and WSL in understanding in-country maturity to define initial split of spoke activities between in-country and SA central function teams, to inform stakeholder engagement and planning requirements.
- Contact the counterparty to receive their list of WSL, and ensure the two sets of stakeholders set time to meet and discuss joint objectives.

text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: Briefing session with Workstream Execs to enable WSL appointment. Briefing session with WSL. Daily standups within Central Hub team.

Completion Gate:
  - Confirmed workstream map
  - Named Workstream Executives, Workstream Leads
  - Agreed Central Hub, functional-spoke and regional-spoke initial accountability split
  - Documented capacity, backfill and specialist-support gaps with owners and dates
  - Updated programme organisation chart, contact directory and accountability matrix

title: Activate governance and programme controls
text:
Day: 5
Title: Activate governance and programme controls
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Decide upon and stand up governance, information-control and reporting mechanisms to enable workstream activity to begin

title: Activities
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- Leveraging the transaction governance structure set out in the Operating Model, define whether any changes or tweaks are required based on the nature of the transaction.
- For each forum, leveraging the ToRs defined in the Operating Model materials, set out cadence and dates; members, contributors, chairs, and facilitators; inputs, outputs, standing agenda; decision mandates and escalation paths; and objectives.
- Define the members for the Internal SteerCo, and share the terms of reference with them.
- Check requirements for Joint SteerCo set out in the SPA, share a list of proposed Absa attendees with the counterparty, and request their list. Ensured the both Absa and counterparty have sufficient representation across key impacted areas.
- Agree and book first Joint PMO meeting with counterparty.
- Leveraging material set out in the Operating Model, design the broader governance and information flow between forums.
- Align internal governance dates with existing Absa committee cycles and the counterparty's proposed governance cadence.
- Assign pack production, quality review, circulation, minute taking, action chasing and record retention responsibilities.
- Publish the initial mobilisation governance calendar, including submission deadlines, pre-reads, decision dates and report-production cut-offs.
- Book the first Internal SteerCo to take place on Day 10.

title: Activities
text:
- Expand the Day 1 information-request and assumptions log into a controlled suite comprising RAID, decisions, dependencies, actions and change requests.
- Define mandatory fields, status values, RAG criteria, ageing rules, escalation thresholds and closure evidence for each programme log.
- Run a governance dry-run using one sample decision and one sample escalation to test routing, authority, record capture.

title: Activate governance and programme controls
text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: PMO controls workshop with the Transaction Director and Programme Manager, followed by a governance Terms of Reference review with the Executive Sponsor and Legal or Compliance where required

    - Legal or Compliance, where required
Ownership:

  Support:

  - Counterparty governance forums and proposed cadence
  - Governance structures and ToRs as set out in the Operating Model
Completion Gate:
  - Approved mobilisation governance map and forum Terms of Reference
  - Published governance and reporting calendar
  - Live controlled workspace with role-based access
  - Live RAID, decision, dependency, action, change and information-request logs

title: Prepare broader-team onboarding
text:
Day: 6
Title: Prepare broader-team onboarding
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Make the onboarding pack, legal clearances, access requests, invitations and tracking mechanisms ready for sequenced rollout to the wider programme.

title: Prepare broader-team onboarding
text:
Activities:
  - Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
  - Segment the wider programme population into leadership, priority delivery, country or regional, enabling-function, specialist and third-party onboarding groups.
  - Sequence the onboarding groups according to mobilisation need, legal permission, leadership availability and access lead time.
  - Update the Day 1 onboarding material with the confirmed organisation, role model, governance, collaboration tools and contact routes from Days 2 to 5.
  - Create role-specific appendices showing each audience's responsibilities, required time commitment, meeting obligations and immediate mobilisation actions.
  - Have Legal or Compliance validate the transaction description, confidentiality wording, insider-list process, clean-team boundaries and permitted disclosures.
  - Check each proposed attendee against NDA, insider-list, conflicts, employment status and third-party engagement requirements.
  - Raise batched workspace, meeting, licence, guest-account and restricted-area access requests for cleared attendees.
  - Nominate presenters, facilitators, access support, Q&A owners and attendance administrators for every session.
  - Create attendance, clearance, access, acknowledgement, question and no-show trackers with owners and closure dates.
  - Dry-run the onboarding session and correct unclear content, failed links, missing permissions and timing issues before launch.

title: Brief programme leadership
text:
Day: 7
Title: Brief programme leadership
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Align appointed leaders on the transaction context, mobilisation responsibilities, governance, controls and their accountability for onboarding their teams.

title: Activities
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- Verify that every attendee is cleared, listed where required and able to access the approved workspace before the session begins.
- Brief Workstream Execs using materials covering core transaction objectives; information sharing restrictions; Workstream Exec roles, responsibilities, and decision rights; WSL key requirements and role card; key considerations for their workstream; explicit acceptance of the role; and actions and next steps.
- Brief each WSL using materials covering core transaction objectives; information sharing restrictions; WSL roles, responsibilities, and decision rights; key considerations for their workstream; planning window requirements and proposed dates; explicit acceptance of the role; and actions and next steps.
- Explain the ten-day mobilisation objective and state explicitly that detailed planning and gap assessment begin after the mobilisation gate.
- Explain the governance forums, delegated decision rights, escalation triggers, submission cut-offs and urgent-decision route.
- Demonstrate the controlled workspace, communication channels, document rules and required use of mobilisation records.
- Reinforce NDA, insider-list, clean-team, competition, employee, customer and other information-sharing restrictions relevant to leaders.
- Review each leader's responsibility for completing team appointments, legal clearance, access and onboarding by the agreed date.
- Confirm the mobilisation meeting commitments and availability of each leader and deputy through Day 10.

title: Activities
text:
- Capture questions, access failures, role ambiguities and unresolved appointments in the relevant controlled record with owners and dates.
- Obtain acknowledgement of the leadership brief and issue the approved material and immediate mobilisation actions.

Activities:
  - Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
  - Deliver the approved transaction, perimeter and mobilisation briefing to priority functional, country and enabling teams.
  - Introduce each team's Executive, Lead, deputy, coordinator, regional contacts, PMO contact and counterparty interface where confirmed.
  - Explain mobilisation responsibilities, required availability, governance attendance, escalation route and immediate administrative actions.
  - Demonstrate the approved collaboration channels, controlled folders, meeting calendar and record-keeping conventions.
  - Test workspace, meeting and restricted-area access live.
  - Confirm that every attendee understands the information-sharing restrictions and records the required NDA, insider-list or policy acknowledgement.
  - Capture role gaps, availability constraints, conflicts, access failures and unanswered mobilisation questions with owners and closure dates.
  - Update the programme organisation chart and contact directory for substitutions, new deputies and confirmed local representatives.
  - Record attendance and follow up no-shows, late joiners and uncompleted acknowledgements within the same business day.
  - Obtain the relevant Workstream Executive's confirmation that the priority team is mobilised or that named exceptions remain.

Title: Complete wider onboarding and connect sessions

title: Activities
breadcrumb: Complete wider onboarding and connect sessions
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- Reconcile the remaining attendee list against appointments, legal clearance, third-party engagement and access status.
- Deliver the approved onboarding briefing to a second wave of functional, country, specialist, adviser and support participants.
- Test workspace, meeting and restricted-area access and close or escalate failures.
- Collect attendance, role, confidentiality and policy acknowledgements and follow up all incomplete records.
- Pair Absa PMO and Workstream Leads with named counterparty counterparts where communication is legally permitted.
- Publish a joint interface directory showing primary contacts, deputies, approved channels, permitted topics and escalation contacts.
- Confirm attendance for Absa SteeCo, joint SteerCo, Transaction Working Group, and Joint PMO forums.
- Agree the administrative protocol for requesting information, circulating materials, recording decisions and escalating unanswered requests.
- Resolve duplicate appointments, unowned support roles and outdated contact details in the programme organisation records.
- Consolidate all no-shows, access failures, clearance delays, capacity constraints and unconfirmed counterpart contacts into the mobilisation exception log.

title: Activities
breadcrumb: Complete wider onboarding and connect sessions
text: - Prepare the Day 10 mobilisation gate pack using evidence from the appointment, access, governance and onboarding records. Gate pack should include confirmation that governance is stood up, including governance calendar; confirmation of key programme appointments; confirmation of briefing sessions and explicit acceptance; confirmation of shared workspaces and collaboration tools in place; confirmation of counterparty key stakeholders and parallel governance; and key next steps for planning phase.

title: Complete wider onboarding and connect sessions
breadcrumb: Complete wider onboarding and connect sessions
text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: Second wave of onboarding sessions followed by a joint-connect confirmation between the Absa and counterparty PMO and Workstream Leads
  Participants:
    - Programme Manager
    - PMO
    - Workstream Leads
    - Counterparty PMO and Workstream Leads
Ownership:
  Lead: Programme Manager
  Support:
    - PMO
    - Workstream Leads
    - Legal or Compliance
Information Required:
  - Wave 2 audience, clearance, engagement and access records
  - Approved onboarding pack and programme operating guide
  - Counterparty organisation and contact information received to date
  - Joint-forum membership and information-sharing permissions
  - Day 10 mobilisation gate criteria and evidence checklist
Completion Gate:
  - Completed Wave 2 onboarding and acknowledgement
  - Published joint directory and communication protocol
  - Confirmed joint-forum attendance
  - Consolidated mobilisation exception log with owners and dates
  - Draft mobilisation Day 10 gate pack

title: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
breadcrumb: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
text:
Day: 10
Title: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
Outcome Lede: Required outcome:
Outcomes:
  - Confirm that people, tools, governance, legal controls and interfaces are operational, then authorise planning and gap assessment to begin after Day 10.

title: Activities
breadcrumb: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
text:
- Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
- Reconcile the final programme organisation against accepted appointments, coverage, and capacity commitments.
- Verify that required users can access the correct collaboration channels, meeting links, controlled folders and restricted areas.
- Confirm that governance forums are staffed and scheduled and that agenda, pack, minute, action, decision and escalation controls operate as designed.
- Confirm completion of required NDA, insider-list, clean-team, conflict, policy and third-party engagement steps.
- Confirm that leadership and broader-team onboarding attendance, acknowledgements, no-shows and follow-up actions are recorded.
- Validate the internal and counterparty contact directories, approved communication channels and escalation contacts.
- Review every open mobilisation exception and classify it as closed, accepted with conditions, or blocking the next phase.
- Assign a named owner, due date, escalation route and closure evidence to each condition that will remain open after Day 10.
- Agree the start date, participants, required inputs and invitations for post-mobilisation scoping, planning and gap-assessment sessions without commencing those activities, these include workstream charters, workstream bricks and workstream blueprints, to enable creation of workstream milestones.

title: Activities
breadcrumb: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
text:
- Hold the first Absa Internal SteerCo to present the gate pack with recommendation and record the decision to proceed, proceed conditionally or hold, and to confirm the Terms of Reference for this session, including objectives and mandate.
- Issue the mobilisation completion pack, decision record, open conditions and authorised next-phase launch arrangements to all programme leaders.

title: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
breadcrumb: Close mobilisation via stage gate, and release the next phase
text:
Touchpoint:
  Title: Mobilisation gate review with the Absa Internal SteerCo
  Participants:
    - Absa Internal SteerCo
    - Executive Sponsor
    - Transaction Director
    - Programme Manager
Ownership:
  Lead: Transaction Director
  Support:
    - Executive Sponsor
    - Programme Manager
    - PMO
Information Required:
  - Final appointment, capacity, deputy and organisation records
  - Workspace, licence, access and support-completion registers
  - Governance calendar, Terms of Reference
  - Legal-clearance, confidentiality and acknowledgement records
  - Leadership and broader-team onboarding completion evidence
  - Counterparty directory and mobilisation exception log
Completion Gate:
  - Approved mobilisation completion dashboard and evidence pack
  - Recorded gate decision to proceed, proceed conditionally or hold
  - Closed or conditionally accepted mobilisation exception log
  - Confirmed programme organisation, access model, governance and interface baseline
  - Authorised date and attendee list for post-Day 10 planning and gap assessment
  - Issued mobilisation closure note and next-phase launch invitations

title: Central M&A Hub
text:
Id: hub
Name: Central M&A Hub
Strapline: Inorganic Change Team
Summary: Permanent core team that owns the M&A method, mobilises every deal and holds programme control from pre-signing through hypercare.
Purpose: Hold Absa's inorganic delivery capability in one place so each deal starts from a codified method rather than from scratch, and so execution discipline is consistent across archetypes and geographies.
Responsibilities:
  - Own and maintain the codified lifecycle, archetype classification and artefact set
  - Mobilise the deal: archetype call, delivery shape, resourcing plan and governance stand-up
  - Run integrated planning, milestone tracking, risk and dependency management
  - Chair the transaction working group and prepare steering committee material
  - Run readiness, dress rehearsals and go/no-go evidence packs
  - Capture lessons learnt and feed them back into the method
Services:
  - Deal mobilisation in a defined number of working days
  - Integrated plan and critical path on a single baseline
  - Programme reporting, RAID and decision log
  - Archetype and complexity assessment
  - Template and artefact library with worked examples
  - Partner accelerator sourcing and onboarding
Decision Rights:
  - Sets the delivery method, plan baseline and reporting cadence
  - Confirms the deal archetype and mobilisation shape
  - Owns the go/no-go recommendation to the steering committee
  - Can escalate directly to the executive sponsor
  - Cannot change deal scope, price or commercial terms

title: Central M&A Hub
text:
Governance:
  - Reports into the transaction director and the deal steering committee
  - Directs functional and regional spoke leads on delivery matters
  - Interfaces with Corporate Development pre-signing and with Internal Audit throughout
Capabilities:
  - M&A programme leadership and PMO discipline
  - Integration and separation planning
  - Regulatory and cutover readiness management
  - Data and reporting capability
Inputs:
  - Deal thesis, structure and indicative timetable from Corporate Development
  - Due diligence findings and conditions precedent
  - Functional and regional capacity positions
Outputs:
  - Mobilisation pack and integrated plan
  - Governance calendar and decision log
  - Readiness and go/no-go packs
  - Post-deal lessons learnt and method updates

title: Functional and regional spokes
text:
Id: spokes
Name: Functional and regional spokes
Strapline: Where the work is delivered
Summary: South African functional workstreams paired with in-country regional workstreams, mobilised according to the deal archetype.
Purpose: Deliver the functional and country-level change required to complete the transaction, using people who already run the business rather than a parallel organisation.
Responsibilities:
  - Own functional delivery to the agreed milestone dates
  - Provide effort estimates, resource names and dependencies at mobilisation
  - Raise risks, issues and decisions into the transaction working group
  - Confirm functional readiness ahead of dress rehearsals and cutover
  - Own local regulatory and market obligations in each in-country spoke
Services:
  - Functional impact assessment and target design
  - Delivery of functional change against the integrated plan
  - Testing, readiness evidence and sign-off
  - In-country execution and local regulator engagement
Decision Rights:
  - Approve functional design and functional readiness within policy
  - Nominate and release delivery resources within their function
  - Cannot move an agreed milestone without working-group approval
  - Cannot accept a local regulatory obligation outside mandate
Governance:
  - Spoke leads sit on the transaction working group chaired by the Hub
  - Regional spoke leads report functionally to their SA counterpart and locally to the country executive
  - Escalation runs spoke lead, Hub, transaction director, steering committee

title: Functional and regional spokes
text:
Capabilities:
  - Functional subject-matter depth with delivery experience
  - Local regulatory and market knowledge in each geography
  - Ability to plan, estimate and hold a milestone date
Inputs:
  - Archetype, perimeter and integrated plan from the Hub
  - Diligence findings relevant to the function
  - Data and system baselines
Outputs:
  - Functional plans, designs and readiness evidence
  - Milestone and dependency status
  - Signed functional approvals at go/no-go

title: Partner accelerator network
text:
Id: partners
Name: Partner accelerator network
Strapline: Pre-agreed external capacity and advice
Summary: Pre-qualified external providers that can be mobilised quickly where Absa lacks specialist advice or short-term delivery capacity.
Purpose: Remove the delay and cost of sourcing external help mid-deal by pre-agreeing categories, providers and mobilisation routes before a transaction starts.
Responsibilities:
  - Maintain pre-qualified provider categories and commercial arrangements
  - Define trigger points where external support is expected
  - Onboard, direct and exit partners against a defined scope and outcome
  - Ensure knowledge transfers back into Absa before partners leave
Services:
  - Specialist advice on regulatory, tax, legal and technical questions
  - Short-term delivery capacity for peak load
  - Independent assurance on migration and readiness
Decision Rights:
  - The Hub recommends the need; the transaction director approves the spend
  - Procurement approves the commercial route
  - Partners hold no Absa decision rights and cannot sign off readiness
Governance:
  - Requested through the Hub, approved by the transaction director, contracted by Procurement
  - Partners report to the accountable Absa spoke lead, never directly to steering
Capabilities:
  - Category management and rapid onboarding
  - Clear scoping and outcome definition
  - Knowledge-transfer discipline
Inputs:
  - Capacity gaps identified during mobilisation
  - Complexity assessment and geography footprint
  - Approved transaction budget

title: Partner accelerator network
text:
Outputs:
  - Mobilised partner teams against defined scope
  - Specialist opinions and assurance reports
  - Capability retained in Absa at exit

title: Deal journey
text:
-
  Window: T-1 month

    - Indicative delivery shape

    - Conditions precedent log
    - Announcement pack
  Activated:
    - Comms

-
